Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for Industrial placement students who want to be part of something extraordinary—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates.
Our Industrial Placement Programme
Our Industrial Placement Programme offers you the chance to spend a year with us, working on meaningful projects alongside subject matter experts, within multidisciplinary teams, and across the product lifecycle. You’ll receive a salary of £26,228, with coaching and support from a dedicated team to help you achieve both your placement objectives and personal development goals.
Successful completion of an Industrial Placement with Leonardo may also lead to an offer on our Graduate Development Programme.
During your placement, we encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience. This Opportunity is based in Luton.
During the programme, you will
As part of our Hardware Engineering team, you'll support the development of high-performance electronic hardware used within advanced Electronic Warfare solutions.
Your activities will include:
- Supporting the design and development of analogue, digital and mixed-signal hardware systems
- Assisting with schematic capture, circuit analysis and design activities
- Supporting integration, verification and qualification activities
- Conducting laboratory testing, debugging and validation using specialist electronic test equipment
- Analysing technical performance data and presenting findings to engineering teams
- Collaborating with systems, firmware, software and RF engineers on multidisciplinary projects
- Contributing to technical documentation and design reviews
Your Industrial Placement Project
Approximately 50% of your placement will be dedicated to a cohort-led Industrial Placement project.
Working with placement students from across the organisation, you'll take ownership of a business-focused project from concept to delivery. You'll be responsible for planning activities, managing stakeholders and delivering outcomes that create real value for the business.
What We're Looking For
You should be studying towards a degree in:
- Electronic Engineering
- Electrical Engineering
- Robotics Engineering
- AI & Cybernetics
- Physics or Applied Physics
- Engineering Physics
- Mathematics or Applied Mathematics
- Communications Engineering
- Information Engineering
- Space Engineering
- Computer Communication and Networks
- Cyber Security or related STEM disciplines
We'd also like to see:
- An interest in electronic hardware design and development
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A willingness to learn and take ownership of challenging tasks
- An interest in laboratory-based engineering and testing activities
The Placement Experience
You'll benefit from:
- Hands-on experience on real engineering projects
- Mentoring from experienced engineers
- Technical and professional skills development
- A dedicated Industrial Placement cohort project
- Exposure to multiple engineering disciplines and technologies
- Opportunities to build your professional network across Leonardo
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting
Why join us
At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, our teams are key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.
- Time to recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year.
- Secure your future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution.
- Your wellbeing matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity.
- Tailored perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.
For a full list of our company benefits please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/company-benefits
We are committed to building an inclusive, accessible, and welcoming workplace. We believe that a diverse workforce sparks creativity, drives innovation, and leads to better outcomes for our people, communities and our customers. If you have any accessibility requirements to support you during the recruitment process, just let us know.
Start your extraordinary career – apply now!

Research Intern, Masters: $106,110 (Annually)
Research Intern, PhD: $140,000 (Annually)
Who You Are:
Ai2 is seeking passionate, early-career researchers to join us for an internship. PhD graduate students in AI-related fields are invited to apply for full-time research internships with us year-round. Our research covers the full spectrum of robotics ranging from low-level control, scaling simulation to solve real-world robotics challenges, world models, RL, and investigating agentic systems for robotics. We are looking for applicants that are experienced and passionate about a particular aspect of robotics. International candidates are welcome to apply. Pay is competitive, and visa sponsorship is available.
Ai2 Research Internship Information:
- Duration : 12 weeks
- Start Date : Flexible
- Candidates : A PhD student with a strong research background
Please apply by January 8, 2027, at 11:00pm Pacific Time to be considered for our Spring/Summer 2027 internships.
Who We Are:
Ai2’s Robotics team is looking for PhD student interns to join our team.
As a research intern in the Robotics team, you’ll have the unique opportunity to support the development and investigate core research problems in foundation models and skills for robotics, contribute to the development of completely open data sets, benchmarks, and models, and experiment with robots in the real world.
Your Next Challenge:
At Ai2, you will be working with world-class AI researchers and talented software engineers. We perform team-based, ambitious research, with a mandate to strive for big breakthroughs, not just incremental progress, in an exciting and interactive workplace.
All interns are paired with a mentor and will participate directly in Ai2's groundbreaking work. There are no restrictions on publications based on internships.
Ai2 Research Interns will have the opportunity to do the following tasks:
- Conducting AI research under the guidance of a mentor, which may include building AI systems or system components, developing datasets, and/or conducting experiments.
- Reading the scientific literature to investigate and understand AI research.
- Meeting with the mentor to discuss research progress and ideas.
To see more about our current, future, and past interns at Ai2, check out the internship page on our website!
What You’ll Need:
Minimum Qualifications:
- Pursuing a PhD in robotics, machine learning, or related fields.
- Have an interest and experience in cutting-edge artificial intelligence and robotics research.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Proven track record of publishing at robotics and AI conferences, such as CoRL, ICRA, IROS, RSS, and Neurips.
- Strong software engineering skills in physics simulation, machine learning, and robot control.
Physical Demands and Work Environment:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.
- Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.
- The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
- The ability to observe details at close range.
- Can work under deadlines.

Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
At Micron, we are transforming how the world uses information to enrich life. The High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Design team develops industry-leading memory solutions that power artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, graphics, and data-center applications. Our engineers collaborate across global teams to deliver next-generation memory architectures, advanced design methodologies, and innovative semiconductor solutions.
As an HBM Design Engineer Intern, you will work alongside experienced memory engineers on the design, development, and validation of advanced HBM products. This role provides hands-on experience with digital design, circuit design, design verification, simulation, and semiconductor development flows while collaborating with Design, Verification, Physical Design, Product Engineering, and CAD teams.
Responsibilities
- Assist with the design, simulation, analysis, and verification of HBM memory and logic circuits using industry-standard EDA tools.
- Support RTL development, circuit implementation, timing analysis, power analysis, and functional verification activities.
- Develop scripting, automation, and AI-assisted workflows to improve design productivity, debug efficiency, and design-flow quality.
- Participate in design reviews, technical discussions, and debugging activities, leveraging AI-enabled analysis to accelerate root-cause identification and engineering decision-making.
- Document technical work, experimental results, build methodologies, and AI-assisted insights to support collaboration and continuous improvement.
Minimum Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
- Completed coursework in Digital Logic Design, CMOS Circuits, Computer Architecture, VLSI Design, Semiconductor Devices, or related subjects.
- Working knowledge of combinational and sequential logic design concepts and familiarity with Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL.
- Basic programming experience in Python, Perl, Tcl, C/C++, or similar languages.
- Demonstrated analytical, debugging, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.
Preferred Qualifications
- Knowledge of memory architectures such as DRAM, SRAM, DDR, LPDDR, or HBM.
- Experience with RTL design, simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, or verification methodologies through coursework, research, or internship projects.
- Familiarity with Linux/Unix environments, scripting, and semiconductor design tools such as VCS, Xcelium, Questa, PrimeTime, Innovus, Virtuoso, or similar EDA platforms.
- Understanding of functional coverage concepts and modern semiconductor development flows from specification through silicon validation.
- Previous academic, research, or internship experience in VLSI, ASIC, FPGA, memory design, or semiconductor engineering, including exposure to AI-assisted or AI-enabled engineering workflows.
As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. At Meta, we’re building the future of human connection and the technology that enables it. This means continuously inventing and developing technologies for the next generation of experiences.
To continue our efforts in the path to AGI, and as we move closer to a future with intelligent robots and advanced AI models, we're hiring talent across a broad range of disciplines from robotics hardware to system software, machine perception, and artificial intelligence. These crucial projects and initiatives taken on by this team have never been done before, so you have a rare opportunity to help us create new ways people connect around the world.
The Meta Robotics Hardware team is seeking a Research Scientist Intern with an emphasis on developing high-performance custom robotics hardware. This role will be part of a hardware research team responsible for consumer humanoid development at Meta.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.
url:https://www.metacareers.com/jobs/226:
The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of contextual AI and robotics.
The Surreal Vision group at RL Research is seeking exceptional Research Scientist interns to contribute to fundamental research on 3D-grounded generalist models for robotics. These models will form the foundation to enable accurate and efficient zero-shot general robotic manipulation in daily environments. As a research intern, you will tackle cutting-edge research challenges, innovate model architectures and training recipes, and deliver general robotics policies.
Your research project may cover or relate to the following topics:
- Generating and delivering effective data and training recipes to significantly improve the 3D/spatial understanding of large-scale foundation models.
- Developing generalist robotics policies based on large-scale 3D foundation models with interactive/real-time performance.
- Validating the developed robotics policies both in simulation and on real robots, with the stretch goal of delivering a live demonstration on physical hardware.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year. Some projects may require a minimum of 24 consecutive weeks.

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.
 
You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date.
 
Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three.
 
Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems.

Technologies We Use
- Java, Scala, Rust, and Python
- Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution
- Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability
- Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage
- Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration
You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.
What We Value
- Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimisers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing
- A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does
- Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack
- A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition
- Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback
- Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software
What We Require
- Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience
- Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Rust, Scala, C++, or C
- Strong foundations in algorithms, data structures, and concurrency
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems
- Contributions to open-source projects
- Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $10,500/month. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.


Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
 
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

Analog Devices is seeking an Analog Design Intern – Power Management to join our engineering team in Edinburgh.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative team developing advanced low-power analog and power-management IP for highly integrated mixed-signal ICs. Working alongside experienced analog, mixed-signal and power-management engineers, the intern will contribute to real IC development activities while gaining practical experience in circuit architecture, transistor-level design, modelling, simulation and verification.
The team develops power-management solutions with a strong focus on low-power operation, high efficiency and small solution size . Key areas include switched-mode DC/DC converters such as buck, boost and buck-boost architectures , together with the analog building blocks required for their control, monitoring and protection.
This internship provides an opportunity to apply university knowledge to real silicon designs and develop an understanding of the complete IC development process, from architecture and modelling through circuit implementation, physical design, verification and potentially silicon evaluation.
Responsibilities
- Conduct circuit architecture research and feasibility studies for low-power power-management functions.
- Contribute to the architecture, design, simulation and verification of DC/DC converter IP , including buck, boost and buck-boost topologies.
- Design and analyse analog sub-circuits used within power converters, potentially including error amplifiers, comparators, voltage/current references, oscillators, gate drivers, level shifters, current-sensing circuits and protection functions .
- Develop simulation testbenches and contribute to design verification across process, voltage, temperature and operating-load conditions.
- Analyse important converter performance trade-offs including efficiency, quiescent current, transient response, output ripple, stability, silicon area and external component requirements .
- Explore different converter operating modes and control techniques to optimise efficiency across load conditions.
- Contribute to behavioural and system-level modelling to evaluate converter architectures and control-loop performance.
- Work closely with layout engineers during physical implementation, including review of parasitic effects and layout-dependent performance.
- Participate in technical and design reviews with experienced analog and power-management engineers.
- Support top-level integration and verification of power-management IP within larger mixed-signal systems.
- Where appropriate, contribute to laboratory evaluation and comparison of simulated and measured silicon performance.
Minimum Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a BEng, MEng, MSc or PhD in Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics or a closely related discipline.
- Good understanding of fundamental analog electronics and circuit theory.
- Understanding of CMOS devices and basic transistor-level circuit operation.
- Familiarity with feedback systems, frequency response and stability.
- Basic understanding of power electronics and switching circuits.
- Some experience with circuit simulation or electronic design tools through university, personal or industry projects.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Enthusiasm for learning and working collaboratively within an engineering team.
Preferred Qualifications
- Understanding of DC/DC converter architectures , particularly buck, boost or buck-boost converters.
- Familiarity with concepts such as PWM/PFM operation, feedback control, loop stability and transient response.
- Familiarity with transistor-level IC design and tools such as Cadence Virtuoso and Spectre .
- Exposure to power-converter modelling or simulation using tools such as SIMPLIS, MATLAB or Simulink .
- Understanding of common power-management building blocks such as LDOs, voltage/current references, comparators, oscillators, current sensing and gate drivers.
- Familiarity with low-power circuit-design techniques and quiescent-current optimisation.
- Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads and signal generators.
- Programming or scripting experience using Python, MATLAB or similar tools for modelling, simulation or data analysis.
- A strong interest in analog IC design, power management and energy-efficient electronic systems .

url:https://intel.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/: Job Details: Job Description: About the Job Intel is seeking exceptional Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and AI/ML students to join an AI Hardware Engineering internship focused on the future of AI inference and AI infrastructure with hardware/software co-design expertise. This internship approaches AI infrastructure as a hardware/software co-design challenge. The intern will analyze how model architecture, inference behavior, memory movement, data-center constraints, and software stacks influence end-to-end customer outcomes, including throughput, latency, time-to-first-token, tokens per second, power consumption, utilization, total cost of ownership, and deployability. The successful candidate will be technically hands-on, capable of independent research and analysis, and comfortable working within a highly technical team of researchers and engineers addressing complex AI hardware and infrastructure challenges. What You Will Do Conduct technical research on the next generation of AI infrastructure, including CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, ASICs, memory systems, networking, storage, rack-scale architecture, power delivery, cooling, and cluster management. Analyze GenAI and agentic AI workloads to understand their hardware implications, including transformer architecture based inference, mixture-of-experts architectures, multimodal models, real-time interactive inference, and distributed serving. Evaluate the hardware behavior of AI inference pipelines, including the distinct demands of prompt processing/prefill and token generation/decode, memory capacity, memory bandwidth, KV-cache management, compute utilization, interconnect bandwidth, and latency. For example, cluster architecture around optimizing both prefill and decode through hardware, memory, and system co-design. Identify product and system gaps that may limit Intel's ability to serve AI customers effectively, including hardware capabilities, developer tooling, performance libraries, reference architectures, deployment models, observability, and ecosystem enablement. - Expertise in modern high-performance CPU, GPU, or AI accelerator architecture and hardware/software interactions. - Support Silicon HW programs through multiple phases of the silicon lifecycle, with end-to-end chip execution from concept to silicon. - Good understanding with firmware codebases, compilers, kernels, serving stacks and model architectures. - Familiar with driving silicon design for subsystems and/or top-level functions with ASICs and SOCs from an architecture specification to production silicon including memory subsystems and interconnects: scale up, scale out, scale across, power management , liquid cooling at rack scale level, deep system level observability & telemetry and dependent impact into Gen AI and LLM level performance/tco/execution KPIs Develop technical recommendations for what Intel should build, optimize, enable, partner on to meet AI customer requirements based on deep understanding of customer use cases, workload performance, and ML systems research. Benchmark and compare relevant AI hardware and infrastructure approaches across performance, power efficiency, cost, programmability, memory hierarchy, scalability, ecosystem maturity, and workload fit. Develop technical models, simulations, prototypes, or analysis tools to evaluate hardware/software trade offs for AI workloads. Investigate system bottlenecks across compute, memory, networking, storage, and software orchestration, and propose methods to improve end-to-end AI workload performance. Work with Intel technical teams and external ISVs to collect data on model requirements, inference bottlenecks, deployment challenges, hardware optimization opportunities, and customer priorities. Engage with AI software ecosystem partners, including model providers, inference-engine developers, cloud providers, framework teams, and ISVs, to understand how their stacks interact with underlying hardware. Good understanding of modern AI software layers, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, model serving, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, Kubernetes, and Neocloud design efficiencies. Present findings through architecture diagrams, benchmark analyses, technical reports, design recommendations, and executive-ready presentations. To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Broadband Plasma (BBP) division is the market-leading optical inspection system used by logic, foundry, and memory customers to detect critical defects at advanced nodes. These tools combine broadband plasma technology with unmatched sensitivity and speed to support high-volume manufacturing.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Job Description:
- Assist engineers with system health checks, calibration, troubleshooting, and data collection.
- Characterize system performance by analyzing images and other data collected through machine control software.
- Participate in system characterization and validation activities to verify performance against engineering requirements.
- Design and run experiments, document results, present to engineering teams.
- Work with cross-functional teams such as systems, mechanical, electrical, software, applications and algorithm teams.
- Develop scripts and utilities to automate data analysis, testing, or engineering processes.
- Participate in engineering reviews, team meetings, and technical discussions.
Required Qualifications:
- Currently pursuing a MS or PhD degree in an Engineering field
- Background in engineering or physics (With experience in Optics is best)
- Experience in basic image processing operations such as filtering, target finding, alignment, coordinate systems etc.
- Ability to parse data from a variety of data sources such as text files, html, csv and other file formats.
- Experience in Python, MATLAB, or other scripting languages.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
- Good understanding of Optics and Image Processing
- Experience with imaging systems / Semiconductor Wafer inspection tools
- Experience in developing / implementing deep learning applications
- Experience in system engineering, prototyping, image analysis, digital signal processing, control systems and statistical analysis.
Minimum Qualifications
Requires less than 1 year of related experience
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

About Exotrail 🚀
Space is becoming more strategic and competitive than ever. Tomorrow’s space leaders will not simply launch satellites into orbit, they will be able to move them, reposition them, extend their lifetime, and maximize their performance in space.
Since 2017, Exotrail has been developing and operating cutting-edge in-space mobility solutions for commercial, institutional, and defense customers. From our high-performance propulsion system spaceware™ to our orbital transfer vehicle spacevan™ , we enable satellites to go farther, stay operational longer, and achieve more.
Today, more than 200 Exotrailers across Massy and Toulouse are working together to make space operations more efficient and sustainable.
Backed by over €75 million in funding , we are pursuing a clear mission:
Making space a sustainable frontier for future generations. 🚀
Job Description
At Exotrail, we are developing spacevan GEO, our orbital transfer vehicle for geostationary missions. To verify and validate its avionics functional perimeter, the IOS Avionics team needs equipment simulators: lightweight stand-ins for onboard units that reproduce their interfaces and protocols, so flight software and avionics can be tested on the bench without the real hardware.
Supervised by an avionics engineer and working within the team, you will take part in designing and developing these simulators and their test tooling. You will start with a first simple equipment model, then progressively take on more complex interfaces, integration on the test bench, and, depending on your progress, embedded development to integrate these equipment into the flight software.
What you'll do
- Develop equipment simulators in Python, C or C++ , running on Raspberry Pi or microcontrollers (STM32, SAM3X…)
- Implement communication links such as UART, RS-422/RS-485, Ethernet (TCP/UDP), CAN, SPI/I2C, as well as software-only simulators when no physical link is needed
- Write automated Python tests that exercise the avionics interfaces and support verification and validation activities
- Set up and maintain test benches: hardware wiring, network configuration , tooling and integration into the team's workflow
- Contribute to embedded flight software development to integrate equipment drivers and interfaces , using your simulators to test them
- Document your work and share it with the team
What we're looking for
- Final-year student (Master's or engineering school) in embedded systems, computer science or a related field
- Solid skills in C/C++ and Python
- Hands-on embedded development experience ( microcontrollers and/or embedded Linux )
- understanding of hardware/software interactions: serial links, buses, signals, basic networking
- Experience with Git and teamwork
- Working level French, English is a plus
Bonus skills
- Knowledge of ground segment/space concepts (TM/TC, CCSDS, ECSS)
- Test automation (pytest) and CI/CD
- Use of lab equipment (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, power supplies)
- A genuine interest in the space domain and the motivation to build a career in this industry
What we value
- Versatility and curiosity: you'll learn across many areas of satellite avionics, from flight software and ground segment to testing and hardware
- Autonomy, rigor and a pragmatic mindset
- eam spirit and clear communication within an agile team
Why Join Exotrail?
- Contribute to technology that truly operates in space.
- Work on complete systems, from embedded software development to in-orbit operations.
- Collaborate with passionate experts across systems, avionics, software, propulsion, and space operations.
- Take part in innovative projects within a rapidly growing international company.
- Make a direct impact on the space missions and technologies of tomorrow.
Working Environment
- 📍 Offices located in the heart of Toulouse.
- ☕ Complimentary coffee, tea, and fresh fruit available on site.
Work-Life Balance
- 🎉 Regular team events and afterworks.
- 💆 On-site osteopathy sessions organized at both locations.
Recruitment Process
1. HR Interview
Discussion about your background, motivations, and career aspirations.
2. Tutor Interview
Conversation focused on the role, team challenges, and your professional experience.
Ready to launch your career beyond Earth? Join Exotrail and help shape the future of sustainable space mobility. 🚀

ABOUT OVERVIEW ENERGY

Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared light. We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is designed end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. Headquartered in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC area and backed by world-class investors, we are advancing the next generation of clean energy technology.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Intern to design the structure that carries our ground beacon system, including transportation of the system from the lab to the field test.



The beacon and its system components all have to travel together, set up fast, and stay co-located with our observational telescope. Portable, modular, and rigid are competing goals. You'll own that trade and defend it. Alongside the mounting, you'll characterize what the environment does to the installed system so we know how much of the pointing error budget the structure is spending.



This internship supports our program under a Department of War energy investment program.  You'll work directly with the optics team to ensure the structure design meets the optical beacon requirements.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design system mounting for three states: pre-delivery, in transit, and installed at the test site

 - Trade portability and modularity against stiffness and alignment retention, and document the reasoning behind the design you pick

 - Design a transportable platform to house beacon equipment

 - Build parametric CAD models and produce drawings a machine shop can quote and manufacture

 - Analyze environmental effects on the installed system, including temperature and wind loading, and quantify the impact on pointing stability

 - Characterize transportation effects - shock, vibration, and handling - and recommend mitigations

 - Support setup, teardown, and field checkout with the optics team
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR FROM YOU

 - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a closely related field with an expected graduation in Spring 2027

 - Working proficiency in CAD, NX preferred

 - Coursework in statics, mechanics of materials, and vibrations

 - Hands-on fabrication or assembly experience: machine shop, Formula SAE, robotics, research lab, or your own builds

 - Able to commit 5-10 hours per week from September 2026 through March 2027, on-site in Northern Virginia




WE HAVE A STRONG PREFERENCE FOR

 - FEA experience for static, modal, or random vibration analysis (NX / NASTRAN)

 - Exposure to shock and vibration testing, or to transportation environment standards such as MIL-STD-810

 - GD&T fluency and practical DFM/DFA judgment

 - Experience designing optomechanical mounts, kinematic mounts, or other alignment-critical hardware

 - Demonstrated interest in defense, space, or energy applications




INTERNSHIP DETAILS

This is a paid, part-time internship running September 2026 through March 2027 at 5-10 hours per week, based on-site at our Northern Virginia headquarters. Hourly rate: $30-$40.



You'll be mentored directly by the engineers running the program, and your work is a funded DoW deliverable, not a side project. 




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

This position is subject to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Candidates must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Overview Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.



If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at talent@overviewenergy.com.



Research shows that women and individuals from underrepresented groups often only apply for roles where they meet every listed qualification. If you believe you can succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply - even if you don't check every box.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

To have the opportunity to collaborate with Cohere researchers and tools on designing and implementing novel research ideas and shipping state-of-the-art models to production. We have openings in teams covering base model training, retrieval augmented generation, data and evaluation, safety, and finetuning, to name a few; and we are open to receiving intern applications in any research area relating to LLMs to broaden your research connections while obtaining deep experience in a growing AI startup. 
Please Note: To be eligible for a Research Internship, you must be currently pursuing a PhD in Machine Learning, NLP, or a related discipline. You need to be available for a full-time internship that lasts for 4-6 months.



As a Cohere Research Intern, you will:

 - Conduct cutting-edge machine learning research, building and training large language models. 

 - Focus on research projects aimed at expanding the frontier of knowledge in language modelling and associate areas such as evaluation, multimodal models, optimisation etc.

 - Disseminate your research results through the production of publications, datasets, and code.

 - Contribute to research initiatives that have practical applications in Cohere’s product development. 

You may be a good fit if you:

 - Are currently pursuing, or in the process of obtaining, a PhD in Machine Learning, NLP, Artificial Intelligence, or a related discipline. We will also consider exceptional non-PhD candidates.

 - Are eligible for work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire and maintain ongoing work authorization throughout the internship period. 

 - Have experience using large-scale distributed training strategies, data annotation and evaluation pipelines, or implementing state of the art ML models.

 - Are familiar with autoregressive sequence models, such as Transformers.

 - Have strong communication and problem-solving skills with the ability to convey complex research findings clearly and succinctly. 

 - Have knowledge, or are knowledgeable, of programming languages such as Python, C, C++, Lua, or related languages.

 - Have knowledge of related ML frameworks such as JAX, Pytorch and Tensorflow.

 - Have previous experience in building systems based on machine learning and deep learning techniques. 

 - Demonstrate passion for applied NLP models and products.

Preferred Qualifications: 

 - Demonstrated expertise through publications in top tier venues in fields such as machine learning, NLP, artificial intelligence, computer vision, optimization, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics, or data science. 

 - Proven ability to tackle analytical problems using quantitative methodologies. 

 - Proficiency in handling and analysing complex, high-dimensional data from various sources.

 - Experience in applying theoretical and empirical research to real-world problem-solving.






FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

About this position:
We're looking for an AI Automation Co-op to embed with teams across Later and help replace manual, repetitive work with AI-powered tooling. This is a hands-on role at the intersection of building and learning: you'll contribute directly to automations that create real business impact across Operations, Finance, Marketing, Customer Success, and beyond while being supported and coached throughout. This role will begin in January 2027.
You'll work closely with Later's AI Automation team and get direct exposure to how AI tools, APIs, and no-code platforms come together to solve real workflow problems across Later's three lines of business (Later Influence, Later Social, and Later Creator). If you're curious about applied AI, love tinkering with new tools, and want to leave a term with a portfolio of things you actually shipped, this is the role for you.
What you'll be doing:
Discovery & Problem Scoping
- Shadow and interview non-technical stakeholders across Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Customer Success to understand their day-to-day workflows.
- Help identify repetitive, manual tasks that are strong candidates for automation.
- Contribute to translating fuzzy workflow problems into clear, scoped technical solutions with guidance from the team.
Building & Shipping
- Build working automations and internal tools using AI-native platforms, APIs, and no-code and low-code tools.
- Ship v1 prototypes quickly so stakeholders can validate value before investment grows.
- Wire together LLMs, agents, and prompt design patterns with existing systems to deliver real workflow outcomes.
- Iterate on automations based on stakeholder feedback and real-world use.
Documentation & Reliability
- Write clear documentation so automations can run unattended and teammates can understand what was built.
- Contribute to error handling and basic monitoring so automations recover gracefully.
- Help maintain a library of reusable templates, prompt patterns, and integration examples.
Enablement & Collaboration
- Support working sessions and lightweight training that helps non-technical colleagues understand and use the automations you build.
- Collaborate with engineers, operations teammates, and other stakeholders to deliver solutions that work in practice.
- Share what you learn openly, contributing to Later's growing citizen-developer community.
What success looks like:
- By the end of your term, you have at least 2-3 automations in production with documented business impact (hours saved, error rates reduced, or cycle times shortened) across different teams.
- Stakeholders can use and understand the automations you built without needing you to explain them every time, because you wrote documentation that actually works.
- You've grown your fluency with AI-native tools, APIs, and no-code platforms and can talk clearly about the tradeoffs of different approaches.
- You've contributed at least one reusable component, prompt template, or integration pattern to Later's shared automation library.
- You leave the term having built real things that are still running, and with a clearer sense of where you want to take your career in applied AI and automation.
What you bring:
- Currently enrolled in a Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or related program, or equivalent practical experience.
- Some experience building with code (Python, JavaScript, C# or similar) and comfort picking up new tools quickly.
- Curiosity about AI and automation: you've experimented with LLMs, prompt design, or no-code tools and want to go deeper.
- A bias toward action: you'd rather ship something imperfect and learn from it than wait for a perfect plan.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, you can explain a technical idea to someone who doesn't code.
- Comfort with ambiguity: you can make progress on a loosely defined problem without needing every detail up front.
- Familiarity with APIs, scripting, or automation tools (Zapier, Make, n8n, or similar) is a bonus.
- Any experience with data: pulling it, cleaning it, and reasoning about what it means, is a plus.
How you work:
- Driven by Impact: You deliver results that matter—prioritizing high-value work, meeting deadlines, and adapting quickly while keeping outcomes clear.
- Strategic & Customer-Centric: You anticipate risks and opportunities, connect decisions to long-term growth, and build trust through proactive insights.
- Curious & Growth-Oriented: You seek knowledge, ask sharp questions, and apply learnings fast—challenging the status quo with a mindset of improvement.
- Collaborative & Resilient: You thrive in change by staying resourceful, solution-focused, and positive—removing roadblocks, sharing insights, and keeping morale high.
- Accountable & Honest: You own your work, hold yourself and others to a high bar, and use transparent feedback to drive growth.
- Emotionally Intelligent: You build trust through empathy and collaboration, foster inclusion, and inspire others with grit, optimism, and integrity.
Our approach to compensation:
We take a market-based & data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation bi-annually, including performance and market-related factors.
Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable) while for others it is structured as Salary only.

$4,000 per month

At Hiverge, our mission is to build algorithmic superintelligence: an AI discovery engine that automatically writes algorithms for the most critical optimisation problems.

Our founding team is composed of world-class researchers from Google DeepMind and University of Cambridge, having co-developed AlphaTensor, FunSearch, and Nobel-prize winning AlphaFold. At Hiverge, you will be working with the brightest minds in AI, algorithms, and mathematics.

If you’re passionate about AI and eager to shape transformative technologies, we’d love to hear from you.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

This role designs, trains, and evaluates LLM‑centric systems. The work blends implementation, experimentation, and benchmarking.

As a Research Engineer Intern you will:

 - Support the development of scalable experimentation foundations with strong reproducibility and observability

 - Help create and improve robust prompt and code-selection tooling.

 - Assist in optimizing our system’s inference and infrastructure for better efficiency.

 - Work with the team (ML engineers and researchers) to implement new ideas.

 - Engage with the research community to advance the state of algorithmic discovery.



QUALIFICATIONS

 - Masters degree in Computer Science, Engineering, related field, or equivalent experience.

 - Strong coding skills in Python and experience with PyTorch/JAX and modern LLM tooling for inference and fine‑tuning.

 - Experience in applied research engineering, demonstrated by impactful academic projects or internships in LLMs, search/RL, or compilers/verification.

 - Exposure to evaluation frameworks, unit/property‑based testing, and performance profiling.



WHAT SETS THE CANDIDATE APART

 - Contributions to open research or community tooling.

 - Familiarity with algorithm design, and practical understanding of reinforcement learning, evolutionary methods and optimization methods.


We offer competitive compensation and a stimulating work environment, with the opportunity to contribute to the future of generative AI.

Outstanding interns may be considered for a full-time Research Engineer position upon completion of the internship.

Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. Applied Intuition is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with offices in Washington, D.C.; San Diego; Ft. Walton Beach, Florida; Ann Arbor, Michigan; London; Stuttgart; Munich; Stockholm; Bangalore; Seoul; and Tokyo. Learn more at applied.co http://applied.co.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for multiple passionate Research Interns to join the Research Group at Applied Intuition. The mission of the group is to create cutting-edge technology enabling next-generation physical AI, with emphasis on the two most challenging applications reshaping our everyday life: end-to-end autonomous driving and robotic generalist. Improvements deployed to our system immediately help our customers with their programs and deliver value to our business.

 - Strong research background and skills on relevant topics, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively on projects

 - Current PhD (or MSc) studies in machine learning, computer vision and graphics, robotics

 - Passion for next-generation, scalable autonomy and robotics

ABOUT CUSPAI 

CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering.

We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock.

We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters.

We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us.





THE ROLE

We are seeking an intern for a 3-month internship to develop fast, accurate machine learning force fields (MLFFs) tailored to high-throughput Monte Carlo simulation, and integrate them into our in-house simulation framework, kUPS. You will be embedded in our chemistry team and work closely with CuspAI colleagues.

Note: You would be joining as an engineering intern within the chemistry team at CuspAI.




YOUR IMPACT

You will deliver one of the foundational capabilities our simulation stack needs to evaluate the next generation of MOFs: an MLFF that is both accurate enough to replace classical force fields for guest–host interactions and fast enough to run inside the inner loop of GCMC. By distilling state-of-the-art equivariant models into a lightweight student potential and integrating the result directly into kUPS, you will expand what is computationally tractable for CuspAI and the wider gas adsorption community.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

Models

 - Distill MLFFs into fast student potentials optimised for Monte Carlo simulations.

 - Curate, version, and document training and validation datasets, including the distillation protocol and any active-learning loops used to close coverage gaps.

Integration & Validation

 - Run head-to-head validation campaigns comparing the distilled MLFF against classical force-field baselines across a curated set of guest molecules, characterising accuracy, throughput, and failure modes.

Systems & Infrastructure

 - Profile and optimise the pipeline for throughput, with particular focus on the MC inner loop where MLFF inference cost dominates.

 - Benchmark accuracy/speed trade-offs systematically and document where the distilled model fails.

Science & Collaboration

 - Collaborate with computational chemists on reference data generation, benchmark system selection, and validation strategy.

 - Contribute to a publication establishing MLFF-driven GCMC for MOF screening.




MUST HAVE SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently enrolled in (or recently completed) a PhD or Master's programme in a relevant quantitative field (Physics, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Computational Science, Machine Learning, or similar).

 - Experience in adsorption modelling at the atomic scale.

 - Hands-on experience with molecular simulation methods (GCMC, MD, or both).

 - Comfortable working on Linux environments and managing simulation campaigns at scale.

 - A genuine interest in the application of ML to chemistry and materials science.




BONUS POINTS (BUT NOT CRITICAL)

 - Familiarity with modern MLFFs.

 - Experience with knowledge distillation or other model compression techniques for scientific ML.

 - Experience with active learning workflows for atomistic data.

 - Familiarity with DFT data generation and the practicalities of curating atomistic datasets.

 - Direct experience with established simulation packages.

 - Background in gas adsorption, MOFs, or porous materials.

 - Familiarity with classical force fields used in MOF simulation.

 - A track record of published research at top-tier ML or computational chemistry venues.





WHAT WE OFFER

 - A competitive salary: We value and reward impact and growth

 - Equity in CuspAI: You have a stake in the success of the company

 - Time off to stay fresh: 28 days holiday (DE, NL, UK) or 21 days holiday (JP, SG, US), in addition to local public holidays

 - ‘Gold Standard’ parental leave: 26 weeks (primary caregiver) and 12 weeks (secondary caregiver) at full pay - we look after you and your family while we work on the most important materials discovery problems together

 - Professional development budget: We invest in your career development so you can stay up to date with the latest industry knowledge or add to your skills to increase impact and growth

 - Solve meaningful problems: See how your work has a direct impact on advancing materials science and solving sustainability and climate-related problems through the creation and application of bleeding-edge SOTA technology and revolutionary techniques

 - True interdisciplinary teamwork: Be part of a deeply collaborative environment bridging AI research, computational chemistry, and experimental science - work with world-class researchers and engineers who enjoy sharing knowledge and supporting each other


Join us in shaping the future of materials with AI. Together, we can create groundbreaking solutions for a more sustainable world.

Work on whatever part of the pipeline your background makes you particularly formidable at. We'll match the project to you, not the other way around.

Logistics and compensation

In-person at our Dumbo office. 10–12 weeks, flexible start. You'll work directly with Antonio (CTO) and Rupesh (CEO), alongside the core team.

We're hiring a Research Intern to help us answer a question no one has answered yet: how do you train a model that is genuinely good at research?

This is hard, and largely uncharted. Very few groups have managed to teach LLMs to perform the open-ended, long-horizon reasoning that real research demands: forming a hypothesis, designing an experiment, reading the result, and deciding what to try next. We're doing it with a small team and a strong prior that research data can be used in a highly efficient and ingenious way.

As a Research Intern, you'll own a real research question rather than a ticket. Depending on your interests, that might mean turning a corpus of arXiv papers into reinforcement learning environments, designing reward signals for ambiguous, long-horizon research tasks, building tight RL loops between user data and model training, or constructing research-focused benchmarks. 



What you'll do

 - Post-train models for scientific and computational research tasks

 - Build evaluations and benchmarks for such tasks, and use them to measure frontier models and our own
   
   

Required qualifications

 - Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Statistics, or Linguistics

 - Research experience in at least one area of machine learning or its neighbors (natural language processing, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimization, statistics, etc.)

 - Ability to move quickly in a zero-to-one environment



Preferred qualifications

 - A track record of research contributions, such as first-author publications at major ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR) or strong journals.

 - Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or benchmarking large modern models.

ABOUT FIRETIGER

Firetiger is on a mission to help our customers build 1-person, $1 billion revenue companies.

We believe that eventually, all companies will be software companies, and the vast majority of coordination will be handled by autonomous agents, not people. To get there, we are helping software companies become "self-driving".

Legacy software engineering operations software is built for humans to manually explore data and patch together brittle alerts. The last generation of tools like Datadog is designed to enable humans to understand how software behaves. Firetiger flips the script. We approach operations from first principles: customers define top-down what success looks like for a business and product, then deploy agents to constantly monitor to ensure those goals are met and close the loop.

We are founded by Rustam http://linkedin.com/in/lalkaka and Achille https://www.linkedin.com/in/achille-roussel/, former leaders from Cloudflare and Segment, and backed by Sequoia Capital and founders and executives at Cloudflare, Segment, Amazon, Anthropic, Cursor, and Plaid.

We are looking for a Product Engineer to build the interfaces between humans and AI agents: the workflows, visualizations, and interaction patterns that make autonomous technical operations intuitive and actionable.




THE ROLE

Firetiger's agents find production problems before your customers find them and your CEO hears about them. Here's how it works:

 1. We ingest telemetry with high-cardinality detail and automatically model what your system is and how it works

 2. Customers define objectives in natural language (e.g., "customers should have OAuth configured correctly") that stay relevant as infrastructure evolves

 3. Agents autonomously investigate issues, determine root cause, and take action to remediate

You'll build the product experiences that make this magic legible—turning complex autonomous investigations into something engineers actually want to use. You'll also build the agents themselves.

This is not a role where you implement specs handed down from product. You will own problems end-to-end: talking to customers, defining what to build, building it, and iterating until it's great.




WHAT YOU WILL ACCOMPLISH

 - Agent interfaces: Design how engineers interact with AI agents operating their software systems. What should autonomous software operations look like? How do you give humans the right level of visibility and control?

 - The agents themselves: Build the brains that turn messy natural-language objectives into the crisp outputs our customers rely on to run their businesses. You'll work on the core intelligence, not just the UI around it.

 - Real-time collaboration tools: Create experiences where engineers can watch agents work, redirect wayward chains-of-thought, and collaborate on complex debugging sessions.

 - Novel data exploration: Design new UX patterns for exploring high-cardinality data that agents surface. Think beyond traditional dashboards to new ways of understanding customer-specific issues at scale.




WHO YOU ARE

 - High Agency: You don't wait for permission. You see a problem, whether a confusing user flow or missing feature, and you fix it. You ship.

 - Product-Minded: You care about the why behind what you build. You talk to customers. You have opinions about what makes developer tools great vs. frustrating.

 - Full-Stack Capable: You're comfortable working across the stack to deliver complete features. You've built complex, data-heavy web applications and know how to make them fast.

 - AI-Curious: You've built with LLMs, or at a minimum collaborated with agentic development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc) to write software. You're excited about the design challenges of human-AI collaboration.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience: You're excited about building and shipping user-facing software products. You have examples of projects you drove end-to-end that users loved.

 - Communication: You can write a clear product spec, explain a technical tradeoff to a customer, and give direct feedback to teammates.




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - $120k salary prorated for internship term

 - In-person in San Francisco




HOW TO APPLY

We care more about your projects than your pedigree.

In your application, please include a link to something you've built: a side project, an open-source contribution, a product feature you're proud of. Show us how you think about building software products.

ABOUT ARCHITECT LABS

Architect is a frontier AI lab for custom silicon. We partner with frontier labs, clouds / neoclouds, physical AI companies, and advanced fabs to tape-out custom chips co-designed for next-generation AI workloads. Our goal is to compress end-to-end software to silicon timelines, and maximize intelligence per watt and per dollar for the world. We are a small exceptional team across silicon, systems, software and frontier AI. Our team have led research teams at nearly every frontier AI lab, and at some of the most complex SoCs in the world.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a Research Intern at Architect, you will spend 3 months working alongside the founding team to push the boundaries of how AI models explore and optimize hardware designs. This is a high-impact role where your experiments will directly influence our core modeling roadmap.

 - Responsible for co-designing and implementing the Reinforcement Learning experiments (GRPO/PPO/DPO), training data mixes and reward signal explorations.

 - Contribute to research on post-training techniques, running ablation studies to improve model reasoning and alignment capabilities.

 - Implement and test new algorithms for model fine-tuning and evaluation, helping to translate research papers into working prototypes.

 - Analyze experimental results and debug model behavior to help establish best practices for our training recipes.
   
   


WHAT WE'D LIKE TO SEE

Qualifications & Skills:

 - Education: Currently pursuing a PhD or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, or a related field. Exceptional undergraduates with strong research experience are also encouraged to apply.

 - RL Knowledge: Strong academic understanding or project experience with Reinforcement Learning (e.g., PPO, DPO, GRPO). You should be comfortable reading and implementing concepts from recent research papers.

 - Coding Proficiency: Strong proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch). You should be able to write clean, efficient research code.

 - Research Mindset: A fast learner who is comfortable navigating ambiguity. You enjoy analyzing complex problems and iterating quickly on experiments.

 - LLM Familiarity: Experience with training or fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) or familiarity with the modern NLP stack (Transformers, HuggingFace, etc.).
   
   


BONUS:

 - Previous internship experience at frontier AI labs or research organizations.

 - Publications (or submissions) in top ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML) or EDA venues (DAC, ICCAD).

 - Familiarity with hardware design concepts (Verilog, RTL, EDA tools), though not required.
   
   


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive internship stipend

 - Mentorship from a team of researchers and engineers from Anthropic, DeepMind, Meta, and Stanford

 - Opportunity to work on 0→1 problems in AI-driven chip design

ABOUT US

Forus is building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to accelerate new science to patients.

Our platform automates the complexity between a doctor prescribing a medicine and a patient starting treatment, including insurance coverage, financial assistance, and supply chain navigation. We provide this support free to doctors and patients, helping them get life-changing medicine faster, cheaper, and easier. The resulting network enables biopharma companies to design better research, launch new drugs more effectively, and invest in harder-to-treat conditions.

Forus has exceptional product-market fit and is growing rapidly through organic adoption:

 - Accelerating scale: We already support patients across more than 85% of ZIP codes and partner with 9 of top 15 largest biopharma companies in the world.

 - AI-native, durable model: Our business becomes stronger as AI improves, as every new doctor, patient, and partner makes the network more valuable.

 - Backing to build for the long term: We raised $300M+ from leading investors to build an exceptional team and unlock the full scale of the opportunity.

Our number one priority is scaling to market demand. We are looking for individuals who are high horsepower, high throughput, and hyper resourceful to help us increase capacity and grow. We move fast and need to move faster.

If we succeed, science will be the only limit to medicine.

All full-time roles are in person in New York.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Software Engineering Intern at Forus, you will join our engineering team as an engineer, not as an observer. From your first weeks, you’ll ship production code, own meaningful technical problems, and build software that helps providers, patients, and life sciences organizations bring innovative therapies to more patients.

Unlike a traditional internship, you’ll work on the same systems as our full-time engineers and contribute to the same codebase, engineering reviews, and technical discussions. You’ll work directly with experienced engineers, the head of engineering, and the CEO on some of the company’s highest-priority technical challenges, whether that’s provider-facing products, AI systems, life sciences platforms, growth acceleration, or infrastructure. This isn’t an internship spent building internal demos or isolated side projects. You will help build the platform that sits between scientific innovation and patient treatment, working on the products and AI systems that providers and biopharma depend on every day.

We invest in exceptional interns differently than most companies. Many stay with us across multiple semesters, take on increasing ownership as they grow, and some receive return offers and start vesting equity before they graduate. We think the best engineers should start building their careers early, and we’re looking for people we hope will help define Forus for years to come.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to “act like an owner” and commit yourself to Forus’ success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

Please note that we hire Interns year-round.




IF YOU JOIN, YOU WILL

 - Own meaningful technical problems from an ambiguous idea through design, implementation, and production

 - Ship production code that directly impacts providers, patients, and life sciences partners.

 - Help decide what to build, not just how to build it, by working closely with users and developing your own product intuition

 - Build product features, AI-powered systems, life sciences products, internal tools, or engineering infrastructure, depending on where you can have the greatest impact

 - Work directly with engineering, product, design, operations, and company leadership while learning how a world-class engineering organization operates and scales

 - Be treated and measured like a full engineer, with the ownership, code review, and quality bar to match
   
   


WE’LL BE MOST EXCITED IF YOU HAVE

 - Strong computer science fundamentals and programming ability, currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related technical field

 - A track record of building things outside the classroom, whether through internships, research, startups, hackathons, open-source contributions, or side projects

 - Strong product instincts. You form opinions about what is worth building and can distinguish what is valuable from what is merely possible

 - The ability and willingness to work wherever the problem is, whether frontend, backend, infrastructure, AI, or something entirely new

 - A track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals

 - High NPS with your former teammates and classmates



This is a list of ideal qualifications for this position. If you don't meet every single one of them, you should still consider applying! We’re excited to work with people from underrepresented backgrounds, and we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.




WORKING WITH US

Forus is based in New York, with our full team working out of a beautiful and spacious office in SoHo. 

We run as a high-trust environment with high autonomy, which requires that everyone is fully competent and operates in line with our principles:

 - Do the math.  Be rigorous, assume nothing. Break problems down and reason from the ground up. Stay open to changing your mind.

 - Resourceful optimism.  Assume problems are solvable. Be audacious. Resist false constraints and push beyond the obvious before deciding.

 - Spit it out.  Speak directly, invite critique, avoid equivocation. We want right answers, not comfortable ones. All killer, no filler.

 - Raise the bar.  Hold a high standard for your pace and execution, and elevate the performance of the team around you. Mamba mentality.

 - Fight for users.  Start with users’ realities, not ours. Resist optimizing for internal convenience over user outcomes.
   

We provide competitive compensation with meaningful equity (for full-time employees). Everyone who joins will be a major contributor to our success, and we reflect this through ownership and pay.

We also provide rich benefits to ensure you can focus on creating impact (for full-time employees):

 - Fully covered medical, vision, and dental insurance.

 - Memberships for One Medical, Talkspace, Teladoc, and Kindbody.

 - Unlimited paid time off (PTO) and 16 weeks of parental leave.

 - 401K plan setup, FSA option, commuter benefits, and DashPass.

 - Lunch at the office every day and Dinner at the office after 6:30 pm.


Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our company’s size and industry, and are one part of the total compensation package that also includes equity, benefits, and other opportunities at Forus (for full-time employees). Individual pay decisions are ultimately based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, geography, and balancing internal equity. 

Forus is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

🧠 About Yotta Labs

Yotta Labs is building the next generation multi-silicon AI cloud and runtime platform to power the world’s most demanding AI workloads. We are seeking a highly motivated Research Engineer Intern to work on Trainium, GPU kernels, and LLM systems optimization.
