Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.
Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
Responsibilities
As a Software Engineering Intern at Keysight’s High Frequency Technology Center, your primary focus will be developing software automation for CAD-related engineering workflows, including design review, CAD data generation, verification, and repeatable process checks. You will help build practical tools that reduce manual review effort, improve consistency across engineering handoffs, and make CAD workflow steps more traceable, reliable, and scalable. This work may include translating engineering rules and review criteria into automated checks, improving how CAD artifacts and related metadata are generated or validated, and supporting workflow documentation so that automation can be maintained and extended over time. In addition to the CAD automation focus, you will contribute to the definition, implementation, and documentation of data ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) workflows and data pipelines that organize engineering and manufacturing data for reliable downstream use. You may also support machine learning model definition and implementation, including data preparation, model workflow development, and evaluation of how these methods can be applied to real engineering and manufacturing problems. Throughout the internship, you will work closely with engineering and manufacturing teams to turn project needs into maintainable software solutions in a technical semiconductor environment.
Preference will be given to candidates that can commit to a 6+ month internship, but shorter internships will also be considered.
Qualifications
Qualifications
- Currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate program in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Electrical Engineering with a software focus, or a related technical field.
- Programming experience in Python, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or a similar modern software development language.
- Interest or experience in workflow automation, CAD/EDA tooling, engineering software, data processing, or manufacturing systems.
- Experience with databases, SQL, ETL concepts, data pipelines, APIs, or structured data documentation is preferred.
- Exposure to machine learning concepts, model development, data preparation, or model evaluation is preferred.
- Candidates must have strong problem-solving, communication, documentation, and collaboration skills for successful interaction with engineering, software, and manufacturing teams.
- Must be highly motivated, detail-oriented, and comfortable learning new tools and technical workflows in a fast-paced engineering environment.

Candidates who wish to be considered must be currently enrolled in an accredited college or university undergraduate or graduate program as of September 2027. Applicants who have graduated before the internship start date will not be considered unless they are starting a new undergraduate or graduate program after graduating.
Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position. Candidates who now or at any point in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B Visa status) may not be considered.

wd:kla:2641392-1:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The RAPID division leads the industry in reticle inspection solutions, helping ensure high lithography yields and cost-effective semiconductor manufacturing. Its systems support both mask shops and fabs by detecting defects early in the process, enabling faster, more reliable production.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Responsibilities
- Apply Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques to image transformation and defect detection.
- Analyze large-scale image datasets and evaluate algorithm performance.
- Prototype algorithms using Python, PyTorch, and TensorFlow.
- Develop production-quality software using Modern C++ and Python.
- Apply best practices in software design, testing, debugging, code reviews, and version control.
- Collaborate with algorithm, software, systems, and application engineers to deploy solutions into production.
Required Qualifications
- Strong background in Computer Vision, Image Processing, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or Pattern Recognition.
- Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python.
- Familiarity with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or equivalent ML frameworks.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with CNNs, Vision Transformers, or segmentation models.
- Experience with Modern C++ software development.
- Knowledge of image enhancement, image registration, feature extraction, or anomaly detection.
- Experience with large-scale datasets and quantitative algorithm evaluation.
What You'll Gain
- Hands-on experience in AI, Computer Vision, Deep Learning, Image Processing, Modern C++, and Software Engineering.
- End-to-end exposure to algorithm development, optimization, and deployment.
- Experience building scalable, production-quality software.
- Mentorship from experts in algorithms, imaging, software engineering, and semiconductor inspection.
Minimum Qualifications
Pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Data Science, or a related field.
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Total Rewards
Base Pay Range: $58.00 - $58.00 per hour based on pursuit of a Ph.D.
Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA
KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave.

We are committed to complying with all applicable federal and state minimum wage requirements where applicable. Job Overview
Are you interested in using environmental data and technology to help one of the world’s busiest airports prepare for future challenges? The Environmental Technical Projects Internship provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience improving data quality, developing meaningful metrics, and supporting environmental resilience at DFW Airport.
Working alongside environmental professionals, the intern will help organize and standardize data across Environmental Affairs Department programs. This work will support the development of a Resilience Stress Testing Tool designed to help assess potential risks and operational performance under extreme conditions. This internship is designed for students interested in environmental science, data analytics, engineering, or a related field.
What you will be doing:
- Inventories environmental and operational datasets, documenting data sources, formats, ownership, and current uses across department programs.
- Reviews datasets for accuracy, completeness, and consistency; identifies gaps and assists with cleaning and standardizing information for analysis.
- Supports the preparation and validation of data for use in the Resilience Stress Testing Tool, working with team members to understand data requirements.
- Assists with reviewing and refining program metrics and developing reports or visualizations that help department leaders assess performance and potential risks.
- Collaborates with program teams to document data definitions, quality checks, and maintenance procedures and recommend improvements that support future analytics projects.
What you need:
- Must be an active student in a Bachelor’s degree program in environmental science, environmental engineering, data analytics, data science, information systems, civil engineering, or a related field.
- 18 years of age or older.
What we desire:
- Current, cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher, including but not limited to students attending the following universities: University of North Texas, University of Texas at Arlington, University of Texas at Dallas, Paul Quinn College, or University of Oklahoma.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position at this time.
About Us
We are Dallas Fort Worth International (DFW) Airport-one of the most successful airports in the world by any definition. We are recognized for our innovation, leadership, drive for excellence and talented employees.
Our success is made possible because of the diverse talents of over 2,100 employees who champion our mission of providing an exceptional airport experience to our customers and connect our community to the world. We are looking for the best talent to join us and help reimagine what an airport can be.
Bring your talents to DFW. Live and work with purpose.

NVIDIA Research is seeking PhD-level students to work as research interns and drive groundbreaking research at the intersection of AI, GPU computing, Formal Methods, and Electronic Design Automation (EDA). AI and GPU acceleration are transforming chip design, and this role offers the opportunity to shape that future. In this internship, you will gain a broad perspective across areas including EDA algorithms, agentic AI, LLMs, and GPU computing. Specific areas of research interest include but are not limited to GPU-accelerated optimization algorithms, physical design algorithms, formal methods, agentic AI, and reinforcement learning techniques.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Apply AI (Agentic AI, LLMs, Generative AI, Reinforcement learning) and GPU acceleration to chip design workflows.
- Research and develop creative and innovative EDA software and algorithms.
- Collaborate with circuits, VLSI, and architecture team members in research and product teams.
- Plan to publish and present your original research
What We Need To See:
- Pursuing a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields
- Publications in leading EDA or AI conferences on AI for EDA, Formal Methods, or GPU-accelerated EDA.
- Excellent programming skills in rapid prototyping environments such as Python; C++ and parallel programming (e.g., CUDA) is a plus.
- Expertise in EDA (e.g., formal verification techniques, logic synthesis, physical design, and timing and signoff) algorithms combined with publications and project experience applying AI to impactful problems.
- Excellent self-motivation, a high degree of creativity, and a passion for research, collaboration skills, and the ability to work effectively within a research team.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with proven experience communicating technical work (e.g., academic presentations, poster sessions); ability to synthesize and explain complex technical concepts.
Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA has some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world inventing the future for us. Are you a creative and collaborative researcher interested in seeking new challenges? If so, we want to hear from you!

The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today.

Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to help ensure products meet quality, performance, and reliability standards. Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
About the Job:
Keysight is looking for an electrical engineering intern to join our R&D team in Colorado Springs, CO. This individual will be responsible for designing next-generation technology for test and measurement applications, including electronic elements for oscilloscope products, modular RF products, and/or probes and accessories products.
The ideal candidate is working towards a BS or MS in EE or ECE and shows proficiency in PCA circuit design and simulation. The candidate should be a self-starter with strong communication skills.
About the Team:
Come make an impact with Keysight’s Digital and Photonics Center of Excellence located in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Enjoy Colorado’s abundance of outdoor recreational opportunities while working in an engineering environment dedicated to innovation, contribution, trust, respect and teamwork. As part of our R&D team you will be a member of our diverse group of world-class electrical, mechanical, and software engineers, helping you transform your designs into high-demand products.
Responsibilities
- Design PCAs for cutting-edge electronic measurement products.
- Own the component selection and schematic design of PCAs under your control.
- Use simulation software as necessary to validate conceptual circuit designs.
- Work closely with PCA layout resources to ensure placement and routing meet your design requirements.
- Work closely with other engineering disciplines on your team to capture and incorporate their requirements into your designs, such as mounting locations, interconnections, heat sinks, RF shields, etc.
- Document your designs for ongoing and future reference.
- Test, debug, and characterize your designs to ensure they function as intended.
- In general, apply EE knowledge and skills to represent your discipline among a collaborative design team. Help your team weigh tradeoffs and solve problems.
- Continue to grow in your discipline and learn new skills as necessary to make your team successful.
Qualifications
Requirements:
- Working towards a BS or MS in EE/ECE or have applicable experience and education
- Familiarity with circuit design and analysis, PCA design, component selection, etc.
- Knowledge of simulation tools for concept validation
- Familiarity with schematic and layout tools
- Experience using electronic test and measurement equipment
- Passion to continuously investigate new technologies, tools, and processes within your discipline
- Self-motivation – must enjoy solving difficult and sometimes open-ended design problems in a team environment
- Strong work ethic
- Strong communication and documentation skills, ability to collaborate cross-functionally with a team-oriented mindset
Desired Qualifications:
- Working towards an MS in EE/ECE
- Familiarity with digital and RF components such samplers, filters, mixers and transmission lines
- Experience with Mentor Graphics
- Experience with Keysight’s ADS software package
- Ability to perform hands-on measurements with VNAs, oscilloscopes and signal generators
- Experience with the complete design-prototype-analyze cycle.
This is a paid, full-time internship of approximately 12 weeks, based on-site at Keysight’s Colorado Springs, Colorado facility. On-site presence is required for access to instrument hardware and measurement lab facilities. Start and end dates are flexible around your academic calendar.
The level of role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the salary listed below.

We are seeking a motivated engineering intern to support the implementation of Smart Visual Inspection within our Austin Order Fulfillment and packaging operations. The intern will work with engineering, operations, quality, and production teams to develop and validate a computer-vision-enabled inspection process for packaging and finished-product verification.
The internship will provide hands-on experience with smart manufacturing, computer vision, machine learning, manufacturing process improvement, inspection-system development, and operational deployment. The intern will help convert existing inspection requirements into repeatable digital workflows, develop image datasets, configure inspection recipes, validate model performance, optimize camera and lighting conditions, and document the solution for production use.
The Smart Visual Inspection platform enables engineers to create guided inspection procedures, train and deploy AI models, provide immediate pass/fail feedback, and capture inspection results for traceability. The Austin proof of concept will initially focus on pack-out applications such as verifying product accessories, quantities, text, labels, orientation, and packaging contents
Responsibilities
- Assist with the development and implementation of Smart Visual Inspection solutions for Order Fulfillment, packaging, and finished-product inspection.
- Study current inspection and pack-out processes, identify improvement opportunities, and translate operational requirements into structured inspection workflows.
- Work with engineers and production personnel to identify representative products and packaging configurations for proof-of-concept testing.
- Capture, organize, and maintain image datasets under representative operating conditions.
- Label and annotate images used for computer-vision model training.
- Safely move, position, and prepare product cartons and packaging materials while capturing images from multiple angles for computer-vision model development and validation.
- Develop and maintain digital inspection procedures and inspection recipes.
- Train and test computer-vision models for applications such as:
- Object presence and absence verification
- Quantity verification
- Packaging-content validation
- Label and text recognition
- Product-position and orientation checks
- Region-based classification
- Evaluate model performance and help adjust confidence thresholds to balance false accepts and false rejects.
- Conduct controlled tests using representative products, packaging materials, accessories, labels, and configurations.
- Support the setup and optimization of cameras, fixtures, workstations, backgrounds, and diffuse lighting.
- Evaluate how camera position, lighting, glare, shadows, object placement, and image quality affect inspection reliability.
- Record test results, model performance, inspection exceptions, process times, and identified improvement opportunities.
- Assist with root-cause analysis and troubleshooting when an inspection process produces inconsistent or unexpected results.
- Develop standard operating procedures, work instructions, training materials, and technical documentation.
- Support operator training and collect feedback during pilot deployment.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to incorporate operational feedback and improve the inspection process.
- Help establish a repeatable process for maintaining inspection procedures, trained models, configuration files, and revision history.
- Present project status, technical findings, validation results, and final recommendations to engineering and operations stakeholders.
These responsibilities reflect the project’s documented needs around image capture and annotation, model training, validation thresholds, camera and lighting consistency, inspection-workflow development, traceability, and pack-out verification

JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

Teaching a 40-ton excavator to move like an expert operator is a very different problem from teaching a car to stay in its lane. The motions are multimodal, there are many good ways to swing, dig, and dump and the consequences of getting them wrong are measured in cubic yards and bent steel. Bedrock's Behavior ML team builds the learned policies that decide what our machines actually do, and diffusion policies are a central bet: models that can represent the full distribution of expert behavior instead of averaging it into mush. As our Behavior ML intern, you'll help train those policies and build the evaluation that tells us whether they're genuinely better working alongside two hosts who sit on both the training and evaluation sides of the problem.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Train and iterate on diffusion flow matching, and related behavior policies using real fleet demonstration data and simulated rollouts

 - Run architecture, conditioning, and hyperparameter explorations, and turn the results into clear findings the team can build on

 - Build and improve evaluation pipelines that score behavior models on task success, smoothness, safety margins, and operator-likeness

 - Investigate failure modes - distribution shift, mode collapse, out-of-distribution scenes and propose fixes

 - Work with the simulation and eval teams to make sure offline metrics actually predict on-machine performance

 - Contribute to the shared training codebase with clean, reviewed, reproducible work

 - Share results regularly with the behavior, controls, and autonomy teams


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, robotics, machine learning, or a related field or bringing equivalent research or industry experience

 - Strong Python and hands-on experience training models in PyTorch (or equivalent)

 - Working understanding of generative modeling diffusion models, flow matching, VAEs, or similar and of imitation learning or behavior cloning

 - Experience running and interpreting real training experiments: you know how to tell a real improvement from noise

 - Clear communication, you can explain what you tried, what happened, and what you'd do next


PREFERRED

 - Published work or substantial project experience in diffusion, flow matching, robot learning, or imitation learning

 - Experience training and building Vision Language Action (VLA) models

 - Experience training Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies for robot manipulation

 - Experience evaluating policies in simulation and reasoning about the sim-to-real gap

 - Familiarity with large-scale training infrastructure and experiment tracking tooling

 - Exposure to robotics, autonomous vehicles, or other physical-world control problems

 - Interest in construction, earthwork, or heavy equipment - no prior experience required

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 






ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring Software Engineering Interns to join our team for a 6-month internship. You'll work closely with our CTO, Sven Beck, and with our project and sales teams, not on the sidelines but on live work.

Depending on where the business's priorities sit at any given time, your day-to-day will flex between two areas of our engineering work:

 - Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE): building production systems directly inside customer environments, alongside a Senior Consultant and other FDEs.

 - Internal Tooling & Applied AI: building the AI-powered internal tools that make our own hiring, finance, and operations run faster.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

On Forward Deployed Engineering work

 - Sit with end-users, process owners, and client engineers to understand the real workflow, and the real problem underneath the stated one.

 - Help translate the target-state process into a concrete technical solution: architecture, data model, integrations, agent and workflow design.

 - Build full-stack: TypeScript backend, integrations, LLM orchestration, evals.

 - Support demos with real users and help fold their feedback into the next iteration.

 - Help own observability and evals once a solution is live, iterating until it's reliable under the customer's real conditions.

On Internal Tooling & Applied AI work

 - Build and ship AI-powered internal tools fast: days and weeks, not quarters.

 - Evaluate, integrate, and chain the latest AI models, APIs, and frameworks (LLMs, agent frameworks, embedding pipelines, AI coding tools) into internal solutions.

 - Write clean, maintainable code that integrates with our existing systems (APIs, databases, third-party services).

 - Help own deployments end-to-end: build it, test it, ship it, monitor it.

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, or a Master's degree in Engineering with Computer Science coursework.

 - Hands-on experience with modern AI tooling: LLM APIs, AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), agent frameworks, or workflow automation.

 - Comfortable with TypeScript, or confident you can get there fast: you pick up new tools and stacks quickly.

 - A fast-moving, entrepreneurial mindset: you've built something (a side project, a hack, a tool people actually used) rather than just studied how to.

 - You enjoy working with non-technical teams and can turn a messy, half-stated problem into a clear, working solution.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast feedback cycles.

 - Fluent in English; German is a plus.

 - Bonus: exposure to ERP or business-process environments (SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar), or tools like Make, n8n, Retool, or Supabase.

 


WHAT YOU'LL GET

 - Live work, not a training exercise. Everything you touch ships to real customers or runs inside the company for real.

 - Work at the frontier. Use and build with state-of-the-art tech, the latest LLMs, agent frameworks, and AI coding tools.

 - Real ownership from day one. Shape internal tooling from the ground up, or own pieces of a live customer engagement.

 - A clear, fast path to a permanent role. For the right candidates.

A LITTLE ABOUT US

incident.io http://incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.




THIS IS A FULL-TIME, ONE YEAR PLACEMENT STARTING IN JUNE 2027 AND FINISHING IN JUNE 2028.




THE ROLE IN ONE LINE

Whether you join as an intern or a grad, your first real code here doesn't sit in a sandbox- it ships to the teams keeping the internet online, even in week 1.

 


WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE DAY TO DAY

You'll sit inside one of our product teams from day one- same stand-ups, same code review, same production access as everyone else. You'll pick up real work alongside full-time engineers, and you'll own at least one meaningful project end to end: idea, build, ship, watch people use it.

Our engineers know what it's like to be paged at 3am- the adrenaline, the scramble to pull the right people in, the frustration of piecing context together from a dozen scattered tools. Everything we build is aimed at killing that experience. Which means the stakes are real: thousands of companies are mid-incident when they open incident.io http://incident.io, so we care about polish as much as we care about speed.

You'll work in Go, TypeScript with React, and Postgres, deployed on Google Cloud using GKE and Cloud SQL. Infrastructure is Terraform, with BigQuery, PubSub and Cloud Storage in the mix. Sentry, Grafana + Prometheus and Kibana for monitoring, CircleCI for testing and deploys. You won't know all of that on day one, and nobody expects you to.

Over the past year we've built some of the most ambitious AI-native features in our space- agents that investigate incidents, explain what's happening, and increasingly fix things themselves. Interns and grads work on this, not around it. We're all-in on AI internally too, and you'll have unlimited AI spend from your first week.

We'll be straight with you about the bar: we'll treat you like a full-time engineer. Full ownership, hard deadlines and shipping fast enough that you'll break things and learn from it. There's genuine support around you- senior engineers, proper mentorship, people invested in you doing well- but nobody's going to hold your hand through it.

 


WHAT YOUR BACKGROUND LOOKS LIKE:

 - You're enrolled in a full-time Bachelors degree in Computer Science (or a related field)

 - Know any programming language such as: Go, C#, Python, Ruby on Rails or Javascript.

 


WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:

 - Have a bias for action and ownership and like to get things shipped, learn from mistakes, and take responsibility for your work.

 - Stay curious and don’t just accept things as they are, enjoying asking “why?” and “what if?”

 - Collaborate in person and get energy from being around others, bouncing around ideas, asking questions, and giving and receiving feedback.

 - Love building whether it’s features, tools, or ideas, and enjoy creating things and seeing them make an impact.

 - Enjoy fast-paced environments and feel comfortable with change and the energy that comes with moving quickly.

 - Keep a low ego by staying humble and staying focused on the wider mission.

A Note on applying to Pangram:

At Pangram, we firmly believe that genuine human expression, and our ability to communicate with each other online and through the written word, is a fundamental right- and a value worth preserving.

Please don't use AI to answer any of the questions as part of your application - we want to hear from you!
 

About Pangram Labs

Pangram Labs’ mission is to protect authenticity and preserve human connection in the context of the generative AI era. We build the world’s best AI detection systems. We publish research on state-of-the-art AI detection techniques and algorithms and build products to bring our technology into people's daily lives. We provide tools for individuals, institutions and companies to detect the use of AI in written content.

Pangram is a recognized thought leader in the space of AI detection. Our CEO & Co-founder Max Spero has been named as one of Time Magazine’s 100 Most Influential People in AI https://time.com/collection/time100-ai/2026/max-spero/ and Pangram has been named one of Time’s Best Inventions of 2026 https://time.com/collection/best-inventions/2026/pangram-3-0/.

We are looking for high agency, mission-driven, and passionate builders to join our team!



About the Role:

Pangram Labs is hiring talented AI Research Interns for Spring or Summer 2027.

As an AI Research Intern at Pangram Labs, you will conduct research relating to frontier AI detection research or related topics, with the goal of publishing a paper in a major conference venue. Examples of past internship projects at Pangram include EditLens (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.03154) and Scaling Laws for Wild AI Text (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40295).



What You’ll Do

Interns are assigned a mentor, and choose a research topic or area prior to the internship. Current active research areas within Pangram include:

 - Adversarial Robustness: how do detectors perform against humanizers and adversarial paraphrasing?

 - Interpretability: can we build more explainable, interpretable AI detection?

 - Mixed Human/AI Authorship: how can we quantify the different facets of human-AI coauthorship?

 - New Architectures: how can we optimize Pangram’s architecture for efficiency or even higher levels of accuracy?

 - Multimodal Detection: how can we improve AI detection for images, video, and audio?

 - Effects of AI-Generated Data on LLM Training: what is the effect of AI-generated data on foundation model training?

 - Agentic AI detection: how can we harness the power of agents to give Pangram more context about authorship?

 - Topics of your choice: propose an original topic relevant to AI detection



Qualifications:

You are a great fit for this internship if you: 

 - Are currently pursuing an M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science/Artificial Intelligence. Exceptional undergraduates entering their senior year are welcome to apply.

 - Have prior research experience that has resulted in a published paper in a top AI venue.

 - Have fluency in deep learning fundamentals and experience training neural networks.

 - Have excellent programming skills in Python and a deep learning framework like Pytorch.

 - Have experience working with an AI agent for research like Claude Code or Codex.



Compensation

 - $8,000-$11,000 per month

 - Relocation stipend available

 - In-office lunch

 - Top interns may receive return offers for full-time roles

ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Research Scientist Intern at Mercor, you’ll work on research at the frontier of post-training, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), data generation, and model evaluation.

You’ll investigate how datasets, rewards, and training methods affect the capabilities and behavior of large language models. This may include designing controlled experiments, developing new evaluation methodologies, conducting systematic failure analysis, and testing approaches to improve tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning.

You’ll work closely with research scientists, research engineers, and domain experts to turn open-ended questions into rigorous experiments. Your work will contribute to Mercor’s research agenda and may support external publications, benchmark releases, and the development of frontier AI systems.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Develop and investigate research questions related to post-training, RLVR, data quality, and model evaluation.

 - Design and run controlled experiments to understand how datasets, rewards, and training strategies affect model performance.

 - Study reward-shaping and post-training methods, including approaches such as GRPO and DAPO.

 - Develop methods for measuring data quality, usability, and performance uplift on key benchmarks.

 - Design and evaluate datasets, rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks for complex model capabilities.

 - Conduct systematic error analysis to identify model failure modes and opportunities for improvement.

 - Analyze experimental results and communicate findings through clear reports, research artifacts, and presentations.

 - Build the research tooling and data pipelines needed to conduct experiments at scale.

 - Collaborate with research scientists, research engineers, applied AI teams, and domain experts producing training and evaluation data.

 - Contribute to research publications, benchmark releases, and other public research outputs where appropriate.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing a master’s or PhD in computer science, machine learning, statistics, mathematics, or another relevant field.

 - Demonstrated ability to formulate research questions, design experiments, and draw sound conclusions from empirical results.

 - Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following:
   
   - Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models.
   
   - Agentic AI system, RL environments
   
   - Developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures.

 - At least one publication or open source project.

 - Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and the ability to write reliable research code.

 - Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals, experimental design, and statistical analysis.

 - Intellectual curiosity.

 - Comfort operating in a fast-paced research environment with rapid iteration and a high degree of ownership.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Previous research experience in language models, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, or post-training.

 - Experience training, fine-tuning, or evaluating language models.

 - Familiarity with RLVR techniques, reward modeling, or agentic AI systems.

 - Experience developing benchmarks, evaluation methodologies, or data-quality measures.

 - Research publications or submissions at competitive CS conferences such as ACL, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or EMNLP.

 - Research papers, technical reports, open-source projects, or other work samples demonstrating relevant skills.



Why Mercor

Impact: Your work powers how AI labs train and deploy their models

Learning: Get early exposure to frontier AI research and engineering

Growth: Work with a high-velocity team where interns ship to production

Benefits

 - Mentorship from experienced researchers.

 - Work on real, high-impact projects.

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

 - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

 - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

 - Free Equinox membership

 - Team events and offsites.

Who we are
Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.
We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
What you’ll do
As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will work alongside senior hardware engineers to help expand our autonomous transport platforms. You will get hands-on experience designing, testing, and integrating real-world hardware solutions for next-generation, on-road autonomous vehicles.
- PCB & Carrier Board Design: Support the design and revision of custom circuit boards and carrier boards for vehicle compute, sensors (camera, radar, lidar), GPS, and actuation systems.
- Vehicle & Protocol Integration: Assist with analyzing and debugging automotive communication protocols (CAN, CAN FD, Ethernet) on real vehicle test platforms.
- Hardware Validation & Testing: Help design, assemble, and execute test procedures and hardware test fixtures to validate board designs and troubleshoot edge cases.
- Fleet Support: Work directly with hardware and software engineers on vehicle bring-up, fleet installations, and physical hardware troubleshooting on-site.
What we’re looking for
- Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.
- Core Technical Knowledge: Solid foundation in circuit design, analog/digital fundamentals, and basic embedded systems logic.
- Hands-on Experience: Practical experience with PCB design tools (e.g., Altium, KiCad, Eagle) and bench equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers) through lab work, student design teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Robotics Club), or personal projects.
- Protocols & Hardware: Familiarity or coursework covering common hardware communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART).
- Mindset: Proactive problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced, highly collaborative startup environment and is excited to work with physical hardware.
Why join us
At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.
What else you need to know
This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.
Program Dates: Our internship is a 12-weeks program. Cohort sessions run as follows:
- Winter 2027: January – April
- Summer 2027: Late May – September
The base salary range for this role is $50.00 per hour.
Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Who we are
Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.
We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
What you’ll do
As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will work alongside senior hardware engineers to help expand our autonomous transport platforms. You will get hands-on experience designing, testing, and integrating real-world hardware solutions for next-generation, on-road autonomous vehicles.
- PCB & Carrier Board Design: Support the design and revision of custom circuit boards and carrier boards for vehicle compute, sensors (camera, radar, lidar), GPS, and actuation systems.
- Vehicle & Protocol Integration: Assist with analyzing and debugging automotive communication protocols (CAN, CAN FD, Ethernet) on real vehicle test platforms.
- Hardware Validation & Testing: Help design, assemble, and execute test procedures and hardware test fixtures to validate board designs and troubleshoot edge cases.
- Fleet Support: Work directly with hardware and software engineers on vehicle bring-up, fleet installations, and physical hardware troubleshooting on-site.
What we’re looking for
- Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.
- Core Technical Knowledge: Solid foundation in circuit design, analog/digital fundamentals, and basic embedded systems logic.
- Hands-on Experience: Practical experience with PCB design tools (e.g., Altium, KiCad, Eagle) and bench equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers) through lab work, student design teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Robotics Club), or personal projects.
- Protocols & Hardware: Familiarity or coursework covering common hardware communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART).
- Mindset: Proactive problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced, highly collaborative startup environment and is excited to work with physical hardware.
Why join us
At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.
What else you need to know
This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

- Winter 2027: January – April
- Summer 2027: Late May – September
The base salary range for this role is $50.00 per hour.
Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

NVIDIA is searching for an outstanding PhD intern working on efficient deep learning to join the Deep Learning Efficiency Research (DLER) team. We are passionate about research that pushes boundaries but also has impact in the real world. The team has two core focuses: (1) efficient diffusion language models and multimodal generative models, and (2) efficient agentic AI with hybrid inference orchestration across cloud and edge. We are also excited about post-training model optimization (pruning, quantization, NAS), efficient architecture design, adaptive/dynamic inference, and resource-efficient training and finetuning.
You will work within an amazing and collaborative research team that consistently publishes at the top venues in computer vision and machine learning. Our existing expertise includes computer vision, deep learning, generative models, diffusion LLMs, multimodal models, and hybrid cloud–edge agentic systems. Your contributions have the chance to create real impact on our products.
What you'll be doing:
- Research, design, and implement novel methods for efficient deep learning in one or both of the team’s focus areas:
- Diffusion LLMs and multimodal models — sampling efficiency, adaptive unmasking, self-speculation / parallel decoding, training and distillation pipelines, and multimodal generation.
- Efficient agentic AI — hybrid inference orchestration across cloud and edge, routing and scheduling policies, on-device vs. cloud expert delegation, and resource-aware agent loops.
- Publish original research.
- Collaborate with other team members and teams.
- Work with product groups to transfer technology.
- Collaborate with external researchers.
What we need to see:
- Pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science/Engineering, Electrical Engineering, etc.
- Excellent knowledge of theory and practice of machine learning and deep learning.
- Experience with large language models, diffusion language models, multimodal / vision-language models, or agentic systems is required.
- Hands-on experience with large-scale model training including data preparation and model parallelization (tensor and pipeline) is required.
- Outstanding research track record with at least one top-tier conference (ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, CVPR, ICCV, etc.).
- Excellent communication skills.
Ways to stand out from the crowd:
- Parallel programming (e.g., CUDA).
- Interest or experience in hybrid cloud–edge inference, orchestration, or adaptive routing.
- Background in pruning, quantization, NAS, or efficient backbones.

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
Overview: Before a single transistor gets placed, someone has to decide what the chip should actually be and ensure it functions to specs. This team makes those calls including System on a Chip (SoC) -level architecture, fabric/interconnect design, verification and not just core compute.
What you might work on: This posting spans multiple teams within Hardware Architecture & AI Hardware and SoC . One application, one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team and location that fits best. What each team does:
- Architecture: We define and evaluate the system, CPU, memory, fabric, and chiplet-level decisions that shape future products. We analyze workloads, performance, power, and system requirements, develop architectural models, do tradeoff analyses, and specifications for implementation.
- AI Hardware: We design and develop the core AI accelerator IP, including compute, data movement, and other specialized hardware blocks that enable high-performance AI workloads. We take these IPs from requirements through RTL design, verification, and delivery for SoC integration.
- SOC : Our team is where everything comes together. We design and verify the integration of all subsystems and the final pieces that allow the chip to interact with the outside world; scaleout, memory and on-chip system management and security. We validate cross functional and performance requirements, and ultimately take the design to silicon.
Who You Are
- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, ECE, CE, or CS.
- Coursework or projects in digital design, computer architecture and performance modeling.
- Self-starter who brings sound judgment and practical problem-solving to every project with a solid interest in AI and hardware, along with the ability to take ownership and deliver results.
What We Need
- Familiarity with ASIC design concepts, ranging from performance simulations, RTL design / verification, and logic synthesis / timing analysis
- Scripting & programming skills (example: Python, PERL, tcl, C/C++); with experience using AI coding platforms
- [Architecture] Experience with architectural simulators.
- Exposure to RISC-V or other open ISAs is nice to have.
- FPGA design experience is nice to have.
What You Will Learn
- Taking designs from specification to RTL to verification, and learning the qualification checks and tools needed to do so.
- How architectural tradeoffs (Architecture: Compute vs. memory vs. interconnect. AI HW/ SOC: Power, Performance & Area) get decided with data, not intuition.
- Best practices for cross-functional collaboration, seeing firsthand how Architecture, RTL, Software, and Physical Design teams stay aligned through implementation.
- Practical methods to integrate AI tools directly into your daily technical workflow.
- [Architecture] Performance modeling methodology used before RTL existed.

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
Overview: Before a single transistor gets placed, someone has to decide what the chip should actually be and ensure it functions to specs. This team makes those calls including System on a Chip (SoC) -level architecture, fabric/interconnect design, verification and not just core compute.
What you might work on: This posting spans multiple teams within Hardware Architecture & AI Hardware and SoC . One application, one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team and location that fits best. What each team does:
- Architecture: We define and evaluate the system, CPU, memory, fabric, and chiplet-level decisions that shape future products. We analyze workloads, performance, power, and system requirements, develop architectural models, do tradeoff analyses, and specifications for implementation.
- AI Hardware: We design and develop the core AI accelerator IP, including compute, data movement, and other specialized hardware blocks that enable high-performance AI workloads. We take these IPs from requirements through RTL design, verification, and delivery for SoC integration.
- SOC : Our team is where everything comes together. We design and verify the integration of all subsystems and the final pieces that allow the chip to interact with the outside world; scaleout, memory and on-chip system management and security. We validate cross functional and performance requirements, and ultimately take the design to silicon.
This role is on-site, based out of Boston, MA or Austin, TX or Fort Collins, CO or Santa Clara, CA.
Who You Are
- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, ECE, CE, or CS.
- Coursework or projects in digital design, computer architecture and performance modeling.
- Self-starter who brings sound judgment and practical problem-solving to every project with a solid interest in AI and hardware, along with the ability to take ownership and deliver results.
What We Need
- Familiarity with ASIC design concepts, ranging from performance simulations, RTL design / verification, and logic synthesis / timing analysis
- Scripting & programming skills (example: Python, PERL, tcl, C/C++); with experience using AI coding platforms
- [Architecture] Experience with architectural simulators.
- Exposure to RISC-V or other open ISAs is nice to have.
- FPGA design experience is nice to have.
What You Will Learn
- Taking designs from specification to RTL to verification, and learning the qualification checks and tools needed to do so.
- How architectural tradeoffs (Architecture: Compute vs. memory vs. interconnect. AI HW/ SOC: Power, Performance & Area) get decided with data, not intuition.
- Best practices for cross-functional collaboration, seeing firsthand how Architecture, RTL, Software, and Physical Design teams stay aligned through implementation.
- Practical methods to integrate AI tools directly into your daily technical workflow.
- [Architecture] Performance modeling methodology used before RTL existed.
USA Hiring Timelines
This internship opportunity is available throughout our 3 terms with the following corresponding recruitment cycles:
- Winter Term: Jan–Apr work term, Sept–Dec recruit.
- Summer Term: May–Aug work term, Oct–Apr recruit.
- Fall Term: Sept–Dec work term, Jan–Aug recruit.
Please note these timelines are for reference only. Actual timelines may vary.
Compensation for all interns at Tenstorrent ranges from $50/hr - $70/hr including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.
Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.
This offer of employment is contingent upon the applicant being eligible to access U.S. export-controlled technology. Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2). These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S. As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency. Position Overview
As a PhD Research intern in Autodesk Research’s AI Lab, you will explore and apply advanced machine learning techniques to empower our customers in designing and building a better, safer, and more sustainable world. We are a team of researchers, engineers, and industry domain experts working on projects that range from learning-based design systems, computer vision, graphics, robotics, human-computer interaction, sustainability, simulation, manufacturing, architectural design and construction.
We are seeking a research intern to join our research team focused on machine learning and generative methods for content creation in the media and entertainment space . In this role, you will conduct research on novel methods for character animation and related problems at the intersection of machine learning and computer graphics. Potential research directions include generative motion models, controllable character animation, data-efficient learning and adaptation, representation learning, and learning approaches that incorporate physics or simulation. The goal of this research is to enable more intuitive use of our animation tools by automating repetitive tasks.
Autodesk's AI Lab is actively engaged in the broader research community, targeting publications at top-tier conferences such as CVPR, NeurIPS, ICML, SIGGRAPH, and ICLR. We collaborate with top academic & industry labs, combining the best of an academic environment with product-driven research.
Minimum Qualifications
- Full-time student pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Graphics, Computational Physics, Machine Learning or a discipline in an accredited program
- Broad understanding of machine learning and deep learning
- Excellent Programming and software development skills, with experience in Python
- Proficient with ML & DL platforms & libraries (PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras, ONNX/Runtime, scikit-learn, etc.)
- Experience conducting research and publishing results
- An excellent communicator and team player
Preferred Qualifications
- Deep expertise in one or more areas such as computer graphics, character animation, motion generation, 2D/3D geometry representation learning, generative models, and unsupervised/self-supervised learning
- Experience with differentiable physics, data-driven computational physics, solver-driven learning (physics-in-the-loop), physics-informed models
- Experience with transfer learning, fine-tuning, few-shot learning, or other data-efficient learning methods is a plus
- Bonus: experience with physics real-time engines (such as Bullet, Unreal, or PhysX)
- Bonus: experience with modeling tools (such as Maya, Houdini, or Blender)
Responsibilities
- Conduct research on machine learning methods for character animation and related problems in media and entertainment
- Formulate research questions, conduct literature reviews, and design experiments to investigate them
- Build prototypes to test and explore concepts
- Evaluate research findings and prototypes to make recommendations for impacting business and products
- Author a full research paper
- Present the results of your research externally and internally

About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across voice, email, and enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z and Base10 with over $200M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments - where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Product Engineer Intern to build internal applications and AI agents to accelerate operations across product, engineering, deployments, and GTM. We build AI workforces for our customers, and this role is about building them for ourselves. You'll ship real software that people at HappyRobot use every day, with mentorship from a strong engineering team.

You'll work directly with the CTO and Head of Product, and your users will be your experts across Product, Engineering, Deployments, Go-To-Market, and Operations. Instead of tracking down inefficiencies by hand, you'll build the tools and agents that remove them: cross-functional agentic workflows, data pipelines, integrations, all the way up to autonomous agents that run entire work-streams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Build internal agents to automate operational work-streams: Design, deploy, and monitor AI agents that take over recurring work end to end.

 - Build internal applications: Design, build, and ship apps that streamline how teams work, such as deployment tracking, release and feature-enablement workflows, field feedback intake, and labeling operations management.

 - GTM & Commercial Enablement: Partner with GTM to drive technical enablement, support Product-Led Sales (PLS) motions, and refine feature pricing structures. You ensure the commercial side understands the technical reality and value of what we are shipping.

Who You Are

 - A Technical Operator: You possess a rare mix of technical literacy (you understand APIs, data structures, and engineering constraints) and operational rigor. You don't just identify broken processes; you fix them.

 - User-obsessed: You enjoy talking to the people who will use your tools, understanding their pain, and iterating until it's actually better.

 - Disciplined and systems-oriented: You find satisfaction in order. You are the person who creates the documentation, builds the dashboard, and sets up the automation that prevents future fires.

 - A self-starter: You don't need a perfectly defined path. You need a goal, and you'll figure out the rest.

Requirements

 - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program (or recently graduated) in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field.

 - Strong analytical & technical aptitude – be able to solve problems with technology.

 - Experience working in a multi-stakeholder environment, specifically interfacing between Engineering and Commercial/Field teams.

 - Ability to balance "big picture" strategic work (pricing, analysis) with "in the weeds" execution (data labeling coordination for RLHF, deployment coordination).

Why Join Us?

 - Real ownership of production tools and agents with real users.

 - A view into deployments, GTM, and operations that most engineers never get.

 - Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

 - Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

 - Ownership and autonomy over projects, and encouragement to ship.

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

 

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

 

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

 

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

 

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

 

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

Application Deadline: November 13, 2026

(You must be available to work full-time, in-office during this period.)
About Our Internship Program:
Dow Jones Internship Program is a 10-week summer experience designed to give students real exposure to how . Our interns work on meaningful projects alongside our teams, gaining hands-on skills that make an impact on the business.
We believe the best way to learn is by doing — that’s why you’ll be paired with a mentor, connected with senior leaders, and included in professional development sessions. You’ll also join a diverse global intern community, sharing experiences and building networks that last beyond the program.

About the Role:
You will work as part of a global team that is responsible for strategic, long-term market forecasts for the chemical industry. You will support updates of chemical product supply/demand data and integrated long-term projections using advanced analytics and models, and related publications. Specific responsibilities include data management, participation in the development of new commercial products and product enhancements, and projects to help improve data quality and process efficiencies. You will be part of a core global team and also work with our international product experts.
This role is hybrid, based in our Houston, TX office.
You Will:
- Participate in data and content updates and publications together with global team members
- Provide support in gathering and auditing of input and output data
- Help with the creation and set up of internal models and client deliverables
You Have:
- Completed at least two years toward a Bachelor’s degree, preferably in chemical engineering, chemistry, or related field
- Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint)
- Fluency in English, written and spoken at a business level
- Experience in Python or familiarity with other languages/ tools like R, SQL and MongoDB, desired.
Program Eligibility:
Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program
Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)
Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying.

Dow Jones is a global provider of news and business information, delivering content to consumers and organizations around the world across multiple formats, including print, digital, mobile and live events. To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Broadband Plasma (BBP) division is the market-leading optical inspection system used by logic, foundry, and memory customers to detect critical defects at advanced nodes. These tools combine broadband plasma technology with unmatched sensitivity and speed to support high-volume manufacturing.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
The right candidate will be dynamic, upbeat individual who is very passionate about delivering rich and powerful solutions that drive meaningful decisions, quality, and significant improvement in business results. Work together with GPG business functions such as Applications, Algorithm and S/W teams to perform proof of study with an end goal of attempting to improve existing methodologies
- Interact with team members to thoroughly understand current methods and collaborate with a cross-functional team to study a different methodology
- Proof of concept of new methodology with existing data
- Determine correlations with existing data sets on a variety of different system configurations
Requirements:
- Creative thinker with good problem-solving abilities
- Working with large data sets
- Excellent proficiency of data analysis techniques in Excel or other plotting S/Ws such as JMP or Origin
- Proficiency in Python, and/or MATLAB applications
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Motivated to learn new skills independently.
- Be willing to travel 50% - 70% if chosen for a full time role in the future
Desired Requirements:
Knowledge of semiconductor process or any relevant course work or previous internships in the semiconductor industry
Minimum Qualifications
Pursuing a Bachelors, Master’s or PhD degree in Physics, Mathematics, Material Science or Engineering
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Total Rewards
Base Pay Range: $35.00 - $47.00 per hour based on pursuit of a Master’s
Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA
KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave.
