About Didi Autonomous Driving
Founded in 2016, DiDi's autonomous driving unit is dedicated to developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology to make transportation safer, more efficient, and accessible. In 2019, the unit became an independent company, Voyager, to accelerate technology development, commercialization, and large-scale deployment. By combining DiDi's unique data advantage, operational expertise, and mobility ecosystem, we aim to build a reliable, scalable autonomous fleet that integrates seamlessly with human-driven services. Driven by real-world customer needs and a strong commitment to safety and user experience , our mission is to deliver autonomous mobility solutions that create meaningful value for riders and communities.
About the Role
We want our vehicles to understand the physical world as it is right now, instead of relying on a map drawn long ago. Roads change, and the world a car actually drives in is always more complex than any static record of it. We are seeking a Research Intern to help give our planner a m ore accurate and up-to-date picture of the world, so the vehicle handles complex real-world scenes more robustly. In this role, you will take on hard, open problems from real-world driving and solve them with frontier research methods. You will report directly to the team lead and work on the problem from definition to validated solution. Strong results will often be worth publishing, and we will support you in writing them up, but the goal is to solve problems that matter to the product.
Responsibilities
-
Survey the latest research in scene understanding, prediction, and planning, and turn it into practical approaches that fit our system and constraints.
-
Design and implement deep learning models that build a richer, real-time understanding of the driving environment from onboard sensors and other available sources.
-
Train and evaluate models on large-scale data from our driving logs and on public benchmarks, and lead failure analysis to find out where and why models fall short.
-
Define metrics and evaluation methods that connect perception quality to how the vehicle actually drives.
-
Turn successful prototypes into solutions that work with our planning stack, with help from production engineers.
-
Collaborate with Perception, Prediction, Planning, and Mapping teams so results move from experiment to product.
Qualifications
-
Currently enrolled in an M.S. or Ph.D. program in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, for the full duration of the internship.
-
Available for a full-time onsite internship of 3–6 months; start dates are flexible.
-
Strong programming skills in Python, and experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
-
Hands-on experience designing, training, and debugging deep learning models for computer vision, 3D perception, or sequential decision-making.
-
Solid understanding of autonomous driving fundamentals, including perception, prediction, and motion planning.
-
Ability to read research critically, form hypotheses, and turn them into well-controlled experiments.
-
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications
-
Publications at top venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, IROS, CoRL or IV.
-
Experience with multi-modal sensor fusion (camera, lidar, radar) or BEV representations.
-
Experience with transformers, graph neural networks, or other structured scene representations.
-
Experience with uncertainty estimation, or with learning-based prediction or planning.
-
Experience with large-scale model training and data pipelines.
-
Experience with public autonomous driving datasets such as nuScenes, Argoverse 2, or the Waymo Open Dataset.
-
Proficiency in C++ (CUDA is a plus) and experience with robotics systems.
The hourly rate for the Intern position in the selected city is $46.

SpAItial is pioneering the next generation of World Models, pushing the boundaries of generative AI, computer vision, and the simulation of reality. We are moving beyond 2D pixels to build models that natively understand the physics and geometry of our world. Our mission is to redefine how industries, from robotics and AR/VR to gaming and cinema, generate and interact with physically-grounded 3D environments.

 

We're looking for bold, innovative individuals driven by a passion for pushing the boundaries of generative 3D AI. You should thrive in an environment where creativity meets technical challenge and be fearless in tackling the hardest problems in 3D world modeling. Our team is built on a foundation of dedication and a shared commitment to excellence, so we value people who take immense pride in their work and place the collective goals of the team above personal ambition. As a part of SpAItial, you'll be at the forefront of building World Models that bridge generative AI and the physical world. If you're ready to make an impact, embrace the unknown, and collaborate with a talented group of visionaries, we want to hear from you.

 

We're seeking PhD Research Interns to work with our research team on open problems in 3D generation and reconstruction. You should have strong knowledge of at least one of our core areas, such as generative video and diffusion models, scene representations like Gaussian splats and radiance fields, or 3D reconstruction from per-scene optimization to feed-forward models. Over a 5-7 month internship, you will own a well-defined research question with the goal of publishing a paper. 

 

Responsibilities

 - You will explore novel research directions in 3D generation, reconstruction, and world models. 

 - You will design, implement, and evaluate state-of-the-art methods, turning innovative research ideas into working systems and prototypes. 

 - You will be working closely with our research team.

 -  You will also present your findings and contribute to scientific publications targeting leading conferences in computer vision, computer graphics, and machine learning, such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, and ICLR.

Key Qualifications

 - Currently enrolled in the third year or beyond of a PhD in computer science, computer vision, computer graphics, machine learning, or a related field.

 - 2-3 first-author papers at top-tier conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or ICLR.

 - Knowledge of at least one of: generative models (diffusion or video models), neural scene representations, or 3D reconstruction.

 

At SpAItial, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and ensure all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.

The Internship Programme at Graphcore
Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.
What you’ll work on
Put your programming skills to work exploring how firmware brings AI hardware to life, from first boot to system monitoring.
As a Firmware Engineering Intern, you’ll contribute to firmware for Graphcore’s next-generation products. Working closely to with our silicon and hardware teams, you’ll contribute to software that supports hardware bootup and provides telemetry and monitoring data that helps data centre operators understand what the hardware is doing.
Your tasks could include writing code, develop unit tests and investigate behaviour on hardware using logs, oscilloscopes and logic analysers. You’ll contribute to a shared codebase and see how software decisions affect physical systems.
Your team and support
The Firmware team sits within System Software and works with teams across Graphcore and our partners. You’ll report to the Firmware Manager and work alongside engineers connecting silicon, hardware and software.

Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build practical experience in firmware development, unit testing and debugging through the work your tasks focus on.
Investigating issues on real hardware will help you connect software behaviour with physical signals and develop a methodical approach to finding problems. Code reviews will introduce you to shared development and coding standards and help you build confidence contributing to a team codebase, giving you a clearer view of a career in embedded software.
Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated.
What we’re looking for
- Currently studying towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Electronic Engineering, Maths or a related field. Equivalent experience is also welcome
- Introductory programming experience in C or Python, with some understanding of continuous integration, build systems and software packaging best practices
- A practical, methodical approach to problem solving, with the ability to organise your work and follow tasks through to completion
- Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to document complex system designs coherently
Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects, research or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.
Benefits
- Flexible working: Find a balance between your internship and life outside work
- 5 days of annual leave: Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship
- Life in the office: Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista
- Learning and development: Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. And just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives.
In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality, and redefining human hearing. See more about our work here: Inside Facebook Reality Labs Research: The future of audio and Filter Out the Noise With Conversation Focus. These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart, and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments.
Meta Reality Labs Research is looking for an intern who is passionate about speech perception and audio quality to investigate why processed speech sometimes sounds degraded or robotic. The project focuses on identifying systematic phonemic errors as causal factors in perceived quality degradation, and linking these errors to human quality and intelligibility judgments. A core method is to explore the capabilities of audio vs video LLMs. This is fundamentally a speech-perception research role; multimodal/LLM methods are a supporting tool rather than the central focus.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Metamorphic is developing new approaches to intelligence by combining machine learning with large-scale experimental neuroscience, informed by the principles that make the brain efficient, flexible, and robust. We are building foundation models trained on rich, continuous neural data — a high-resolution model of the brain at a scale never before possible.

Our founding team spans machine learning, neuroscience, and neurotechnology, with prior work including the MICrONS project https://www.nature.com/immersive/d42859-025-00001-w/index.html, Neuropixels http://neuropixels.org/, and the Enigma project https://www.enigmaproject.ai/, as well as foundational scientific contributions in learning, neural computation, and generative modeling. Our work sits at the frontier of AI research, and we believe the highest-impact discoveries will come from researchers and engineers working as a single, tightly collaborative team.

FSH Tech builds modern software that just works for the public sector. When we deliver, taxpayer dollars go further, agencies move faster, and millions of Americans get tangibly better service and quality of life.

Local governments, schools, libraries, and emergency services run on brittle software that was built decades ago. This results in wasted budgets, broken workflows, and bad outcomes for the public. We believe that the institutions closest to people's daily lives deserve products as good as anything in the private sector. We're building them.

We're a small, high-agency team. The people who do their best work here are:

About FSH Engineering

Our ideal candidate is an expert in their craft. They gain energy from understanding how their chosen tools work, and have used their tools to build software many times. Our ideal candidate is obsessively curious, motivated by customer outcomes, and is a technical artist.

We use Python, Postgres, Unix, TypeScript and React to build software. We maintain a set of internal tools to deterministically generate Python and Typescript. There is no predefined destination for this role and we don’t believe in having others do work we wouldn’t do ourselves (e.g. this isn’t a cover for ‘you will simply respond to tickets'). We want to help you ship customer value and will enable you to do so throughout your internship.

 - Iterate quickly

 

What You'll Need (optional)

You’re the right person for the job if many of these are true:

 - You believe programming is a creative pursuit

 - You are a perennial tinkerer

 - You gain energy from being close to the customer, always

 - You believe abstractions can simplify complexity

Job Details
About Salesforce
Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
The Experience
Salesforce AI Research is a global leader in Enterprise AI, driving innovations that advance the state of AI while powering enterprise products at worldwide scale.
Our research has helped shape multiple generations of modern AI: we helped pioneer prompt engineering through DecaNLP; introduced BLIP, a foundational breakthrough in multimodal AI; trained state-of-the-art large language models including CodeGen; and pioneered foundation models for time series with Moirai. Today, we continue to advance the frontier of enterprise AI through innovations in AI simulation environments like eVerse, our simulation and agent-training environment; the Atlas Reasoning Engine, which powers Agentforce reasoning capabilities; and other AI systems that are redefining how enterprises reason, plan, and act.
What makes our team unique is our ability to take ideas from research to real-world impact at scale. We work closely with product teams and enterprise customers to translate cutting-edge research into production AI capabilities used by millions of users. We also continue to publish at the world's top AI conferences, open source influential research, and collaborate with leading academic institutions. Learn more at Salesforce AI Research .
We are looking for entrepreneurial Research Interns for Summer 2027 who want to help build the next generation of Enterprise AI. This is not a traditional research internship. You will work like a founder within Salesforce: exploring high-impact research directions, prototyping cutting-edge AI capabilities, and seeing how ideas are validated with customers and turned into production-ready solutions. You will have the freedom to propose and explore new ideas, alongside mentors and research scientists, with access to Salesforce's global customer and product ecosystem. We are looking for people who are comfortable with ambiguity, bring energy and focus to their work, and care as much about customer adoption as technical innovation. If you want the pace and ownership of a startup, combined with the reach and resources of Salesforce, this internship offers a unique opportunity to do research with global impact.
What You'll Actually Be Doing
- Collaborate with research scientists and engineers on a project focused on real-world product impact, with the opportunity to publish your work at top-tier conferences.
- Explore research directions with the potential to transform Enterprise AI.
- Help turn promising ideas into zero-to-one AI product prototypes.
- Build models, agents, and AI systems for real-world enterprise use.
- Learn how research partners with product, engineering, and go-to-market teams to bring solutions to market.
You're Our Person If...
- You have a strong publication record at top AI venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ACL, EMNLP) and/or experience building AI research into real-world systems.
- You have experience with Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or DeepSpeed.
- You are motivated by real-world impact and care about seeing your research leave the lab and reach users at scale.
- You bring expertise in one or more core focus areas:
- Agentic AI and Reasoning: LLM-powered agents, reinforcement learning (RL), reasoning and planning, autonomous workflows, computer use agents, deep research agents, and coding agents.
- Multimodal and Computer Vision: Vision-language models, video understanding, and multimodal AI agents.
- Speech Intelligence: Voice intelligence, text-to-speech/automatic speech recognition, and low-latency audio processing.
- Core Modeling and Post-Training: Pre-training and post-training techniques including RLHF and direct preference optimization, model distillation, evaluation, and time series modeling.
- You can conduct research with guidance from mentors, and you are ready to grow toward independence and translate ideas into impactful systems.
Even Better If...
- You are a PhD or MS candidate in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical field.
- You have experience building and scaling ML models for real-world applications.
- You have strong programming skills (competitive programming, e.g., ACM-ICPC, or open source experience).
- You are thoughtful about responsible AI, trust, and the real-world impact of the systems you build.
- You are a fantastic problem solver, able to tackle challenges the world hasn't solved before.
- You have excellent written and spoken communication skills.
- You collaborate effectively with teammates.

This is a Summer 2027 internship with a minimum duration of 12 weeks.

PROGRAM OVERVIEW

The ClickHouse PhD Research Internship Program offers doctoral students the opportunity to pursue ambitious research alongside ClickHouse Labs researchers and engineers working on some of the most interesting challenges in databases, systems, and data infrastructure.

Research interns join ClickHouse Labs for approximately 10-12 weeks to explore meaningful research questions, develop new ideas, and investigate technologies that have the potential to advance both the broader research community and the future of ClickHouse.

The program is intentionally designed around research collaboration. Interns are paired with experienced researchers and have the opportunity to pursue work that aligns with their academic interests, ongoing research, and areas of interest within ClickHouse Labs. In some cases, an internship may build on research, a prototype, or a system the student has already begun exploring at their university.

We believe the strongest research relationships extend beyond a single summer. Interns may continue their work after returning to their university through academic research, open-source contributions, publications, or other forms of collaboration. Where there is a strong mutual fit, an internship may become the beginning of a longer-term relationship between the researcher, ClickHouse Labs, and the broader academic community.

During their internship, researchers will have the opportunity to work closely with ClickHouse Labs, engage with ClickHouse's open-source technology and engineering community, share their findings, and contribute to the intellectual life of the broader research community.

Program length: 10-12 weeks, with flexibility based on academic calendars and research needs

Typical timing: Summer, beginning approximately June 1

Locations: Opportunities available across the US and Europe, subject to role and employment requirements. Remote first.

Research environment: ClickHouse Labs

Internship format: Research-focused, mentor-supported, and shaped around areas of mutual research interest

Compensation: commensurate with experience, a monthly stipend will be paid




RESEARCH AT CLICKHOUSE LABS

ClickHouse Labs explores ambitious ideas at the intersection of databases, distributed systems, data infrastructure, and the broader systems research community.

We believe some of the most interesting advances in these areas happen through close collaboration between industry and academia. ClickHouse Labs brings together researchers and engineers to explore new ideas, investigate challenging technical problems, and connect academic research with real-world systems at scale.

Research interns are an important part of that community. Interns have the opportunity to bring their own research interests and perspectives into ClickHouse Labs while working alongside researchers and engineers who are deeply engaged with both the practical challenges and open research questions shaping the future of data systems.




PROGRAM GOALS

 1. Identify exceptional PhD researchers working in areas directly relevant to ClickHouse.

 2. Give researchers the opportunity to work on meaningful, open-ended problems with ClickHouse Labs.

 3. Build long-term relationships with researchers and academic institutions.

 4. Encourage continued research and open-source contributions after the internship.

 5. Create opportunities for co-authored papers, thesis advising, or other academic collaboration.

 6. Increase ClickHouse's visibility within the database and systems research community.

 7. Publish and share meaningful research outcomes through the ClickHouse website and other appropriate channels.


WHAT MAKES THE PROGRAM DIFFERENT

This is intentionally not a highly structured engineering internship and should not detailed planning. ****But the high-level problem area and expectations should defined several months before the internship begins. This flexibility is intentional and allows ClickHouse Labs to respond to:

 - Emerging research questions

 - Current ClickHouse priorities

 - New academic research

 - Interesting systems or database prototypes

 - Work candidates have already completed

 - Opportunities to apply new research ideas to ClickHouse

The goal is to identify researchers whose work is already closely aligned with areas ClickHouse cares about and then determine the most valuable research problem to pursue together.




CANDIDATE PROFILE

We are looking for exceptional PhD students conducting research directly relevant to ClickHouse and the broader database/systems space.




IDEAL CANDIDATES

 - Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science or a closely related field

 - Conducting research in areas relevant to ClickHouse

 - Demonstrated research excellence

 - Strong database systems, distributed systems, hardware, or related technical background

 - Has demonstrated ability to independently pursue complex research questions

 - Ideally has prior experience with ClickHouse open source but not required**.**

 - Has research, prototypes, or publications that could translate into meaningful work with ClickHouse

 - Interested in continuing research beyond the internship

 - Potential interest in open-source contribution and academic collaboration


CANDIDATE SELECTION PHILOSOPHY

The strongest candidates will be researchers whose work is specifically relevant to what ClickHouse Labs wants to explore.

A candidate who has already:

 - Worked with ClickHouse

 - Built a relevant database or systems prototype

 - Published research in an area relevant to ClickHouse

 - Explored a technical problem ClickHouse is interested in

may be significantly more valuable than a candidate with an otherwise impressive academic profile but no meaningful connection to our research areas.




RESEARCH AREAS & PROJECT SCOPE

Unlike an engineering internship program, specific projects do not need to be defined when recruiting begins.

Research projects may emerge from:

 - A candidate's existing research

 - A recent academic paper

 - A prototype or system the candidate has developed

 - An emerging ClickHouse Labs research priority

 - An opportunity to test or extend an existing research concept within ClickHouse




IF THIS IS RELEVANT AND EXCITING TO YOU, PLEASE APPLY!


PERKS

 - Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

 - Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

 - Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

 - Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

 - A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

 - Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.


CULTURE - WE ALL SHAPE IT

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here https://clickhouse.com/company/careers. Check out our blog posts https://clickhouse.com/blog or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/clickhouseinc/life/0c1ee7f4-2129-488d-b413-e7f6270659fd/?viewAsMember=true to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & PRIVACY

ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Please see here https://clickhouse.com/legal/applicant-privacy-notice for our Privacy Statement.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our AI Search research team. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in how AI agents learn from their own experience — improving their search and reasoning workflows, retaining useful knowledge, and transferring those gains to unfamiliar tasks. A central research challenge is making repeated self-improvement reliable when feedback is sparse or noisy.
The intern will work in one of three directions, scoped closer to the start date together with the intern manager:
-Learning to improve research workflows — agents learn better search, tool-use and verification strategies from prior attempts by improving their harness: the workflow, memory, tools and feedback loop around the model. Topics include meta-learning across tasks, automated agent design, and learning from natural-language feedback.
-Persistent memory and continual learning — agents retain useful lessons and update knowledge across tasks, whether in context, in compressed memory, or in weights, without forgetting what they already know. Topics include long-context modeling, context compression, continual learning, and test-time training.
-Learning from imperfect feedback — turning noisy judgments and failed attempts into useful learning signals, and improving the strategy an agent uses to learn, including how it selects and evaluates its next improvement. Topics include reward learning, credit assignment, and learning to learn.
Across all three directions, the key test is whether improvements transfer to new tasks. The goal is to develop novel methods and experiments toward a first-author submission at a leading ML/NLP venue. Recent internships on this team have produced work such as REFRAG, a new architecture for retrieval-augmented generation.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.
Your Team, Your Impact
The Rack Scale Switch Chip Validation team validates and delivers the high-performance switching silicon and system-level solutions used inside modern AI and cloud data center racks. As an intern, you will contribute to day-to-day engineering work such as running emulation and verification tests, debugging silicon and hardware issues, troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency, and writing scripts to automate workflows, all alongside experienced engineers. Your work will support the team's efforts to deliver reliable, high-bandwidth, low-latency switch products that are a key part of Marvell's data infrastructure portfolio. These products help customers scale AI workloads and enable the next generation of data center networking.
What You Can Expect
Support post-silicon validation of high-speed switch silicon under the guidance of senior engineers.
· Assist in developing, documenting, and executing test plans and test cases for switch chip validation.
· Support lab-based silicon bring-up and run unit tests on hardware and firmware functionality, including emulation and verification environments.
· Help collect and analyze high-speed signal and link data (such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER) using lab test equipment.
· Assist in debugging silicon and hardware issues, and in troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency.
· Use diagnostics, software tools, oscilloscopes, and protocol analyzers to help isolate the root cause of failing tests.
· Write and maintain scripts (for example in Python) to automate test execution, data collection, and result reporting.
· Document test results, findings, and debug progress, and present them to the team.

· Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028

· Basic hands-on lab experience through coursework, research, or projects, such as hardware bring-up, testing, and debug.
· Familiarity with common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or BERTs.
· Programming or scripting experience in Python, Perl, or a similar language.
· Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with a willingness to learn.
Preferred/Plus:
· Coursework or project experience with PCIe, Ethernet, or other high-speed interfaces.
· Exposure to the physical and protocol layers of high-speed interfaces (for example PHY, PCS, MAC).
· Experience with emulation, simulation, or verification environments.
· Ability to read board schematics and layouts.
· Familiarity with signal integrity concepts such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER.

28 - 56, $ per hour.
The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

Future AR and VR devices occupy ever-smaller, glasses-like form factors and thus require ever-tighter power budgets. At the same time, we require higher-quality passthrough rendering and scene understanding. In particular, depth estimation, which reconstructs scene geometry in real time from sensor signals, is one of the biggest power consumers in AR and VR devices. However, most existing work targets datacenter GPUs, or at best mobile silicon with an order of magnitude more power headroom than what glasses form factors allow.
Reality Labs is Meta's innovation engine for next-generation AR/VR and wearable technology and XR Graphics is involved in building the next-generation imaging and reconstruction stack that closes this gap. We are looking for a Research Scientist Intern to work on low-power real-time reconstruction of scene geometry for AR/VR.
Today, VR passthrough, hand interaction, and environment understanding run on separate pipelines, each tuned for different accuracy, latency and power target. We are interested in deduplicating the compute (and thus reducing power):
- What is the right depth estimation and processing strategy, from the ground up, for a glasses power budget?
- Can we train a single lightweight scene representation that can serve passthrough, hand occlusions, and background occlusions simultaneously?
These are open questions, and you would help define the approach. This is a research internship. You will own a genuinely open problem, choose the methods, build the evaluation, and present your results, with support for publication where the work warrants it.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. Just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives.
In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality and redefining the human hearing.
These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments. The Devices and Hardware Research team of the Reality Labs Research Audio is looking for innovative PhD student interns interested in one or more of the following areas:
> Electrophysiological and bio-signal sensing technologies and the associated signal processing — EEG, EMG, EOG, ECG, PPG, EDA, and other wearable biopotential/physiological modalities, including electrode and front-end design, artifact rejection, and robust on-body signal quality.
> Extremely low-power, energy-autonomous wearable design — sub-milliwatt and duty-cycled sensing architectures, analog/mixed-signal front ends, event-driven and always-on wake-up circuits, and self-powered operation via energy harvesting.
> Embedded real-time signal processing on resource-constrained hardware — ANC, echo cancellation, hear-through, adaptive filtering, and efficient implementations on MCUs and DSPs.
> Hearing biomechanics characterized through experimentation and numerical simulation.
> Conventional and ML-based signal processing — feature extraction, classification, regression and event detection, sequence/temporal modeling, self-supervised and transfer learning for scarce physiological labels, subject-independent generalization and calibration, sensor fusion across modalities, and on-device/TinyML inference (quantization, pruning, distillation) under tight compute and energy budgets.
This internship can be twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks, with various start dates throughout the year.

About Tacit

We are an early-stage, deep tech startup based in San Francisco, developing innovative hardware that rethinks human-computer interaction. We are backed by General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, and Greylock Partners, with a founding team from Stanford, BrainGate, Oculus, and Tesla. While we can’t reveal too much just yet, our team is tackling cutting-edge engineering challenges to bring revolutionary products to life.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a System Electrical Engineer Intern to help validate, debug, and improve the electrical blocks in our sensing hardware. You'll work alongside our hardware engineers on real prototype boards: bringing them up on the bench, measuring how they perform, tracking down problems, and helping turn what you learn into the next design.

You'll take part in the product's journey from prototype to mass production, including bring-up, design updates, and testing. We hire interns on a rolling basis and are flexible on start date and timeline.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Help bring up prototype boards and get them ready for testing.

 - Run bench measurements on power rails, battery charging, sensor front ends, and digital interfaces, following validation plans and helping write new ones. Use oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, and multimeters to characterize how blocks perform.

 - Help debug hardware issues and narrow down root causes with the hardware team. Propose and implement small schematic and layout changes to improve performance, power, or board area.

 - Build and automate repeatable bench tests, and collect and analyze data across multiple boards.

 - Document results and present findings and recommendations to the team.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

 - Solid grasp of EE fundamentals: circuit analysis, analog and digital electronics, and power basics

 - Hands-on experience with lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, and power supplies, from coursework, projects, or prior internships.

 - Experience designing or debugging a circuit board, in class, in a club, or on your own.

 - Curiosity and persistence when tracking down why something isn't working. Clear communication and good documentation habits.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY HAVE

 - PCB design experience in Altium or a similar tool.

 - Python for test automation or data analysis, or embedded C/C++.

 - Background in signal integrity and power integrity simulation.

 - Familiarity with RF circuits and components.

 - Exposure to mixed-signal, power, or battery-powered designs.

 - Experience with high-speed or communication interfaces such as USB, SPI, or I2C. Independent work ethic, flexibility, and resourcefulness.

 - Comfort in a fast-moving startup, and excitement to build independently.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
SCOPE OF WORK :
The Development Data and Research Intern will support IRC Silver Spring’s Development team by organizing program data, creating impact materials and conducting research to support fundraising efforts. The intern will analyze FY27 outcomes, research local benchmarks, coordinate with program teams to verify data and support donor prospecting and funding research.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Review and organize program data, tracking sheets and reports to identify key annual results and achievements.
- Create data summaries, program one-pagers and materials that show IRC Silver Spring’s impact for proposals.

- Work with program teams to collect program data updates, confirm information and ensure data accuracy.
- Maintain organized data files, templates and resources for fundraising and reporting.
- Research potential foundation, corporate and individual donors aligned with IRC Silver Spring programs.

- Support proposal development, reporting and other Development team projects as needed.

Job Description
Ready to fuel the success of globally renowned brands like Gillette? Do you want to be part of the innovation and technological advancement of products used every day by millions of the world’s consumers? Want to work for a company consistently recognised as one of the UK’s leading graduate employers?
We are offering summer internship opportunities in July 2027 at our Reading Innovation Centre . This specific role is focused on Master Data and Digital Transformation.
About our Reading Innovation Centre
This role is available in our Reading Innovation Centre which is home to over 200+ scientists and engineers responsible for innovating consumer products in several business areas including Personal Health Care (Vicks) Oral Care (Oral-B), Grooming (Gillette and Venus) and Beauty Care (Olay).
The site is a specialist Healthcare & Grooming Research & Development Hub in Europe and supports our European Beauty Franchise business. The site is friendly, diverse and has a rich history in innovation in multiple business areas.
Our site is located close to the town centre and is served by motorway networks of M4 and M25 as well as the A33. We’re within 20 mins of Reading Central and Green Park railway stations and are served by buses that run every 10 minutes.
What To Expect:
Research and Development (R&D) at P&G will help you to discover the essence behind crafting some of the world's most renowned brands. Delve into a realm where science takes centre stage. Some of the best scientists in the world go to work making our products just right for the billions of consumers who use them. We're talking cutting edge technology, "hands-on" labs and pilot plants, 41,000+ active patents and a team full of inventors.
During your summer internship, you will get a first-hand experience of what a career in R&D with P&G involves, and if it is right for you. You will be working on live business R&D projects and expected to dive straight in and take the lead. Each intern receives a customized learning plan to ensure they get the right levels of coaching, mentoring, and training as they deliver their work. If you are looking for an exciting and challenging experience, have a passion for winning, strong leadership credentials and an interest in pursuing a career at P&G – this internship is for you!
What You Will Gain:
- Responsibilities and Real Work from Day 1: You will be given specific projects and responsibilities working on real and live business challenges, just like a true P&Ger.
- Continuous training & coaching: You will work with passionate people and receive both formal training as well as day-to-day mentoring from your manager.
- Competitive Compensation & Benefits: The monthly salary for this summer internship is £2,625. On top of this you’ll enjoy lots of benefits like the option to enroll in our pension, flexible working arrangements, and your very own ‘Flex4Me’ Fund which enables you to allocate a portion of your benefits package to the areas that matter most to you.
- Full Time Role: Successful interns have the potential to secure a full-time position with P&G after graduation. As a 'build from within' company, our people start at entry level and progress through the organization. When we make a job offer, it’s with the expectation that you will grow into one of our future leaders, and to help you get there, you will work closely with skilled P&G veterans for mentoring and coaching at every step.
Job Qualifications
What We Look For:
- University students pursuing a degree in a scientific or engineering discipline (please note the additional detail below on required knowledge) graduating in 2027 or 2028. We also welcome applications from those who have already graduated who are able to complete a summer internship.
- Evidence of passion and achievements in academic and/or non-academic activities. Tell us what you’re proud of – be it playing a musical instrument or holding down a job alongside your studies. We want to get to know you during your application!
- Demonstrated leadership skills and a strong passion for research and innovation.
- Strong verbal and written English language skills.
- Knowledge of at least one of the following (the candidate is not expected to be knowledgeable in every area): Python (Pandas, NumPy), SQL & data modeling, Data wrangling and ETL, Data visualization (Power BI/Tableau), Machine Learning fundamental, API integration, Generative AI & prompt engineering, AI application development, Workflow automation, Web application development (Streamlit/React/Flask), Cloud platforms (Azure preferred), Product thinking and user-centric design, System integration and APIs.
Start date:
The internship's duration is from July 5th, 2027, until September 24th, 2027.
Right to Work:
For our internship roles, you will need to provide your own right to work in the UK for the full duration of your internship without requiring sponsorship from P&G. Note, this will require your right to work permission to be valid between 5th July 2027 to 24th September 2027 for a minimum of 37.5 hours per week.
P&G is legally required to ensure all candidates have the right to work in the UK from Day 1 of their employment. All applicants will therefore be asked to provide evidence of their right to work at the conclusion of the recruitment process as a condition of employment.
Application Deadline:
1pm (GMT) December 2nd, 2026. You must apply by the deadline. We encourage you to apply and complete our online assessments as soon as possible , as we may close early if positions are filled.
Application Process:
- Complete your Application (Deadline 1pm GMT 2nd December 2026)
- Complete our Online Assessments (Deadline 1pm GMT 9th December 2026)
- Virtual Interviews (These will run from October until our roles are filled)
At P&G #weseeequal
We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. At P&G we strive to build a culture where everyone feels welcome, included, and able to bring their full selves to work.
We champion social mobility and believe socio-economic status should not be a barrier to accessing job opportunities. That’s why in addition to this internship being paid, we offer provision of all the necessary technology and electronic equipment, access to a range of benefits, and financial support if you need to relocate for your internship - such as covering the cost of travel to your internship location.
We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process. Please click here if you require an accommodation during the application process. Please make sure to wait to hear back from us regarding your accommodation before proceeding with the online assessment, we thank you in advance for your patience.

Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.
Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
Responsibilities
About the Job: You will join our team for a 3-month project in RF signal conditioning circuit design aimed at future products. You will get experience with the tools, skills, insights and tradeoffs necessary for successful integrated circuit design. Keysight fosters a collaborative engineering environment which emphasizes teamwork, mentoring, enthusiasm, and excellence in design
About the Team: Our Keysight Labs team develops (and often publishes) world’s-fastest amplifiers and other mixed-signal integrated circuits. Our chips provide the speed and accuracy performance that enable many of Keysight’s world-leading electronic test and measurement products.
Responsibilities: You will do design and simulation of RF blocks. Design may be at the block or circuit level, and simulation may include circuit simulation, electromagnetic simulation, and/or high-level custom software simulation.
Qualifications
- Enrolled in a MS or PhD EE program
- Strong skills in transistor-level design of mixed signal CMOS and/or BiCMOS circuits
- Familiar with schematic entry / layout / simulation tool flow (preferably Cadence)
- Familiar with the use of one or more software scripting tools to support design, such as Bash, Python, PERL, Awk or SKILL
- Familiarity with electromagnetic simulations such as HFSS, RF pro, EM pro, CST
Desired Qualifications:

About fab2

The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves.

We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible.

 

fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof https://www.youtube.com/@SamZeloof and Jim Keller https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Keller_(engineer). Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years.

 

About the Role

We're hiring Process Engineering Interns for the winter term. The internship begins in January, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. We’re rebuilding the chip fabrication process from the ground-up, so you’ll be exposed to some really interesting and impactful work. This is a hands-on process engineering role—you’ll be responsible for experiment design and execution of new semiconductor and thin-film fabrication methods. We're looking for someone with both a strong understanding of traditional semiconductor processing methods and an open-mindedness to new techniques. 



This is a high-ownership role with lots of autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment. You’ll have the opportunity to contribute to novel R&D processes and influence tool design. Candidates should have hands-on cleanroom experience and a track record of developing nanofabrication recipes from scratch, ideally across multiple process steps.

 

Responsibilities

 - Design and run experiments alongside senior process engineers

 - Read academic papers and technical literature to inform experimental design; whiteboard ideas and iterate quickly

 - Learn and operate a range of semiconductor tools, including deposition, etch, lithography, and metrology systems

 - Develop, transfer, and optimize process recipes across platforms with a focus on consistency, yield, and throughput

 - Analyze process data, troubleshoot recipe or equipment issues, and clearly document findings and results for the team

 

Required Experience

 - Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or higher in engineering

 - Ability to learn quickly and troubleshoot technical problems

 - Hands-on experience with wafer fabrication tools (etch, deposition, patterning) and metrology tools (AFM, SEM, thin film measurement, etc.)

 - Recipe development and optimization for some subset of thin film deposition, dry etch, or lithography.

 - Strong foundation in theoretical semiconductor knowledge (devices, fabrication, etc.)

 

Nice-to-have

 - Familiarity with data processing in Python

 - Mechanical or maintenance experience with fab tools

 

Working at fab2
We’re an early-stage hardware startup with solid funding, world-class advisors, and labs/offices in Austin, TX, Lockhart, TX, and San Francisco, CA. fab2 is committed to fair and equitable compensation. Process Interns are paid hourly, at a rate equivalent to on an annualized range of $108,000–$126,000 depending on experience and education. Actual earnings vary with hours worked.


Internship Benefits:

 - Housing Stipend to help with first month expenses

 - Lunches daily, Dinners 3x per week, Stocked Office Kitchen with Snacks and Spindrifts

 - Weekly Learning & Development opportunities

 - Commuter Benefits including Parking and Late Night Uber rides from the office

 - Paid Time Off inclusive of Holidays and Sick Time

 - Visa Sponsorship

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance

 - 401(k) retirement plan

 - Life and Disability Insurance



We are an equal-opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

Location

About Us
BorgWarner is a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions. We are a company of innovators and independent thinkers that brings together talented employees, meaningful work and amazing technology in a unique environment. At BorgWarner, we constantly work towards our vision of a clean and energy-efficient world.
Our Culture
BorgWarner promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive environment, honors integrity, strives for excellence, commits to responsibility for our communities and the environment, and builds on the power of collaboration. We believe the health and safety of our employees are a top priority.
Career Opportunities
We manage talent as seriously as we manage our businesses and encourage you to learn about our proud history, strong culture, technologies, and vision for the future. We offer positions locally and globally with over 80 locations in 19 countries.
If this position energizes you and you feel you can help us achieve our mission and vision, you are invited to submit an application for consideration.
You may see the list of requirements and feel you do not meet all of them. However, remember that BorgWarner thinks differently. If your qualifications align with the majority of those outlined in this job description, we encourage you to apply and share your experience and skills with us.
Job Purpose
BorgWarner PowerDrive Systems is currently looking for “dynamic, results driven” individual to join as an Electronics Hardware Design Intern in our Summer Internship Program.
The Electronics Hardware Design Intern will be focused on day-to-day support and assisting engineers in designing, characterizing, and testing various aspects of automotive power conversion products. Further, the intern will assist in related problem resolution in the exciting and growing field of power electronics for hybrid and electric cars.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in the electrical design, simulation and analysis of power electronics circuits and systems to meet technical product requirements
- Perform the electrical debug, test, characterization, and verification of power electronics designs
- Assist in specifying, identifying, and testing of key, critical electrical components
- Support BorgWarner product development team with technical design analysis, trade off studies, and design reviews
- Gain understanding of the vehicle system components and functions that interface to the power electronics subsystem
- Work with other engineering competencies and suppliers to aid in the development and verification of electronics products
- Use a broad range of electronic lab equipment to build, analyse, test, and verify designs functionally. Examples of tests are:
- Embedded controller verification
- Power Electronics efficiency, static and dynamic performance
- Thermal test bench
- Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC)
What We Are Looking For
- Currently enrolled in an accredited college, university, or be a graduate from an accredited college; however, students pursuing a Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering with a focus in Power Electronics will be preferred
- GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or B average, upon initial hire date
- Candidate needs to have a strong interest in the automotive and / or power electronics field
- Experience in Power Electronics is preferred through one of the following: organizations, research programs, internships
- Knowledge of modelling, simulating, and/or circuit design required

Why Engineering?
Engineering drives the innovation and solutions that power our growth and success, connecting ideas to real-world impact and delivering value at scale. Our Engineers create cutting-edge solutions that make a real difference for millions of customers. Whether it's enhancing mobile apps, leveraging AI and emerging agentic technologies for personalised experiences, or simplifying core systems, our engineers are shaping the future of banking.
We’re not just building tech, we’re building better customer journeys, smarter systems, and a more secure digital future.
Your internship journey
Our Engineering internship is structured differently to all other internships and is designed to give you a real appreciation of what it means to work for us as an Engineer. The programme emphasises agile ways of working and immerses you in a dynamic and collaborative environment in which you’ll get to work in Scrums on real business projects supported by engineering experts.
At the end of the internship, we’ll assess you on what you’ve learned. Complete this successfully and you could be offered a place on our Engineering graduate programme, where you can carry forward the skills you’ve learnt into the next stage of your career.
Over the course of this eight-week programme, you can look forward to:
- Actively participating and contributing to real engineering projects
- Attending daily stand ups in your scrum project teams to drive real business progress as well as participation in end of sprint demos, retros, and feedback sessions
- Developing your engineering skills and application through agile methodologies, AI-assisted engineering practices and NatWest ways of working
- The opportunity to attend regular business and engineering spotlight so you can understand how our engineers contribute to the broader business and our customers
- Learning about how we operate, and how the contribution of Engineering makes a difference across our business technology functions including Retail, Wealth, Commercial & Institutional and Customer & Operations
- Learning how engineers collaborate with AI tools and emerging agentic technologies to solve complex problems while applying human judgement and critical thinking
- Building an understanding of the products and services we provide for our customers and colleagues
- Attending Engineering specific networking events, social engagements and the opportunity to hear from senior leaders across the bank
How you’ll benefit
We’ll reward you with a starting salary of £29,400 pro rata.
Plus, you can expect to:
- Learn from industry experts and immediately apply your learnings
- Enrich your learning with access to our Learning Academy
- Test and learn new approaches in a safe, inclusive environment
- Start building a professional network
- Grow your confidence, build your resilience, and elevate your presence
- Experience first-hand what it’s like working in a purpose-driven organisation
Entry requirements
To be eligible for our Engineering internship, you’ll need:
- To be in your penultimate year of university
- To be on course to achieving a 2:1 in a STEM subject
- Clear communication skills, and the ability to break down complex problems and explain your ideas
- A curious, logical mindset with a passion for solving problems and exploring emerging technologies, including AI
- Confidence working with data, statistics, and experimentation, and evidence-based decision making
- A flexible attitude, comfortable with change and ambiguity and continuous learning in a rapidly evolving technology landscape
- A drive to learn, grow, and make a real impact
Ready to apply?
The application window for this programme will be open until we receive enough applications to fill our cohort. When that happens, we’ll close the programme to new applications. It’s important to take the time to make sure you’re making the right decision about the programme you want to apply for (you can only apply for one programme) but please complete your application as soon as you can to make sure you don’t miss out!
Have another question?
Head over to our ‘Applying and eligibility support’ page now for answers to some of our most commonly asked questions.

35

Ways of Working:Hybrid

Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.
Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
About the Job:
Keysight is looking for an electrical engineering intern to join our R&D team in Colorado Springs, CO. This individual will be responsible for designing next-generation technology for test and measurement applications, including electronic elements for oscilloscope products, modular RF products, and/or probes and accessories products.
The ideal candidate is working towards a BS or MS in EE or ECE and shows proficiency in PCA circuit design and simulation. The candidate should be a self-starter with strong communication skills.
About the Team:
Come make an impact with Keysight’s Digital and Photonics Center of Excellence located in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Enjoy Colorado’s abundance of outdoor recreational opportunities while working in an engineering environment dedicated to innovation, contribution, trust, respect and teamwork. As part of our R&D team you will be a member of our diverse group of world-class electrical, mechanical, and software engineers, helping you transform your designs into high-demand products.
Responsibilities
- Design PCAs for cutting-edge electronic measurement products.
- Own the component selection and schematic design of PCAs under your control.
- Use simulation software as necessary to validate conceptual circuit designs.
- Work closely with PCA layout resources to ensure placement and routing meet your design requirements.
- Work closely with other engineering disciplines on your team to capture and incorporate their requirements into your designs, such as mounting locations, interconnections, heat sinks, RF shields, etc.
- Document your designs for ongoing and future reference.
- Test, debug, and characterize your designs to ensure they function as intended.
- In general, apply EE knowledge and skills to represent your discipline among a collaborative design team. Help your team weigh tradeoffs and solve problems.
- Continue to grow in your discipline and learn new skills as necessary to make your team successful.
Qualifications
Requirements:
- Working towards a BS or MS in EE/ECE or have applicable experience and education
- Familiarity with circuit design and analysis, PCA design, component selection, etc.
- Knowledge of simulation tools for concept validation
- Familiarity with schematic and layout tools
- Experience using electronic test and measurement equipment
- Passion to continuously investigate new technologies, tools, and processes within your discipline
- Self-motivation – must enjoy solving difficult and sometimes open-ended design problems in a team environment
- Strong work ethic
- Strong communication and documentation skills, ability to collaborate cross-functionally with a team-oriented mindset
Desired Qualifications:
- Working towards an MS in EE/ECE
- Familiarity with digital and RF components such samplers, filters, mixers and transmission lines
- Experience with Mentor Graphics
- Experience with Keysight’s ADS software package
- Ability to perform hands-on measurements with VNAs, oscilloscopes and signal generators
- Experience with the complete design-prototype-analyze cycle.
The level of role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the salary listed below.

Location: Vancouver, B.C, Canada
Employment type: Internship/Co-op
About Astera Labs
Astera Labs develops purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure. Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform brings together high-performance connectivity technologies for AI, cloud, server, and networking systems. We design cutting-edge connectivity solutions that power the world’s largest cloud service providers, server manufacturers, and networking OEMs.
The role
As a Platform Application Engineer Intern, you’ll play a pivotal role in building and supporting the validation tools and infrastructure that enable our products to be tested, integrated, and deployed at scale with confidence.
You’ll develop and maintain tools that make our products easier to integrate, debug, and validate for both customers and internal engineering teams. Your work will range from developing automation and validation frameworks to working hands-on in the lab with state-of-the-art hardware and test equipment.
You’ll collaborate closely with cross-functional engineering teams to investigate complex technical challenges, improve validation coverage, and accelerate product deployment. You’ll also have opportunities to drive innovation in validation methodologies and streamline development and deployment processes.
This is a high-impact, hands-on role at the intersection of software and hardware, where curiosity, creativity, and technical depth come together to help define the next generation of data center infrastructure.

PREDICTING WHAT HAPPENS NEXT IS JUST THE beginning OF YOUR JOURNEY.
The Opportunity
If building models that help people make better decisions, understanding uncertainty, and turning complex systems into meaningful predictions sounds like your kind of challenge, we’re looking for you.
As an Architecture Research Intern, you’ll use simulation and queueing theory to understand how business changes (new service channels, process redesigns, demand shifts) ripple through operations and shape the customer experience. You’ll contribute to initiatives in Queue Management, Estimated Wait Time, and Predictive Simulation. From forecasting wait times to modelling the dynamics of complex operational systems, you’ll help develop solutions that improve experiences for our members.
Your background might be in queueing theory, simulation science, applied mathematics, stochastic processes, differential equations, or optimization. Either way, you’ll apply your research skills to real-world problems where uncertainty isn’t a complication, it’s part of the solution.
*This role is for a 12-month opportunity with the possibility of extension.*
The Team You’ve Been Looking For
AMA is more than a workplace; it’s a family. Together, we help protect the things that matter most to our more than one-million members—everything from roadside safety to retail savings, food security to childhood well-being. And with operations that span automotive, registries, travel, insurance, and more, the opportunities to grow with us are almost limitless!
Building on a century of proud service in Alberta communities, we’re passionate about making a meaningful difference in the places where we live and work. And that all begins with our people. As part of the AMA team, you’ll enjoy:
- Competitive wage
- Employee-exclusive discounts on travel, insurance, memberships, and more
- Ongoing professional development
- Vacation earnings paid out with each pay period
- Flexible work models that makes sense for your lifestyle
For us, curiosity fuels innovation. We value people who are eager to explore new ideas and who are comfortable putting emerging technologies into practice. We see experience with AI‑powered tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, and similar platforms as a real plus - especially when it’s used to work smarter, increase efficiency, and find better ways to get things done.
Who You Are
- You’re fascinated by uncertainty and enjoy understanding how complex systems behave over time.
- You see queues everywhere and naturally think in terms of arrivals, service, congestion, and waiting.
- You naturally think in terms of probabilities, outcomes, and trade-offs.
- You ask “what if we changed this?” and know how to build a model that answers it rigorously.
- You’re comfortable working with incomplete information and building models that help make sense of it.
- You can balance model fidelity against computational cost and decision deadlines.
- You communicate technical concepts clearly and can explain uncertainty without creating confusion.
- You’re analytical, curious, and motivated by solving real-world problems.
- You enjoy collaborating and know the best solutions come from combining different perspectives.
- You love turning research ideas into practical models that create measurable value.
How You’ll Make an Impact
- Contribute to predictive models and simulation frameworks that support queue management and estimated wait-time forecasting.
- Apply queueing theory to model customer flow, congestion, and waiting (for example multi-server queues, priority queues, queues with abandonment and retrials, and queueing networks) and use it to derive fast, interpretable wait-time estimates.
- Build simulation models (discrete-event, agent-based, and/or system dynamics) to evaluate how proposed business changes affect wait times, service levels, abandonment, and overall customer experience before they are implemented.
- Compare analytical queueing results against detailed simulation and real operational data to determine where theory holds, where it breaks down, and which approach best suits each decision.
- Formulate and analyze continuous-time models of system behavior using ordinary and stochastic differential equations (for example fluid and diffusion approximations of queues, including heavy-traffic limits based on reflected Brownian motion), and validate them against detailed simulation and real operational data.
- Design and apply time-constrained optimization algorithms (such as simulation-based optimization, parameter tuning, and anytime or heuristic methods) that deliver good decisions within real operational time limits.
- Design, test, and refine models that capture uncertainty, customer behavior, and system dynamics.
- Apply probabilistic and statistical techniques to evaluate performance, calibrate and validate models, and improve predictive accuracy.
- Run scenario, sensitivity, and what-if analyses that help business leaders understand bottlenecks, trade-offs, and future outcomes.
- Analyze results and communicate key insights, assumptions, limitations, and recommendations to stakeholders.
- Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and business teams to turn theory into practical, deployable solutions.
- Explore innovative approaches that improve decision-making across AMA’s products, services, and operations.
What You Bring to the Table
- You’re currently pursuing, or have completed, an MSc or PhD in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Operations Research, Computational Science, or a closely related quantitative discipline.
- You have in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience of queueing theory, including Markovian and general queues (M/M/c, M/G/1, G/G/c), Little’s Law, queues with abandonment and priorities, queueing networks, transient and steady-state analysis, and heavy-traffic and diffusion approximations. You can fit queueing models to real data and judge when their assumptions hold.
- You have in-depth knowledge of simulation science, including discrete-event and/or agent-based simulation, Monte Carlo methods, variance reduction, input modelling, model verification and validation, and experimental design for simulation studies.
- You have a strong foundation in differential equations (ordinary, partial, and/or stochastic), including Brownian motion and diffusion processes, Fokker-Planck equations, and numerical methods for SDEs, and can apply them to model the dynamics of real systems.
- You have working knowledge of optimization, particularly time-constrained or real-time settings: simulation optimization, stochastic and dynamic programming, metaheuristics, or anytime algorithms.
- You have a strong foundation in probability and stochastic processes, with experience in one or more of the following:
-
- Markov chains and Markov decision processes
- Renewal and point processes (for example Poisson and non-homogeneous Poisson arrival processes)
- Statistical mechanics
- Stochastic differential equations
- You have strong statistical judgment and understand the nuances of uncertainty, including the distinction between prediction intervals and confidence intervals.
- You’re proficient in Python and can independently translate models and research concepts into reliable, well-tested code (for example NumPy, SciPy, SimPy, and optimization libraries).
Belonging Matters Here
AMA is committed to providing an inclusive, respectful, and accessible environment. If you require an accommodation at any time during our recruitment process, please contact recruitment@ama.ab.ca . We’ll work with you to feel supported throughout your journey with us.

About GlobalFoundries
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, powerefficient and highperformance solutions for highgrowth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.
Internship Program Overview:
Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives.
Summary of Role:
Join the MIPS CPU IP Engineering organization for hands-on experience in the design and verification of advanced RISC-V processor IP. You will work with CPU architects, RTL designers, and verification engineers on CPU microarchitecture, RTL implementation, functional verification, performance analysis, automation, and debug in Austin, Texas or Santa Clara, California.
Essential Responsibilities include:
- Support RISC-V CPU microarchitecture and SystemVerilog RTL design and development.
- Contribute to CPU functions including instruction fetch and decode, execution, load/store, caches and memory interfaces, control and status registers, exceptions, and interrupts.
- Develop verification tests, assertions, checkers, and functional coverage for CPU features.
- Run CPU simulations and regressions and debug failures using logs, architectural traces, and waveforms.
- Verify processor functionality across instructions, privilege modes, memory operations, and architectural corner cases.
- Support CPU power, performance, and area analysis and optimization.
- Develop Python, C/C++, or scripting-based automation to improve design, verification, regression, and debug productivity.
- Document technical results and communicate findings to the engineering team.
Other Responsibilities:
- Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.
Required Qualifications:
- Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.
- Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing.
- Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)
- Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.
- Coursework or project experience in digital logic design and computer architecture.
- Familiarity with Verilog or SystemVerilog.
- Understanding of CPU fundamentals including pipelines, instruction execution, loads/stores, caches, and memory hierarchy.
- Programming or scripting experience with Python, C/C++, or similar languages.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills.
