- Prior related internship or co-op experience
- Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc.
- Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a diverse team of scientists and engineers.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our research team within Meta Recommendation Systems (MRS). This team brings together a world-class team of AI Research Scientists and Engineers. Our vision is to leverage AI frontier models and technology in all aspects of recommendation systems including but not limited to deep understanding of multi-modal content (especially images/videos, posts, user interactions), modeling user interests and preference, agentic AI for recsys, recursive self-improvement for recsys, values of the ecosystems. We contribute to the mission of connecting users to the content they enjoy, are inspired by, and that they want to see more of. To this end, we conduct cutting-edge research using the complete suite of audio, visual, text and metadata signals associated with posts and videos to improve recommendation relevance across all surfaces and provide a better, more meaningful experience to users. We build tools, create frameworks and train models that we deploy together with product and infrastructure teams to gain adoption across the FoA. We also publish scientific papers to help advance the state of the art in all aspects of the technology stack.
Our team offers twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long internships and we have various start dates throughout the year.

About Trace

 

Trace is building the data, infrastructure, and research that enable robots to learn from the real world. General-purpose robotics requires a deeper understanding of how robots learn from real-world data. Our research explores how to transform human experiences, including egocentric video, demonstrations, hand-object interactions, and multimodal sensory signals, into transferable representations, actionable knowledge, and generalizable robot behaviors. At our Brooklyn research lab, we combine fundamental research in robot learning, computer vision, and embodied AI with large-scale datasets, machine learning infrastructure, and real-world robotic experimentation. Our goal is to advance the science of robot learning while developing the datasets and learning foundations for increasingly capable, adaptable, and reliable robots.

 
 

About the role

 

We are looking for highly motivated Research Interns to join our research team and work on challenging, high-impact problems at the intersection of robot learning, embodied AI, and learning from human experience. This internship is designed for PhD students and exceptional Master's students who are passionate about advancing the state of the art in robotics and machine learning.

 
 

As a Research Intern, you will take ownership of a focused research project, working closely with our scientists and engineers to formulate research questions, develop novel methods, design rigorous experiments, and evaluate results using real-world datasets, simulation, and/or robotic platforms. We encourage ambitious, scientifically grounded research with the potential to contribute to top-tier robotics, machine learning, and computer vision conferences. You will have opportunities to pursue original research, collaborate with an interdisciplinary team, and help shape Trace's long-term research directions.

 
 

Research areas

 

Research projects may span one or more of the following areas, but are not limited to:

 
 

• Learning from Human Experience and Egocentric Data

 

• Human-to-Robot and Cross-Embodiment Transfer

 

• Foundation Models for Robot Learning

 

• Visual-Tactile and Multimodal Robot Learning

 

• Data-Centric Robot Learning and Scaling

 

• Dexterous Manipulation and Generalizable Robot Skills

 

• Robustness, Generalization, and Reliable Robot Learning

 
 

We particularly welcome candidates who bring novel perspectives, strong methodological expertise, or creative research ideas that complement these directions.

 
 

What you'll do

 

• Lead an original research project from problem formulation and hypothesis development through method design, implementation, experimentation, and evaluation, with guidance and collaboration from Trace's research team.

 

• Develop and evaluate novel robot learning methods, including learning algorithms, representations, models, or training strategies that leverage human demonstrations, multimodal datasets, and robotic interaction data.

 

• Design rigorous experiments and benchmarks to investigate fundamental questions about data quality, human-to-robot transfer, policy learning, generalization, and real-world robotic performance.

 

• Work with diverse data modalities, potentially including egocentric video, human hand and body motion, teleoperation demonstrations, visual-tactile signals, force measurements, and robot trajectories.

 

• Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to build reproducible experimental pipelines, train and evaluate models, and validate research findings in simulation and/or on real robotic platforms.

 

• Analyze experimental results and failure modes, draw actionable scientific insights, and communicate findings through technical discussions, presentations, and written reports.

 

• Contribute to high-quality research publications and open research artifacts, with opportunities to submit work to leading robotics and machine learning venues.

 
 

What we're looking for

 

• Currently pursuing a PhD or Master's degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field.

 

• Strong research background in at least one relevant area, such as robot learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, computer vision, embodied AI, foundation models, dexterous manipulation, multimodal learning, or learning from human demonstrations.

 

• Demonstrated research excellence and potential, evidenced by high-quality publications, impactful research projects, open-source contributions, or other substantial research accomplishments. Publications at leading venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, T-RO, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or CVPR are highly valued. First-author or co-first-author publications are a strong plus.

 

• Excellent programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX. Experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

 

• Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

Nice to have

 

• Experience with real-world robot learning experiments, robotic manipulation platforms, or deployment of learned policies on physical robots.

 

• Experience with egocentric video, human demonstrations, hand tracking, pose estimation, motion retargeting, or cross-embodiment learning.

 

• Experience with vision-language-action models, diffusion-based policies, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or world models.

 

• Experience with tactile sensing, force estimation, multimodal sensor fusion, or contact-rich manipulation.

 

• Experience with robotics simulation environments and tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or related frameworks.

 

• Previous research experience in an industrial research lab or a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment.

 
 

How to apply

 

Please submit your CV/resume, along with links to your Google Scholar profile, personal website, GitHub, or other relevant research portfolio, if available. Internship start dates are flexible. Academic credit may be available if required by your degree program, subject to institutional requirements.

 
 

Trace is an equal opportunity employer.

Job Details:
Job Description:
About Altera
At Altera™, our independence as the world’s largest pure‑play FPGA solutions provider gives us the focus, speed, and agility to innovate without compromise. With more than four decades of industry‑leading FPGA expertise, our singular mission is to deliver the programmable technologies that help customers differentiate, innovate, and scale across rapidly evolving markets like AI, cloud, networking, and edge. As an independent company, we move faster, invest deeper, and partner more closely—empowering our teams to drive breakthrough innovation and shape the future of the FPGA industry.
About the Role
Join Altera IP solutions team and work on cutting edge FPGA RTL and IP design!  Altera's IP Solutions Engineering (IPSE) team develops comprehensive solutions to provide customers easy and efficient access to the capabilities of Altera’s FPGA devices. These solutions are provided as highly configurable intellectual property (IP) cores that are fully integrated with Altera's software CAD tool, Quartus Prime. The External Memory Interfaces (EMIF) and IO team is responsible for developing IPs for communication with state-of-the-art DDR and LPDDR devices, MIPI cameras and sensors, and other high-speed I/O applications. The ever-growing demand for faster I/O interfaces - especially in the data center and machine learning sectors - presents a challenging design problem that requires system-level knowledge of silicon, software, IP, and customer applications.
You will work with a team of engineers to develop and verify state-of-the-art IP cores for interfacing with external memories and other I/O devices. You will be working on advanced FPGA architectures, design definition, implementation, and verification. Additionally, you will also be developing design examples and simulation models, accompanied by a rich set of technical documentation. In this role, you will work closely with multiple teams, including silicon design and validation, post-silicon validation, application engineering, and customer experience teams, to ensure seamless development, integration, and optimization of high-speed interface IP solutions.
Your specific responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
- Architecture and Design based on the latest protocol specifications for DDR, LPDDR, and MIPI devices
- RTL development
- Device support and CAD tool integration
- Verification (e.g. verification IP, methodologies, frameworks, bus functional models, regression tests)
- Hardware power-on and debug
- New product release and rollout support
- Customer technical support
The candidate should possess the following behavioral traits:
- Strong skills in communication, initiative, innovation, and teamwork
- Highly motivated to learn and adapt to fast-changing technologies and environments
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
- Demonstrate fundamental values such as accountability, integrity, and a winning mindset
- Collaborative mindset, strong influencing skills, and a willingness to work across geographical locations
Salary
Our compensation is designed to reflect the Canadian labour market. The actual salary offered may vary based on several factors, including the position’s location, as well as the candidate’s experience, skills, training, and job-specific knowledge. In addition to base salary, we offer performance-based incentive opportunities that reward both individual contributions and overall company success.​
Estimated Salary Range: $90,000 - $100,000 CAD​
​

Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes, project work, internships, and/or military experience. Overview
Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Wireline Network Test is seeking an FPGA intern to support development of our wireline Ethernet test products. You’ll work with advanced technologies and standards, including FPGA logic operating at 600+ MHz and line speeds exceeding 1600Gbps.
Join a highly talented and motivated team of hardware and software engineers developing a state-of-the-art wireline Ethernet test system. Leveraging the latest generation of FPGAs and multi-core CPUs, our test instruments are designed to stay ahead of mainstream solutions—enabling validation of equipment and networks before deployment. Driven by the growing bandwidth demands of hyperscale data centers and carrier networks, our systems must support the highest speeds and newest technologies well before they reach the market. - Create and developing innovative new products and features
- Drive continuous process and code base improvements

- Enrolled in a B.Sc or M.Sc in EE or CE program
- Strong analytical skills. Excellent written, verbal, presentation communication skills. Must be able to read and interpret complex information.
- Able to cultivate interpersonal relationships and cohesive team interactions and communications.
- VHDL or Verilog proficiency
- Basic C programming knowledge
- Knowledge or experience in the following areas is a plus
- Knowledge of Ethernet technologies from 1G to 1600G+
- Experience with SerDes up to 212Gbps, memory technologies such as DDR4, RLDRAM3, and interconnect protocols such as PCIe and Interlaken
- Understanding of data networks, networking protocols, switch/router operation, and protocol stack implementations is desirable
- Understanding of interpreted languages such at Tcl or Python

About Orbital Operations
At Orbital Operations, we’re building the future of dynamic space maneuvering. Our mission is to enable rapid-response orbital capabilities, executing maneuvers without hesitation and without regret.
Our flagship technology, the Cryogenic Propulsion Management System (CPMS), is redefining what’s possible in space mobility. Designed for military and commercial spacecraft, CPMS delivers sustained, high-thrust maneuverability in geosynchronous and cislunar orbits. It integrates low-loss cryogenic storage, reverse Brayton cycle (RBC) thermal control, and turbomachinery-driven propulsion to make spacecraft more agile, resilient, and responsive.
Beyond defense, CPMS is poised to transform commercial orbital logistics. By powering next-generation orbital transfer vehicles (OTVs), it can slash LEO-to-GEO transit times from six months to just eight hours—unlocking new possibilities for satellite servicing, deployment, and beyond.
Join us in building the infrastructure for a more maneuverable and mission-ready space domain.
About the Role
At Orbital Operations, we believe bold missions demand exceptional builders. We’re assembling a world-class team to push the boundaries of dynamic space maneuvering, and we’re looking for engineering interns who have already demonstrated that they can take real hardware from an idea to a tested result.
This is not an internship where you’ll spend the your time observing from the sidelines or working on isolated analysis. You’ll own a meaningful hardware project with a clear technical objective and be responsible for driving it through execution. Depending on the project, that may include defining requirements, performing analysis, designing components, creating drawings, working with vendors or manufacturing equipment, assembling hardware, developing test plans, running tests, analyzing results, troubleshooting failures, and implementing the next iteration.
You’ll be paired with a dedicated mentor, but you’ll be expected to take initiative, make sound engineering decisions, communicate blockers, and keep your project moving. You’ll work directly alongside engineers across design, analysis, manufacturing, test, and operations while contributing to hardware that supports our cryogenic propulsion and orbital mobility systems.
We are specifically looking for interns who have previously owned hardware through most or all of its lifecycle. That experience may come from a student engineering team, research laboratory, previous internship, personal project, machine shop, startup, or other hands-on environment. The scale of the project matters less than the depth of your ownership.
Strong candidates can clearly explain:
- What they personally owned and delivered
- How they translated a need into engineering requirements
- Which design decisions and tradeoffs they made
- How the hardware was manufactured and assembled
- How they tested it and determined whether it worked
- What failed, what they learned, and what they changed
- What they would do differently on the next iteration
Internship opportunities are available across our engineering teams, including:
- Mechanical Design
- Fluid Systems Design and Analysis
- Test and Integration
- Manufacturing and Assembly
- Avionics
If you want to be judged by the hardware you deliver and are ready to take a project from concept through test we’d love to hear from you.
Qualifications
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related STEM field
- Demonstrated ownership of at least one hands on engineering project from concept or requirements through fabrication, assembly, testing, and iteration
- Strong command of engineering fundamentals and the ability to apply them to practical, open ended problems
- Experience designing, building, integrating, or testing physical hardware through a student team, internship, research program, employment, or personal project
- Ability to make engineering tradeoffs and move forward when requirements or information are incomplete
- Willingness to work directly with hardware, including assembly, instrumentation, troubleshooting, and test operations
- Ability to independently plan and execute a complex technical project while identifying and communicating risks and blockers
- Resourceful, self-directed, and comfortable learning unfamiliar tools or technical subjects quickly
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document designs, test results, failures, and lessons learned
- Able to work full-time and onsite in Long Beach, California, for a minimum of 10–12 consecutive weeks
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with CAD, engineering drawings, tolerance analysis, machining, additive manufacturing, composite fabrication, electronics, instrumentation, or fluid-system assembly
- Experience creating and executing test plans, collecting data, and comparing results against analytical predictions or requirements
- Participation in a hands-on engineering organization such as Formula SAE, Baja SAE, liquid or solid rocketry, CubeSat, robotics, Design/Build/Fly, or a similar project team
- A portfolio, technical report, project page, or other work sample that clearly demonstrates your individual contribution to completed hardware
- Experience diagnosing a hardware failure and carrying the resulting lessons into a successful design iteration

We are looking for a Hardware Field Quality Engineer Intern to join our Field Quality team at our Longueuil facility. Once our bikes, e-bikes, batteries, and stations leave the factory, Field Quality owns how they hold up in the real world: millions of rides, all four seasons, in cities across the globe. You will work alongside field quality engineers to help spot emerging hardware issues, investigate their root cause, and support fixes with engineering, manufacturing, and market operations teams. You will spend time hands-on with failed parts in the lab, and just as much time in the data working out how big a problem really is.
Responsibilities:
- Support failure analysis on parts returned from the field, including requests from enterprise customers, by helping with teardown, inspection, and electrical testing and documenting findings with photos.
- Help monitor field data, such as vehicle and station alerts and repair records, and flag emerging issues to the team.
- Build and update dashboards and queries that track reliability metrics and retrofit progress.

FIRST ORDER EFFECTS

Operations Engineering Intern

Infrastructure for the Autonomous Era  ·  First in. First up.

On-site · Austin, TX · Paid: $20–$35/hour (depending on experience) · Flexible 2–6 month term - a semester, a co-op, or the rest of your summer

---------------------------------------------------




WHO WE ARE

First Order Effects (FOE) is building America's Infrastructure Prime for the robotic era. Autonomous ships, drones, and robots are rewriting how the world moves, fights, and builds - but none of them work without infrastructure to power them, connect them, and launch and recover them. That's what we build.




WE'VE BUILT CUTTING EDGE SYSTEMS AT LEGENDARY COMPANIES

Our team comes from SpaceX, Anduril, Saronic, Lockheed Skunk Works, Forterra, and Fuse Energy. Before founding FOE, we built satellite ground stations that closed a national comms gap in days, deployed multi-megawatt power systems at commercial speed, and shipped autonomous surface vessels into Navy fleet production. We've built infrastructure at lightspeed before - now we're applying that playbook to an entire company.

As an intern here, you won't be six layers away from the people who did those things. You'll be right alongside them.




THE ROLE

Operations engineering is the connective tissue between a CAD model and hardware sitting on a beach doing its job. You'll help us build, test, and deploy real systems - and help build the machine that builds them: the tooling, processes, supply chain, and test infrastructure a seed-stage hardware company needs to move fast without breaking the wrong things.

This is not a shadowing program. You will own real work with real deadlines, and what you touch will ship.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build real hardware. Assembly, integration, and test of MESH Box and SURGE systems - mechanical, electrical, and everything in between.

 - Own projects end-to-end. Scope it, design it, build it, test it, write it up. Fixtures, jigs, test rigs, harnesses, ground support equipment.

 - Run tests. Write test procedures, instrument hardware, collect data, and tell us what it means - in the shop and at the waterfront.

 - Wrangle the supply chain. Source parts, chase vendors, drive procurement, and keep the build moving when a component is three weeks late.

 - Unblock engineers. If it's slowing the team down - a missing tool, a broken process, a spreadsheet that should be a script - you fix it.

 - Whatever the mission needs. Seed-stage means the org chart is a suggestion. The interesting problems go to whoever grabs them.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Pursuing a degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, industrial, or a related engineering field.

 - Evidence you build things outside of class: FSAE, rocketry, robotics, solar car, a shop job, a garage project that got out of hand. Show us, don't tell us.

 - Raw horsepower, judgment, ownership, and execution. These matter more than your GPA or which classes you've taken.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. You'd rather be handed a problem than a procedure.

 - Willingness to get your hands dirty - literally. Warehouses, waterfronts, weather.

 - Command of English at a CEFR Level C1 (C2 Preferred). Bonus points for speaking a second language fluently.



ITAR Requirements:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.




WHY FOE

 - Real ownership, real hardware, real deployments. Your work goes on systems headed for the water, not into a slide deck.

 - Seed-stage leverage. Everything is being built for the first time. The systems you set up become how the company works.

 - Learn from people who've done it. Daily, direct access to engineers from SpaceX, Anduril, Saronic, and Skunk Works.

 - Paid, flexible, and real. $20–$35/hour depending on experience. Semester, co-op, or summer - we'll build a 2–6 month window that works with your program.

 - A path forward. Crush it here and there's a return offer or a full-time conversation waiting.




THIS IS NOT A NORMAL INTERNSHIP

We're a small team moving very fast on a mission that matters. Some days are CAD and spreadsheets; some days are a 4 a.m. drive to the waterfront to catch a tide window. We optimize for signal over noise. If you want a structured rotation program with a polished intern curriculum, this isn't it. If you want to find out what you're capable of when someone hands you something real, it is.



FOE is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with FOE is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.




HOW TO APPLY

Send your resume and three bullet points demonstrating evidence of exceptional ability via our careers portal (https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/firstordereffects ). Projects, wins, things you shipped - whatever proves it. A founder will personally read every application.



Sovereignty is built, not declared — come build it with us.

At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. As a Forward Deployed Test Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work at the intersection of software, hardware, and testing to help our customers build and operate better test systems.

BONUS POINTS

About Taara:

Born at X, Google's Moonshot Factory, Taara is on a mission to connect billions of people lacking abundant and affordable internet today by pioneering the way we use light to deliver faster, cheaper, more reliable connectivity. We are bringing groundbreaking wireless optical communication and photonics chip technologies to the world to bridge the digital divide.

Joining Taara allows you to work as part of a multidisciplinary team of experts in optics, software, and hardware, all collaborating to solve the hardest connectivity challenges on a global scale. If you want to tackle problems that matter and build tools with real-world impact, we would love to meet you.

About the Role:

At Taara, as a Coherent Optical Systems Intern, you will work on receiver synchronization for next-generation wireless optical communication (WOC) links. This is a larger-scope opportunity (6 to 12+ months) spanning both lab and simulation work, and could form the basis of a longer-term collaboration or thesis project.

What such a receiver can achieve is bounded by real lasers, modulators, and analog electronics. You will evaluate components against system requirements, assemble the benchtop experiments that test them, and work toward stable closed-loop operation. In parallel you will extend the simulation that predicts this behavior, using each to check the other. 

There is real room to shape the direction: survey what is available, design the experiments that separate real limits from prototype artifacts, and follow the evidence to the strongest design.

How you will make 10X Impact:

 - Component Evaluation: Screen commercially available lasers, modulators, and front-end electronics against system requirements, and measure the characteristics vendors do not publish (tuning response, wavelength stability and drift, linewidth, bandwidth, range, noise).

 - Synchronization & Control Loop Design: Design and analyze the feedback loops that track carrier phase and frequency, and validate them against control theory using transient, frequency-domain, and stability analysis.

 - Physical-Layer Simulation: Extend our end-to-end model of the link and its tracking loops, and reconcile it against measurement.

What you should have:

 - Currently pursuing a Master's, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Optics, Communications, or a related field.

 - Working knowledge of Analog / RF Electronics, and a feel for how hardware limits (delay, bandwidth, noise, saturation) shape the loop and the signal processing around it. Strong foundation in Digital Communications / Signal Processing (modulation, detection, BER, spectral analysis).

 - Hands-on lab experience, including work with lasers and modulators, and comfort with high-speed scopes, spectrum analyzers, and power meters.

 - Strong familiarity with Control theory on hardware measuring an open-loop response, closing a feedback loop, and diagnosing why one oscillates, drifts, or loses lock.

 - Experience with scientific Python (NumPy/SciPy), and comfort writing clean, modular, tested code.

 - An owner's mindset, able to take an underspecified hardware problem and drive it forward independently in the lab.

 - A habit of reaching a clear conclusion and documenting it, including when the conclusion is that an approach does not work.

 - Ability to commit to a 6-12 months internship, with flexibility to fit your academic schedule.

 - Ability to work in the Sunnyvale office at least 3 days per week.

It'd be great if you also had one or more of these:

 - Laser Frequency Control: Stabilizing or locking lasers, or hands-on work with narrow-linewidth sources, tunable lasers, and optical modulators.

 - Synchronization: Familiarity with phase-locked loops, carrier and timing recovery, or coherent detection.

 - Hardware Depth: Hands-on circuit design (analog, RF, or mixed-signal), or lab characterization of high-speed electronics.

 - High-Performance Numerics: Experience with accelerated array frameworks such as JAX, and functional, vectorized programming.

 - Stochastic Methods: Phase-noise modeling, rare-event Monte Carlo, or first-passage / cycle-slip statistics (Fokker-Planck, Kramers rate).

 - Domain Knowledge: Optical or RF communications, photonics, free-space optics, or atmospheric turbulence/fading channels.

 - Judgment about real components, knowing which datasheet specifications are guaranteed and which are typical, and a willingness to go measure the ones that matter.

 - Control theory you have applied on hardware, including measuring an open-loop response, closing a feedback loop, and diagnosing why one oscillates, drifts, or loses lock.

What we offer:

 - Competitive salary: $7,000-$10,000/month depending on degree.

 - Flexible duration to fit your academic schedule.

 - Direct mentorship from industry-leading engineers in a "moonshot" environment.

 - Opportunity to work on technology that has the potential to change how billions of people access the internet.

MaiaSpace is a European space tech company, designing, manufacturing and operating competitive and sustainable solutions for space mobility. We are driven by the belief that access to space is a major enabler for a better and more sustainable life on Earth, addressing the challenges faced by humanity: climate, resources, connectivity, and data. Our aim is to design, test and fly a cost-effective and reusable mini-launch vehicle.
Inside MaiaSpace development teams, you will join the Avionics team. This team defines and develops the launcher’s electrical and data architecture, including onboard computers, sensors and data acquisition, telemetry and the associated ground processing chain. It is responsible for making test and flight data available, reliable and usable by all launcher teams. The team works closely with the propulsion, fluid systems, GNC, test and mission teams. As part of this team, you will be at the heart of the preparation and analysis of the first test campaigns and launches.
Within the Avionics team, we propose the following training topic for 2027 :
Test & flight data exploitation and physical model calibration
Test campaigns and flights generate large volumes of measurements from the launcher’s sensors and acquisition systems, such as pressures, temperatures, flow rates and valve states. Turning this data into usable engineering knowledge and using it to calibrate the physical models that support design and flight predictions, is a key part of the development loop. The goal of this internship is to automate this loop, from the acquisition chain output to the recalibrated models. Your tasks will include:
- Data exploitation pipeline: develop Python tools to ingest, decode, clean, synchronize and post-process test and flight data, including telemetry. This covers format handling, sensor health checks, filtering, event detection and time alignment across acquisition sources.
- Data quality and traceability: define data validation rules and metadata conventions and contribute to structuring the test and flight data archive so it can be queried by all teams.
- Automated reporting: with the user teams, define the key indicators to monitor, then generate standardized plots and reports for each test or flight.
- Model calibration: together with the Fluids & Pressurization team, set up automated recalibration of physical models against measured data, for example pressurization, tank thermodynamics or feed line hydraulics. This involves parameter identification, optimization and sensitivity analysis.
- Uncertainty and validation: assess model accuracy and parameter uncertainties and take sensor uncertainties into account in the calibration process.
- Integration: contribute to integrating these tools into the ground processing chain so that each new campaign automatically feeds the models used for the next predictions.
Depending on the context at the beginning of the internship and on your profile, the emphasis may be placed more on the data pipeline side or on the model calibration side.
Know-how
- Team spirit, sharing and solidarity
- Curiosity, adaptation
- Pragmatism
- Rigor and precision
Conditions
- 6 months from March 2027

The Team

Our team in the Robotics division is developing pretrained generalist policies that can support a broad range of tasks, environments, and robotic systems. A central scientific challenge is determining how these broadly pretrained policies can be efficiently adapted to new target tasks while achieving the reliability, precision, and robustness required for real-world use.

Pretraining can provide a policy with broad behavioral capabilities, but those capabilities may not immediately translate into dependable performance in a specific deployment setting. Effective post-training methods are therefore essential for converting general capabilities into policies that can adapt quickly, learn from limited additional data or interaction, and perform consistently on demanding downstream tasks.

The Opportunity 

Our research interests include reinforcement learning, imitation learning, human-in-the-loop learning, simulation, world models, policy distillation, and large-scale robot learning. We aim to advance the scientific foundations of policy adaptation while developing methods that may ultimately be evaluated or deployed within internal research projects involving real-world industrial tasks.

Potential research directions include, but are not limited to: 
Offline-to-online reinforcement learning
DAgger, imitation learning, and human-in-the-loop policy improvement
Sim-to-real policy distillation and adaptation
Policy improvement, planning, or data generation using world models
Data-efficient adaptation to new tasks and environments

Resposibilities
-
Develop post-training methods that adapt pretrained generalist robot policies to new tasks, environments, and robotic systems.
-
Design and conduct rigorous experiments in simulation and, where appropriate, on real robotic systems.
-
Analyze results, communicate findings, and contribute to research publications and internal technical reports.

Job Description:
About Altera
At Altera™, our independence as the world’s largest pure‑play FPGA solutions provider gives us the focus, speed, and agility to innovate without compromise. With more than four decades of industry‑leading FPGA expertise, our singular mission is to deliver the programmable technologies that help customers differentiate, innovate, and scale across rapidly evolving markets like AI, cloud, networking, and edge. As an independent company, we move faster, invest deeper, and partner more closely—empowering our teams to drive breakthrough innovation and shape the future of the FPGA industry.
About the Role
Join Altera’s Product Architecture and Chip Engineering (PACE) team and help develop cutting-edge FPGA RTL and IP solutions. The PACE team creates comprehensive solutions that give customers easy and efficient access to the capabilities of Altera’s FPGA devices. These solutions are delivered as highly configurable intellectual property (IP) cores, fully integrated with Altera’s Quartus Prime software CAD tool.
Altera's IP cores provide configurable access to the high-speed, high-bandwidth, low-latency interfaces, leveraging dedicated and specialized silicon subsystems in the FPGA. The constantly rising speed and complexity of video, display, and high-speed data transmission interfaces presents a challenging design problem that requires system-level knowledge of silicon, software, IP, and customer applications.
You will work with a team of engineers to develop and verify state-of-the-art PHY-lite, MIPI, and LVDS-based IP cores for high-speed data transmission. You will be working on advanced FPGA architectures, design definition, implementation, and verification. Additionally, you will also be developing design examples and simulation models, accompanied by a rich set of technical documentation. In this role, you will work closely with multiple teams, including silicon design and validation, post-silicon validation, application engineering, and customer experience teams, to ensure seamless development, integration, and optimization of high-speed interface IP solutions.
Your specific responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
- Architecture and Design based on the latest protocol specifications for video processing, display interfaces, chip-to-chip, and high-speed data transmission interfaces
- RTL development
- Device support and CAD tool integration
- Verification (e.g. verification IP, methodologies, frameworks, bus functional models, regression tests)
- Hardware power-on and debug
- New product release and rollout support
- Customer technical support
The candidate should possess the following behavioral traits:
- Strong skills in communication, initiative, innovation, and teamwork
- Highly motivated to learn and adapt to fast-changing technologies and environments
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail
- Demonstrate fundamental values such as accountability, integrity, and a winning mindset
- Collaborative mindset, strong influencing skills, and a willingness to work across geographical locations

Students currently in the final or penultimate year of a degree in Electronic Engineering (MEng) have the opportunity to experience a 6-month paid MEng placement working as an Electronics Engineer within Leonardo. ABOUT HIYA

At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.

Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.

Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.

This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The engineering intern position is for an individual contributor who is responsible for architecting, implementing, and maintaining significant systems that serve hundreds of millions of requests per month. Hiya provides high-availability, latency-sensitive capabilities to telecoms, mobile apps, and other partners. In addition, you'll work with engineering teams across Hiya, some in Seattle and some in Europe, to define and deliver shared components and services. From day one, you will be paired with a dedicated mentor who provides structured guidance, technical feedback, and ongoing career mentorship.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Design, code, and operate high-performance services and data processing pipelines on a modern technology stack, supported by a structured technical crash course during your first two weeks covering our core tools, architecture, and repositories.

Work at a supportive and fast-growing startup with a fantastic team, where you can collaborate with and learn from other great team members.

Make an impact in the lives of hundreds of millions of consumers.

Be supported in developing your skills and accelerating your career.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Engineering: CS majors - 2nd year (graduating 2028) 

 - Excitement to work on  innovative technology advancements

 - A philosophy of iteration and continuous improvement

 - Working knowledge of building services that adhere to operational SLAs

 - A preference for velocity over perfection

 - A commitment to respectful and impactful collaboration

 - Self-motivated and excited to learn about new technologies


OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS: THE HIYA VOICE AI CHALLENGE

Once we’ve confirmed your eligibility, you’ll receive the Hiya Voice AI Challenge by email-- a chance to build a working prototype of a voice-driven product in one of five tracks: Accessibility, Productivity, Creative Voice, Security, or Real-Time Assistance. You’ll have one week to build it, with optional virtual office hours along the way if you’d like to pitch your idea and get steering from our team first.

From there:

 - Submit and get reviewed. One of our engineers reviews your work. If we’d like to explore your project further, you’ll get a link to book a 30-minute virtual session with an engineer or two-- a quick demo, a walkthrough of your code, and some questions.

 - Final interviews, in person at Hiya. Candidates who advance join us for a final round in London (2nd & 3rd of December): a debugging/fixing session, a chance to add a feature to your own project, and a conversation about Hiya’s values.

AI tools are welcome and encouraged the whole way through.


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM US

 - Dedicated technical mentorship with structured, regular feedback check-ins

 - Clear project scope and goals provided right at the start of your internship

 - Comprehensive onboarding to get you up to speed on Hiya's tooling, codebases, and systems quickly

 - A supportive, collaborative environment built on psychological safety and genuine impact


HOW WE WORK

Hiya is not a passive environment. We expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems.

We work with a high degree of transparency and autonomy. Context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. Once a call is made, we commit and move forward.

You'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust.

Every team member at Hiya is expected to live our core values:

 - Serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and quality

 - Own, share in success and open up to failures

 - Lead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been made

 - Improve, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselves

 - Do, rather than observe


COME WORK WITH US!

We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career.

We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us!



Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

Job Title:
AI and Automation (IT) Intern
Company:
Prologis
Do you want to play a role in global commerce? Are you seeking practical experience to supplement your academic pursuits?
The Prologis Summer Internship Program offers students of diverse educational backgrounds the opportunity to secure work experience within their field of study.

You will help design, prototype, test, and document internal AI agents and workflow automations. Working with the AI team, you will use ChatGPT, Codex, workspace agents, and related enterprise tools to explore ways to improve employee productivity and automate repeatable work. You will also create reusable prompts, agent skills, documentation, and self-service tools, then gather user feedback and prepare demos and handoff materials.

- Support the design, prototyping, testing, and documentation of internal AI agents and workflow automations.
- Develop and evaluate AI solutions using ChatGPT, Codex, workspace agents, and related enterprise tools.
- Identify and prioritize opportunities to improve employee productivity and automate repeatable business processes.
- Create reusable prompts, agent skills, documentation, and self-service tools for business teams.
- Conduct user testing and quality evaluations, summarize findings, and prepare demos and handoff materials.
- Present project outcomes, key learnings, and recommendations to AI leadership at the conclusion of the internship.
Building blocks for success

- Experience using Microsoft Office applications.
- Clear verbal and written communication skills.
- Attention to detail and commitment to professionalism and integrity.

- Experience with relevant tools such as Python, SQL, Dataiku, AWS, OpenAI, Pinecone, or similar AI technologies.

- Experience creating prompts, prototypes, or workflow automations with ChatGPT, Codex, workspace agents, or comparable tools.
- Experience with user testing, quality evaluation, technical documentation, or demonstrations.
- Demonstrates willingness and capability to leverage emerging technology, automation, and AI tools to improve efficiency, quality, and speed. Exercises sound judgment, creative thinking, and accountability for outcomes.

Who You Are:
Ai2 is seeking talented and motivated Research Interns to join our Open Ecosystem team, working on fully open foundation models like Olmo and Molmo . This internship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research in AI in an exciting, fast-paced research environment. As a Research Intern, you have the opportunity to:
- Define and lead a high-impact research project.
- Train and release leading models.
- Collaborate with and learn from team members across Ai2.
- Build open-source software for the research community.
- Author scientific papers for publication in a high-profile conference or journal.
Ai2 Research Internship Information:
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Start date: Flexible
- Candidates: A PhD candidate or a master/undergraduate student with a strong research background
We are currently hiring for start dates in 2027. If you have questions, feel free to reach out to olmo-careers@allenai.org . ​​Please apply by January 8, 2027 at 11:00pm Pacific Time to be considered for our Spring/Summer 2027 internships.
Who We Are:
We build the world’s most fully open AI models, working to advance new capabilities, improve performance and robustness, and make the building process more rigorous, transparent, and efficient. We deliver high-impact research and masterfully-engineered open-source tools to accelerate AI research around the world.
Your Next Challenge:
Why Open Ecosystem? We are building the foundation to foster years of open science and research on AI models.
- All interns are paired with one or more mentors from the Open Ecosystem team.
- We encourage open collaboration on intern projects, even with researchers at external institutions. We have close ties to the University of Washington, only 1.5 miles away.
- Our pay is competitive, and visa sponsorship is available.
- We are committed to open science and support students freely publishing papers. Examples:
- Olmo 3: Charting a path through the model flow to lead open-source AI
- Molmo2: Open Weights and Data for Vision-Language Models with Video Understanding and Grounding
- DR Tulu: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics for Deep Research
- OlmoHybrid: From Theory to Practice and Back
- OlmoCore 3: Supercharging Olmo-core for Efficient and Scalable MoE Training
To see more about our current, future, and past interns, check out our internship page on our website!
What You’ll Need:
Qualifications:
- Pursuing a doctoral degree in Computer Science or similar field with research experience in machine learning, natural language processing, language and vision, or related areas.
- Strong software engineering skills, especially with deep learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch).
Bonus qualifications:
- A strong publication record at AI-related venues, such as NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, COLM, ACL, EMNLP.
- Experience in related areas of foundation model research like training dynamics, scaling laws, efficiency, data curation, post-training methods (e.g., SFT, DPO, RL), agentic training and infrastructure, and applications in scientific domains.
- Contributions to open-source research libraries (e.g., PyTorch, Huggingface Transformers, olmo-core, AllenNLP).

- The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
- The ability to observe details at close range.
- Can work under deadlines.

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.
Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our Search AI teams within Facebook. Facebook Search helps people find the people, groups, events, videos and posts they are looking for, across one of the largest and fastest-changing content collections in the world. Our teams build AI that helps people decide what to search for and find useful results. This spans personalized query suggestions before and during a search, suggested queries on Reels, and retrieval and ranking of relevant content. We bring together generative AI, multimodal understanding, and personalization to help people express intent, act on curiosity, and discover useful content at Facebook scale. Our interns will have the opportunity to frame practical, high-impact search problems as rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance of our research scientists and software engineers.
The central research challenge is to connect what a person wants to explore with content that makes the journey worthwhile. For example, a video can spark curiosity before someone has a query in mind; the system must suggest a useful question and deliver results that reward that curiosity. Models must understand explicit queries or infer interests from multimodal content, generate useful suggestions or retrieve relevant results, and balance engagement with relevance, groundedness, and factuality within strict latency and compute constraints. Open problems include generative retrieval using learned identifiers that represent content, personalized query generation, sequence models for ranking individual results and composing a useful results page, and joint learning across suggestions and results. LLM-based supervision, post-training, and online experiments help us connect model improvements to useful exploration and sustained search habits.
If you are excited about helping billions of people turn curiosity into useful discovery, from the first search suggestion to the results that follow, come join us!
Our internships are twelve (12) to sixteen (16), or twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

In the rapidly evolving fields of AI, Augmented Reality (AR), and Virtual Reality (VR), industry compression research is shifting from human-consumed media to non-human-consumed internal neural model states. These representations include latent tensors, weights, Gaussian splats, feature maps, and depth/alpha buffers exchanged between neural networks. As high-capability models exceed on-device compute limits while cloud execution is constrained by latency, privacy, and power, systems are adopting split inference—partitioning model execution between devices and datacenters connected by neural bitstreams. In this architecture, the compression ratio on the split link serves as a primary determinant of round-trip latency, bandwidth efficiency, and battery performance.
Advancing compression techniques for neural representations expands beyond rendering outputs to critical non-media data streams. Key emergent areas include Feature Coding for Machines (FCM) for intermediate network features, visual and multimodal token pruning/compression, low-latency action and control streams for embodied systems, KV cache compression for distributed LLM prefill and decode stages, model deltas for on-device personalization, and persistent scene state streams for interactive world models. Establishing specialized compression capabilities across these representations directly impacts the operating efficiency and scalability of split-inference AI and XR applications.
The intern will explore several key directions in compression and streaming techniques for neural representations:
1. Latent Vector Compression: Developing efficient quantization, entropy coding, and learned prior models for compact, high-dimensional latent spaces exchanged in split-inference architectures.
2. Gaussian Splat Compression: Creating specialized compression and streaming algorithms that maintain the spatial distribution, opacity, and color parameters of 3D Gaussian splats with high rendering fidelity and low memory footprint.
Throughout the project, the intern will conduct a thorough review of existing literature, implement prototype models, and benchmark them against traditional compression methods. The final goal is to develop a neural compression framework that outperforms current techniques in terms of compression ratio, speed, and fidelity.
This research not only contributes to the academic field but also has direct applications in improving the operational efficiency of AR/VR systems, ultimately pushing the boundaries of what is possible in digital interaction spaces.

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across AI, hardware, software, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. Who we are
Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across AI, hardware, software, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.
We are researchers, roboticists, engineers, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
About the role
We are seeking an AI Research Intern to join our founding team and bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. In this role, you will contribute to core research initiatives on Perception, World Models and Action models. You will help translate cutting-edge theoretical breakthroughs into scalable, real-world deployment on physical autonomous systems, driving how our platforms perceive, simulate, and navigate complex environments.
What you’ll do
- Integrate and adapt emerging AI research into internal model pipelines, validating performance on real-world datasets and simulation.
- Prototype and evaluate RL, trajectory planning, and distillation algorithms based on state-of-the-art literature.
- Train and fine-tune multimodal models that map real-time sensor inputs and behavioral goals to vehicle actuation.
- Experiment with world model architectures using multi-sensor log data to improve simulation fidelity and trajectory querying.
- Analyze edge cases and failure modes in novel driving environments to iterate on model performance and stability.
- Run rigorous simulation experiments alongside research and validation teams to identify performance bottlenecks and track model improvements.
What we're looking for
- Education: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, EECS, Robotics, AI, or a closely related field.
- Core Expertise: Coursework, project experience, or research background focused on at least one of the following domains:
- Generative World Models / Video Generation / Diffusion Models
- Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or embodied AI
- Reinforcement Learning (RL), trajectory optimization, or decision-making systems
- Large-scale multimodal Transformer architectures applied to robotics or spatio-temporal data
- Framework Fluency: Advanced hands-on proficiency with PyTorch or JAX for training and fine-tuning large-scale neural networks.
- Programming: Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of C++.
Preferred Qualifications
- Prior research, project, or internship experience in autonomous driving, mobile robotics, or spatial AI.
Why join us
At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.
What else you need to know
This role is based in our Mountain View or San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change, we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.
The hourly pay range for this internship role is $70/hr per hour.
Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.
Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

SUMMER 2027 INTERNSHIP/CO-OP: AVIONICS HARDWARE & TEST ENGINEER

Kirkland, WA · Full-time · Onsite




ABOUT SKYBAND

GPS jamming and spoofing affect thousands of flights every day (GPSThreatMap.com http://GPSThreatMap.com). Skyband Systems has built the M100, a certified avionics system to overcome this threat to safety and operational reliability. The M100 fuses satellite signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with inertial sensing to give pilots a trusted position source that doesn't depend on GPS.

We're a VC-backed, fast-paced team based in Kirkland, WA, made up of engineers who built and scaled Starlink Aviation at SpaceX. We design, build, test, and fly our own hardware in our own aircraft. Everyone on the team has significant ownership over product areas or problem spaces.




THE ROLE

You'll be hands-on with the hardware team as the M100 goes from first production units through qualification, certification, and aircraft installation. You'll work directly with senior engineers who will give you real ownership and expect real results. By the end of your internship, you should expect that hardware you worked on will be test flown and used on commercial aircraft.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Bring up, debug, and characterize production M100 circuit boards and assemblies

 - Design and build test fixtures and automated test setups for development and production

 - Support environmental and EMI/EMC qualification testing to DO-160: planning, execution, and data review

 - Build and expand hardware-in-the-loop test stands used to validate the full system on the ground

 - Support aircraft integration and flight test, including harnessing, instrumentation, and post-flight data review

 - Write test scripts and analysis tools and document results to the standard certification requires


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field

 - 3+ months of hands-on engineering experience from internships, research labs, or student project teams

 - Comfortable with basic lab equipment: oscilloscope, multimeter, power supplies, soldering iron

 - Authorized to work in the United States


PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

 - You've built, tested, and debugged something yourself outside the classroom (such as project teams, research, or personal projects)

 - Schematic capture and PCB layout experience (Altium, KiCad, or similar)

 - Python or similar scripting for test automation and data analysis

 - Familiarity with embedded systems and interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, or ARINC 429

 - Exposure to environmental, EMI/EMC, or RF testing

 - Interest in aviation, navigation, or GNSS; a pilot's license or flight test experience is a plus

 - Clear written communication and the discipline to document what you did and what you found


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Full-time, onsite in Kirkland, WA for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning June-July 2027

 - Able to lift up to 25 lbs. and work in lab and hangar environments

 - Occasional travel for aircraft integration and flight test may be required


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - $50.00/hour

 - $2500 relocation bonus

 - Paid holidays based on company holiday schedule

 - Direct mentorship from engineers who have shipped flight hardware at scale

ABOUT BRIDGE NEUROTECH

Bridge Neurotech is building a non-invasive functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) platform with AI-based neural decoding for brain-computer interface applications. We are a seed-stage neurotechnology company developing technology that has the potential to transform how we interact with the human brain.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Hardware Engineering Intern to join Bridge for a six-month internship or co-op and help turn ideas into physical parts. Almost nothing we build can be bought, so we make our own as one-off or low-volume production, and you will work across all of it: design it, build it, test it, improve it.

This is a hands-on lab role with breadth: CAD in the morning, soldering in the afternoon, and Python scripting in between. We expect you to use AI coding tools to build automations and bespoke tools.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and iterate parts in CAD, for example probe housings, mounts, fixtures, enclosures, and lab hardware.

 - Run our 3D printers: dial in materials and profiles, manage the queue, and keep turnaround measured in hours.

 - Help build the automation around 3D printing and CNC, for example scripted slicing and job submission, print monitoring, and part tracking.

 - Help develop processes for low-volume part production, for example molding, casting, potting, bonding, and the jigs and fixtures those processes need.

 - Do the work that makes hardware real: soldering, cable and harness assembly, and careful assembly of delicate parts.

 - Build test fixtures and benchtop setups, and help keep the lab organized and working.

 - Write Python to glue the shop together: automation, instrument control, data logging, and inventory tracking.

 - Work directly with our imaging scientists and research team to understand how each part will actually be used.


WHO YOU ARE

Required

 - Enrolled in a bachelor’s program in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related discipline, in your junior year or later, or in a master’s program.

 - Available full time for six months.

 - Working proficiency in CAD: parametric modeling, assemblies, and drawings.

 - Hands-on 3D printing experience, for example tuning, troubleshooting, and repair.

 - Comfortable soldering both boards and wire, and assembling precision hardware without breaking it.

 - Some experience with Python: you can write a real script, for example file handling, an API call, or a serial interface.

 - Comfortable using AI coding tools to get to working tooling.

 - A bias toward building, testing, and improving over designing to completion first.

Nice to have

 - PCB layout experience, particularly in Altium.

 - CNC machining experience, for example CAM programming, fixturing, and workholding.

 - Personal projects, a shop of your own, robotics or FSAE, or other evidence that you build things unprompted.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Six months of hands-on ownership of the hardware this company runs on.

Your work will be used to train large language models to master tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning in real-world production environments.  - Design and run reward-shaping experiments and algorithmic improvements (e.g., GRPO, DAPO) to improve LLM tool-use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning.

 - Quantify data usability, quality, and performance uplift on key benchmarks.

 - Build and maintain data generation and augmentation pipelines that scale with training needs.

 - Create and refine rubrics, evaluators, and scoring frameworks that guide training and evaluation decisions.

 - Build and operate LLM evaluation systems, benchmarks, and metrics at scale.

 - Collaborate closely with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and experts producing training data.

 - Operate in a fast-paced, experimental research environment with rapid iteration cycles and high ownership.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong applied research background, with a focus on post-training and/or model evaluation.

 - Strong coding proficiency and hands-on experience working with machine learning models.

 - Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, backend systems, and core engineering fundamentals.

 - Familiarity with APIs, SQL/NoSQL databases, and cloud platforms.

 - Ability to reason deeply about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality.

 - Excitement to work in person in San Francisco, five days a week (with optional remote Saturdays), and thrive in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Real-world post-training team experience in industry (highest priority).

 - Publications at top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL).

 - Experience training models or evaluating model performance.

 - Experience in synthetic data generation, LLM evaluations, or RL-style workflows.

 - Work samples, artifacts, or code repositories demonstrating relevant skills.

ABOUT IXIAN

Ixian Robotics is building intelligent machines to reindustrialize America. We’re based in San Francisco and backed by a16z and Accel.

We believe robotics is a full-stack problem. Software, hardware, and machine learning are only part of it. Bridging advances in robot learning with America’s industrial base requires invention in how we understand customers, design products, navigate supply chains, and make the economics work. We’re building a company that takes responsibility for all of it.

At Ixian, deployment isn’t the final step after the “real innovation” is complete. Deploying robots is the point of robotics, and deployment is our forcing function for innovation. Putting a machine to work reveals what the lab can’t: what breaks, what matters to the people using it, and what it will take to make our machines indispensable.

Robots are called machines when they work. We intend to build machines.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a hardware intern at Ixian, you’ll design, build, and test hardware for real robotics systems. Working directly with our engineers, you’ll take on business critical projects, and own them from initial ideation through prototyping, testing, and design revisions.

The work is hands-on and spans mechanical design, fabrication, assembly, and testing. We’re interested in people who enjoy making things, notice when the physical result differs from the design intent, and iterate aggressively to problem solve. Your projects will reflect your skills and the team’s current needs.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and revise parts, fixtures, and assemblies in CAD, considering how they will be manufactured, assembled, and tested.

 - Build prototypes using available fabrication tools and processes, then document what worked and what needs to change.

 - Implement design changes and drive iterative improvements.

 - Define and run tests, collect measurements, and use the resulting data to make recommendations or drive improvements.

 - Maintain clearly documented drawings, bills of materials, build notes, and test results.
   


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Evidence of hands-on building through coursework, a robotics team, research, a previous internship, or personal projects. Photos and portfolios are welcome.

 - Familiarity with a CAD tool such as Onshape, SolidWorks, or Fusion, and basic understanding of mechanical design and fabrication.

 - Workshop knowledge of measurement, assembly, and safe tool use.

 - Willingness to test assumptions, accept feedback, and revise a design when the evidence points to a better approach.

 - Clear communication skills, dependable work ethic, the ability to self start, and an interest in physical robotic systems.
   

Location: San Francisco · On-site

Schedule: Full-time

Pay: $50–$75 per hour


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Ixian Robotics is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

COMPANY

Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, we turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into a formal representation, so every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved. Pramaana's architecture pairs foundation models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4. Pramaana was founded by a team out of Google, DeepMind, and Glean, combining frontier AI researchers and formal methods experts.




THE ROLE

As a Research Intern at Pramaana, you’ll contribute to one of several areas: model training, harness engineering, AI for Formal research or benchmark development. You’ll help run training experiments, investigate new approaches to symbolic reasoning, or build evaluation harnesses that help us measure and improve model performance.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run model training experiments and analyze the results.

 - Design harnesses for auto-formalization and prover systems.

 - Build and maintain benchmarks to measure performance.

 - Investigate where models succeed or fail, and suggest improvements.

 - Work with researchers and engineers to turn findings into the next set of experiments.
   
   


YOU WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - A solid grasp of deep learning fundamentals and how to evaluate models.

 - The ability to run careful experiments, communicate findings clearly, and work well with a research team.

 - Technical depth in at least one area relevant to the role, such as model training, formal methods, or evaluation systems.

 - The initiative to make progress on open-ended problems with limited direction.

 - Close attention to detail in your code, data, and results.




ESPECIALLY STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - A background in formal verification (Lean, Coq, or Isabelle)

 - Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning LLMs, including work on pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, or reinforcement learning.

 - A strong publication record in top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
