JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

Putting an autonomous 40-ton excavator on a live jobsite means being able to say, precisely, what we know about its safety and what that knowledge rests on. Today that argument lives in hazard analyses, requirements, tests and logs, linked by hand.

As a Safety Engineering intern, you’ll explore how formal methods and LLM-assisted proving can strengthen that argument. Working at the intersection of formal methods, statistics, and field robotics, you’ll formalize a narrowly scoped safety claim, verify a checker in Lean, and evaluate it on real fleet data, with explicit assumptions and auditable results.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Become fluent in Bedrock's safety case and trace safety claims through the hazards, requirements, mitigations, and evidence that support them

 - Build an end-to-end demonstration for one claim: define the property and assumptions, implement a checker in Lean, prove its correctness against the specification, and run it on fleet data

 - Develop checks for assumptions that can be monitored in fleet data, and document those that require other evidence

 - Build audit tooling for LLM-assisted proving: record proof dependencies, document toolchain trust assumptions, and reject proof placeholders or unapproved axioms in automated builds

 - Work with Safety, Systems, and Autonomy teams to review formal specifications and turn findings into safety case improvements

 - Document the results, limitations, and recommendations for adoption in our review process


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Hands-on experience with Lean and mathlib experience, particularly real analysis or probability.

 - Working knowledge of probability and statistics (distributions, confidence intervals, tail bounds).

 - Familiarity with knowledge graphs or structured document analysis

 - Ability to translate informal claims into precise specifications and identify their assumptions

 - Experience evaluating LLM-generated code or proofs.

 - Background in autonomous vehicles, heavy equipment, or other safety-critical robotics.


PREFERRED

 - Exposure to safety or assurance-case practice (GSN, UL 4600, ISO 13849, IEC 61508) or runtime verification.

 - Experience with Rust verification tools (Aeneas, Verus, Kani) or differential/property-based testing.

 - Familiarity with knowledge graphs or structured document analysis

 - Background in autonomous vehicles, heavy equipment, or other safety-critical robotics

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

About Xterra
Xterra is a Khosla Ventures-backed company building AI agents that reason about complex scientific problems. We’re not a wrapper around existing models, we’re training our own foundation models on top of large-scale proprietary datasets. This is a rare intersection of frontier AI and real-world scientific impact.

Xterra is still in stealth mode. Please reach out to us for a full picture.


The Role
We're looking for research scientists and research interns who want to work at the intersection of research and engineering — developing new methods for teaching AI systems to reason, and building the infrastructure to train and evaluate them at scale. You'll own problems end-to-end, from idea through experimentation to production.
We're hiring across multiple levels (intern through senior/staff) and will calibrate scope and expectations to match your experience.


What You'll Work On
• Reasoning via reinforcement learning: Designing and training reasoning systems using RLHF,
RLAIF, and reward modeling approaches, applied to geological hypothesis generation and
evaluation.
• Process reward models and verifiers: Developing fine-grained supervision over intermediate
reasoning steps — not just final answers — so the system learns to reason well, not just get
lucky.
• Search and planning: Exploring chain-of-thought strategies, search-time compute (e.g., Monte
Carlo Tree Search), and other techniques that enable deeper, more deliberate reasoning over
geological evidence.
• Scalable oversight: Contributing to alignment and oversight research — figuring out how to
reliably supervise models on geological tasks where ground truth is expensive, delayed, or
ambiguous.
• Infrastructure and experimentation: Building robust training pipelines, running large-scale
experiments, and iterating quickly across the research-to-production lifecycle.
• Evaluation: Contributing to meaningful benchmarks and evaluation methods for geological reasoning capabilities.



What We're Looking For
• Strong fundamentals in machine learning, with hands-on experience training large models (LLMs preferred but not required).
• Demonstrated experience with reinforcement learning — ideally applied to language models, but strong RL backgrounds from other domains (robotics, game-playing, scientific discovery) are valued.
• Comfort working across the research-engineering spectrum: you can write a paper and you can debug a distributed training job.
• Familiarity with at least some of: reward modeling, RLHF/RLAIF pipelines, search and planning methods, or AI alignment techniques.
• Publication record is a plus but not a strict requirement — we care more about the quality of your thinking and what you've built.

 

For Interns
We welcome outstanding PhD and Masters students (and exceptional undergraduates) for research internships typically lasting 12–16 weeks. Interns work on the same problems as full-time researchers, embedded in a team and owning a meaningful project from day one. What we look for in intern candidates:


• Currently pursuing a graduate degree (PhD or Masters) in machine learning, AI, or a related field - or an undergraduate with significant research experience.
• Coursework or research experience in reinforcement learning, NLP, or deep learning.
• A strong project portfolio or publications demonstrating independent research ability.
• Eagerness to tackle open-ended problems and ship real experiments on real data.
At More Senior Levels, We'd Also Expect
• A track record of identifying and driving high-impact research directions independently.
• Experience mentoring other researchers and influencing technical strategy.
• Deep expertise in one or more of the core technical areas listed above.

ABOUT SYCAMORE

Sycamore is building the trusted agent operating system for the enterprise. Our platform helps companies build, deploy, and orchestrate agentic apps that take on real operational work, with the security and control large organizations need.

We are a small, engineering-led team working directly with Fortune 500 enterprises. We have raised $65M from Coatue and Lightspeed, along with other investors and industry leaders.




THE ROLE

This is a real engineering internship. You will own a piece of work that ships, that other people depend on, and that is still running after you leave. The scope is narrower than a full-time engineer’s and you will have a direct partner accountable for your project succeeding, but the bar is the same as for anyone else here: correct, tested, and able to hold up when someone depends on it.

This is one application for engineering internships across our teams. We will match you to a team and a project after we have talked.




THE TEAMS YOU COULD JOIN

Core AI builds the shared runtime and intelligence systems every agent depends on: agent loops, tool execution, memory, durable workflows, model routing, and the evaluation systems that tell us whether a change actually improved anything. The feedback is fast, because an evaluation either catches a regression or it does not.

AI Services builds the governed control plane around our agents: the registry of which agents exist, the identity and delegation machinery that decides whose authority an agent acts under, the connectors that reach customer systems, and the model gateway every inference call crosses. The correctness bar is unusually visible: controls either hold or they do not.

Products builds what enterprise users see and touch: Sycamore Forge, where customers describe what they need and watch agents build it, and Sycamore Guard, where a customer’s own AI program is registered, assessed, and approved. The interface problems are genuinely unsolved, because streaming, long-running, non-deterministic systems break most of the patterns you will have learned.

Applied AI builds directly with enterprise customers, turning a real operational workflow into an application their team uses. The platform gives you a great deal to build on, so an intern can get to something consequential quickly.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own a real project end to end, from scoping through implementation, testing, review, and deployment.

 - Write production code that meets the same bar as everyone else’s, and go through the same review.

 - Ask for help early when you are stuck, and be specific about what you have already tried.

 - Document what you built well enough that the person who inherits it does not have to reconstruct your reasoning.




THE ENVIRONMENT YOU WILL WORK IN

Depending on the team, you might work in Python cloud services on FastAPI with typed data models and PostgreSQL; React and TypeScript product surfaces with TanStack and Tailwind; asynchronous and streaming systems; durable workflows; protocol-based tool execution over MCP; relational and vector data; and cloud-native deployment on Kubernetes.

We use automated tests, coding agents, traces, evaluations, browser automation, and production feedback as part of everyday engineering, and we lean on contract tests to keep independently deployed services honest with each other.

This is context, not a checklist. We do not require previous experience with every language, framework, or vendor in our stack. Strong engineers who understand systems, learn quickly, and have shipped production software can become effective here without matching our tools one for one.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or recently graduated. We care about what you have built, not your year or program.

 - Evidence that you have built and shipped something real: a project with users, a substantial open-source contribution, a previous internship where you owned production code, or something you built because you wanted it to exist.

 - Solid software fundamentals. You can design a data model, write an API, reason about failure, and debug code you did not write.

 - The instinct to test your own work and to try the realistic path rather than the happy path.

 - AI-native. You use coding agents and modern models as a force multiplier while still understanding the code you ship and being able to explain your decisions.

 - Clear communication, including the ability to say when you are stuck.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. The problem you are given will not arrive fully specified.

You do not need prior experience with agentic apps, enterprise software, or our stack. You do need to learn quickly and to care about whether what you built actually works.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. A 30-minute introductory conversation.

 2. Two 60-minute technical interviews, one focused on coding and one on how you approach an open-ended problem.

 3. A short take-home where you build something real and walk us through your decisions.
    
    


WHY JOIN

 - Ship production software that enterprise teams actually use, during an internship.

 - Work alongside engineers building something genuinely hard, with the same standards applied to your work.

 - Learn what production AI systems require, which is very different from what a demo requires.

 - Get real ownership and real feedback in a short window.

 - Receive competitive compensation, and a genuine conversation about a full-time role if it goes well.

 - Work with people who will tell you honestly when something is not good enough yet.

Our mission is to build the foundational infrastructure that brings intelligent robots out of the lab and into the real world.

We’re looking for exceptional students who are excited to work at the intersection of robotics, AI, and real-world deployment.

As an Engineering Intern, you’ll work directly alongside our research and engineering teams on meaningful technical problems, contribute to systems running on real robots, and gain hands-on experience building at an early-stage robotics company.

Depending on your background and interests, you may work across robot learning, computer vision, 3D perception, manipulation, navigation, simulation, or robotics software and infrastructure.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Work alongside our researchers and engineers to develop and test robotics and AI systems.

 - Contribute to projects across robot learning, perception, manipulation, navigation, simulation, or robotics infrastructure.

 - Prototype, implement, and evaluate new algorithms and technical approaches.

 - Test software and models in simulation and on real robotic systems.

 - Take ownership of a meaningful technical project with direct mentorship from the team.


WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, AI/ML, Computer Vision, Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++.

 - Hands-on experience through robotics projects, research labs, internships, competitions, or open-source work.

 - We especially love candidates with experience in leading robotics and research labs, including SLAM, RAI, Boston Dynamics, and similar environments.

Agios is a full stack research organization within Reality Labs Research, spanning materials and manufacturing, sensors and actuators, simulation, and learned control. Our mission is to build systems that enhance human capabilities through intelligent machine collaboration. Today that work centers on what we call the last bottleneck: AI has compressed the digital side of research and development, while the physical side still moves at human speed. Dexterous Manipulation is the pillar attacking that problem directly, pairing a custom dexterous robotic hand with in-house wearable sensing, high accuracy simulation, and glove-driven teleoperation.
As a Research Scientist Intern, you will work at the intersection of robot learning, dexterous control, and human-to-robot transfer, with mentors who span hardware, simulation, controls, and policy learning. Your focus will be learned models that turn human demonstration data into executable robot behavior, covering retargeting, manipulation policies, and teleoperation.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, we're redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



Job Summary
Core Engineering is our special projects team. This team identifies critical gaps across Etched and builds solutions 0 to 1, often in days, with immediate feedback loops. You might build internal tools to unblock a hardware team, prototype systems for manufacturing execution, or design, evaluate, and deploy agentic systems for our most challenging R&D problems.

This role is for engineers who thrive on ambiguity, move fast without sacrificing quality, and get energy from solving whatever problem matters most right now. It is a whiteboard for future founders – if you're interested in shipping 0-1 production-level code every week, this role is for you.



This role requires exceptional full-stack engineering capabilities, deep product sense, personal accountability, and a knack for building from the ground up. At Etched, we're developing our processes for scale, and we're looking for engineers to deploy to our toughest challenges. The problems we solve are time-sensitive and business-critical. This role will not be a 9-5, and the ideal candidate is excited about that. This is not a shadowing program. You will own a real project, scoped to land in production and shape how Etched executes.



You may be a good fit if you:

 - Have a track record of solving hard problems across stacks and domains — you enjoy being dropped into unfamiliar territory and figuring it out

 - Have something you built that you can walk us through in depth. Depth in one thing beats a list of ten

 - Are comfortable with Python and TypeScript: you can read it, modify it, debug it, and direct AI to write it well. We don't care whether you write code from scratch, but we do care whether you ship things that work

 - Have product sense and its necessary prerequisites, from AI tooling proficiency to design taste

 - Bias towards action and comfort with incomplete information
   
   

Strong candidates may also have:

 - Data engineering, infrastructure or DevOps experience, and deploying operational systems in enterprise environments

 - Experience wielding frontier models on frontier problems: an eval-driven mindset — you measure whether AI systems work, identify where they fall short, and know how to hillclimb

 - High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you find the real problem to solve

 - Prior startup experience, especially during hyper growth

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification



Program details

 - 12-week paid internship (June - August 2026)

 - Generous housing support for those relocating

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Based at our office in San Jose, CA

 - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers

 - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time

For any questions, contact internships@etched.com



How we're different
Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

The Internship Programme at Graphcore
Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.
What you’ll be doing
Put your engineering foundations to work exploring the electronic hardware behind Graphcore’s AI compute platforms.
Your internship could focus on Hardware Design, Signal Integrity or elements of both, depending on your interests, the available projects and how your strengths develop. You’ll contribute to a clearly scoped design, analysis, validation or debugging task, with guidance as you work towards a conclusion supported by evidence.
In Hardware Design, your tasks could include schematic and circuit design, component evaluation, PCB development, board bring-up or laboratory testing. You could help check power rails and clocks, exercise interfaces, investigate faults or develop test and debug access.
In Signal Integrity, you could explore high-speed links such as PCIe and Ethernet, DDR and other memory interfaces, or clocks and timing-critical signals. Tasks could include reviewing PCB layouts and routing, simulating interconnect behaviour or comparing laboratory measurements with analysis to understand design trade-offs.
Your team and support
Hardware Design and Signal Integrity engineers work closely with PCB layout, silicon, validation, firmware, mechanical and thermal engineering, manufacturing and system teams. You’ll see how different engineering perspectives come together to make complex boards work.
Staff Hardware Engineers and Team Leads will support you with clearly scoped work and regular technical guidance. You can ask for help as you explore unfamiliar concepts, discuss your findings and use feedback to improve your approach.
Decisions are shaped by simulation, measurement and engineering judgement. As an intern, you’ll be encouraged to ask questions, speak up and try out ideas early, with support from experienced engineers as you learn.
How you’ll learn and grow
Over the 12 weeks, you’ll connect your studies with how boards are designed, analysed, brought up and validated. Your project will help you develop a methodical approach to defining a problem, testing your thinking and explaining what the evidence shows.
You’ll gain exposure to professional tools such as Mentor Expedition, Ansys HFSS and Keysight ADS, as relevant to your work. Comparing simulations, design choices and laboratory results will help you understand how real hardware behaves and which areas of hardware engineering you’d like to explore further.
Your internship is a chance to explore a future at Graphcore. Depending on your performance and the roles available, there may be an opportunity to join one of our graduate programmes once you’ve graduated.

- Currently studying towards a degree in Electronic Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics or a closely related technical discipline
- Strong electrical and electronic engineering foundations, with an interest in hardware design or signal integrity and how real electronic systems work
- A logical, first-principles approach to unfamiliar problems, with practical engineering experience from university projects, laboratory work, personal projects or activities such as Formula Student, robotics or engineering societies
- The ability to work with measurements or technical data and explain your conclusions clearly, with curiosity, willingness to take ownership and openness to feedback and collaboration
Your interests might include schematic design, PCBs, component selection, bring-up, validation, test or fault finding; or transmission lines, impedance, reflections, crosstalk, simulation and electronic measurement.
Previous industry experience and professional experience with the tools listed above are not required. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned.

Want to gain real-world experience in manufacturing while building the foundation for your future career? Our 10-week Manufacturing Management Internship gives students the opportunity to work side-by-side with experienced leaders, explore key areas of operations and contribute to projects that make a real impact.
What You’ll Do
-
Dive into daily plant operations and learn how a high-performing manufacturing facility runs.
-
Lead or support projects that improve safety, quality, efficiency, and cost performance.
-
Collaborate across departments to analyze processes and recommend improvements.
-
Attend professional development activities, including a professional development week at our corporate headquarters in Colorado.
-
Meet regularly with plant leaders through weekly check-ins and mentorship opportunities.
-
Gain exposure to production and support teams while developing leadership skills.
-
Follow all plant safety practices, SOPs, and policies.
Who We Are Looking For
-
Current students pursuing a bachelor's degree in manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline at an accredited 4-year college or university.
-
And has completed at least one year of coursework with a graduation date of December 2027 or later
-
Students interested in pursuing a career in manufacturing and entering the workforce directly after undergrad.
-
And able to work in a fast-paced 24/7 environment, including 12-hour shifts on the plant floor when needed.
-
Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship now or in the future.
What You’ll Gain
-
Hands-on manufacturing experience in a plant environment.
-
Mentorship and guidance from experienced leaders.
-
Exposure to multiple areas of plant operations and professional networking opportunities.
